Soon, the fire reached the shed, where Tom's bike and toys were. The shed was made of wood and paint. It burned very fast and made a lot of smoke. The smoke was black and thick. It hurt Tom's eyes and nose. He started to cough and cry.

Tom's mom and dad ran to the backyard. They saw the fire and the smoke. They saw Tom crying near the pile of ash. They were very scared and angry. They grabbed Tom and took him away from the fire. They called the firemen to put out the fire.

Tom was very sorry for what he did. He lost his bike and his toys. He burned his fingers and his clothes. He made his mom and dad sad and mad. He learned that fire was bad and dangerous. He never played with fire again.

"Reverse means to make something go back to how it was before," her mom explained. "You have to help your brother write his story again. You have to use your crayons to draw his words. You have to be quiet and careful. Do you understand?"

One day, she saw a big dragonfly. It had shiny wings and a long tail. It flew very fast and made a buzzing sound. Lily wanted to catch it. She chased it with her jar. She ran and ran, but the dragonfly was too quick.

"Come here, dragonfly!" Lily shouted. "I won't hurt you. I just want to look at you and talk to you."

But the dragonfly did not listen. It flew away from Lily. It flew over the pond, over the bridge, over the trees. Lily followed it, but she was getting tired. Her legs were sore and her breath was short. She wished the dragonfly would stop.

Finally, the dragonfly landed on a flower. Lily ran up to it and put her jar over it. She was very happy. She had caught the dragonfly. She screwed the lid on and lifted the jar. She smiled at the dragonfly.

"Hello, dragonfly," she said. "You are very pretty and fast. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

But the dragonfly did not smile back. It looked scared and sad. It banged against the jar and tried to fly away. It wanted to be free. It did not want to be in the jar.

Lily saw the dragonfly's eyes. They were big and shiny. They looked at her with a plea. Lily felt sorry for the dragonfly. She realized she had made a mistake. She did not want to make the dragonfly unhappy. She wanted to make it happy.

She opened the jar and let the dragonfly go. It flew out of the jar and into the air. It buzzed and circled around Lily. It seemed to say thank you. Then it flew away, back to the pond, the bridge, the trees.

Lily waved goodbye to the dragonfly. She felt a little sad, but also a little proud. She had done the right thing. She had let the dragonfly be free.

She put her jar back in her backpack and walked back to her mom. She was very tired, but also very happy. She had learned a lot from the dragonfly. She had learned to respect and love the bugs. She had learned to fly.

Ben and Lily shook their heads.

"Yield means to let someone else go first. You have to let the cars and bikes go first. They are bigger and faster than you. If you go into the street, they might hit you and hurt you. That would be very bad." Mom said.

Ben and Lily nodded. They understood.

"OK, mom. We will yield to the cars and bikes. We will wait for them to stop." Ben said.

"Good. That is very smart and safe. You are good kids." Mom said.

The whale swam around them for a while. It played with them and sprayed water from its hole. It let Tom and his dad touch its skin. It was smooth and wet. Tom felt the whale's heart beat. It was strong and slow. Tom felt a connection with the whale. He felt like the whale was his friend.

Tom and his dad had to go back to the boat. They said goodbye to the whale. They thanked it for the amazing time. The whale said goodbye with another loud sound. It waved its tail and swam away. Tom and his dad climbed on the boat. They hugged each other and smiled. They had met a whale!

Tom and Lily were playing with blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and houses and cars with the blocks. They had many colors and shapes of blocks to choose from.

Tom wanted to make a very tall tower with the blocks. He reached for the highest block he could find. It was red and square and shiny. He put it on top of his tower and smiled. He was proud of his tower.

Lily saw Tom's tower and wanted to make one too. She reached for the same block that Tom had used. She pulled it from his tower and tried to put it on hers. But Tom saw what she did and got angry.

"Hey, that's my block!" he shouted. "Give it back to me!"

"No, it's mine!" Lily shouted back. "I saw it first!"

They both tugged at the block and started to fight. They did not notice that their towers were falling down. The blocks crashed to the floor and made a loud noise.

Mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the mess and the crying children. She was not happy.

"What is going on here?" she asked. "Why are you fighting over a block?"

Tom and Lily stopped fighting and looked at Mom. They felt sorry for what they had done. They knew they had been bad.

"We're sorry, Mom," they said. "We both wanted the same block and we didn't share."

Mom sighed and picked up the block. She held it in her hand and showed it to them.

"Look, this is just a block," she said. "It is not worth fighting over. There are many other blocks you can use. And you can have more fun if you play together and help each other. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They understood. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry again. Then they picked up the blocks and started to build a new tower. This time, they shared the blocks and worked as a team. They made a bigger and better tower than before. They were happy and so was Mom.

"Oh no, let's put a bandage on it to make it feel better," his mom said.

Timmy watched as his mom mixed some medicine and put it on his boo-boo. He giggled as she put a silly bandage on it with cartoon characters. "Thank you, Mommy," Timmy said with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to build towers with his blocks. One day, he built the tallest building he had ever made. It was so tall, it almost touched the sky! 

But then, a fierce wind blew and knocked the tower down. Timmy was very sad. His mom came to comfort him and said, "Timmy, it's okay. We can build it again, but this time we'll stir the blocks together with glue." 

Timmy learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but with a little help and some stirring, he could make his tower even stronger than before. The moral of the story is to never give up and to always keep building, even when things get tough.

From that day on, the frog would hop over to the tree every day to listen to the bird's song. The bird and the frog became good friends and would sing and hop together. The frog loved his new friend and was grateful for the beautiful song that brought them together.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the garden. They see a big tree with many fruits. The fruits are red and round. They look yummy.

"Can we pick some fruits?" Lily asks Ben.

"OK, but we have to ask Mom first," Ben says. They run to the house and find Mom.

"Mom, can we pick some fruits from the tree?" Ben asks.

"Sure, but only a few. The fruits are not regular. They are special. They make you grow very fast," Mom says.

Lily and Ben are curious. They want to grow very fast. They run back to the tree and pick two fruits each. They bite into them. They are sweet and juicy.

"Wow, these are good!" Lily says.

"Yes, they are!" Ben says.

They finish their fruits and start to feel funny. They look at each other and gasp. They are growing very fast! Their clothes are too small. Their shoes are too tight. Their heads are touching the branches.

"Help! We are too big!" Lily cries.

"Mom! Mom!" Ben shouts.

Mom hears them and comes to the garden. She sees them and laughs.

"Don't worry, my big kids. The fruits are magic. They only make you grow for a little while. Soon you will be regular again," Mom says.

She hugs them and gives them some water. They drink and wait. After a few minutes, they start to shrink. They are happy and relieved. They are regular again.

"Mom, we are sorry. We ate too many fruits," Lily says.

"It's OK, my loves. You were curious. But next time, listen to me. The fruits are for special occasions, not for every day," Mom says.

She helps them change their clothes and shoes. They hug and thank her.

"Can we still play in the garden?" Ben asks.

"Of course, but be careful. There are many other things to see and learn in the garden. And remember, you are perfect the way you are. You don't need to grow very fast," Mom says.

Lily and Ben smile and nod. They run to the garden and play. They are happy and regular.

Sara and Tom were bored. They had no toys to play with and no books to read. The sky was dull and grey. It looked like it was going to rain.

"Let's go outside and find something fun to do," Sara said to Tom. She had an urge to run and jump and explore.

"But it's cold and wet," Tom said. He did not want to leave the warm house. He liked to stay inside and watch TV.

"Come on, it's not that bad," Sara said. She pulled Tom by the hand and dragged him to the door. "Maybe we can find some flowers or bugs or rocks."

Tom followed Sara reluctantly. He put on his coat and boots and hat. He hoped they would not get too dirty or wet.

They walked around the yard and looked for interesting things. They saw a worm crawling on the ground, a bird singing on a branch, and a snail hiding in a shell. They picked some daisies and made a necklace for Sara. They threw some pebbles into a puddle and watched the ripples.

They were having fun, but they still wished the sun would come out and make everything bright and warm.

"Look, look!" Sara shouted suddenly. She pointed to the sky. "The sun is coming out!"

Tom looked up and saw a gap in the clouds. A ray of sunshine broke through and shone on their faces. They smiled and felt happy.

"Yay, the sun is here!" Tom said. He felt his urge to go back inside fade away. He wanted to stay outside and play with Sara.

They ran and chased each other in the sun. They laughed and shouted and had a good time. They forgot about the dull sky and the cold air. They were glad they went outside and found something fun to do.

Lily felt more sad and angry. She did not like Tom. He was mean and rude. She wanted to make him stop laughing. She grabbed his scissors and ran towards him. She said, "No, Tom, you are bad. You are mean. I will cut you."

Tom saw Lily coming with the scissors and he was scared. He tried to run away, but he tripped and fell. Lily reached him and stabbed him with the scissors. He screamed and bled. He felt a lot of pain.

Lily saw what she did and she was shocked. She did not mean to hurt Tom. She just wanted him to be nice. She dropped the scissors and ran away. She felt very troubled.

She opened the pack and took out a pink gum. She put it in her mouth and chewed. It was yummy. She blew a big bubble and popped it. She smiled. She took out a blue gum and chewed it too. She blew another bubble and popped it. She giggled.

She wanted to try all the colors. She took out a green gum, a yellow gum, a purple gum, and a red gum. She chewed them all together. It was hard to chew. It was not sweet. It was not soft. It was sticky and icky. She did not like it. She tried to blow a bubble, but it did not work. She tried to spit it out, but it did not come out. It was stuck to her teeth and her tongue and her lips. She felt bad.

She ran to her mom and showed her the gum. Her mom was not happy. She said, "Sara, you should not chew so much gum. It is bad for your teeth and your tummy. You need to rest and drink some water. I will help you get the gum out."

She took Sara to the bathroom and got a wet cloth. She gently wiped the gum from Sara's face. She used a comb to get the gum from Sara's hair. She used a toothbrush to get the gum from Sara's teeth. She used a spoon to get the gum from Sara's tongue. It took a long time. Sara was sorry.

When the gum was all gone, Sara hugged her mom and said, "Thank you, mom. I will not chew so much gum again. I will chew one gum at a time. I will be normal."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "You are welcome, Sara. I love you. You are my normal girl." They smiled and went to the couch. They cuddled and watched a show. Sara felt better. She rested.

Mom was in the kitchen, making lunch. She called them to come and eat. "Ben, Lily, it's time for lunch. Come and wash your hands, please."

Ben and Lily did not want to stop playing. They ignored Mom and kept zooming and crashing their cars. They made a lot of noise and mess.

Mom came to the living room and saw the cars scattered everywhere. She was not happy. She said, "Ben, Lily, look at this mess. You have to clean up your toys before you eat. It's not nice to leave them like this. Someone could trip and get hurt."

She picked up all the cars and put them in a big box. She carried the box to the closet and locked it with a switch. She said, "This switch is red. That means you can't open the closet. You can only open it when the switch is green. And the switch will only be green when you say sorry and promise to clean up your toys next time."

Ben and Lily nodded and said, "OK, Mom. We will. Thank you, Mom."

Leo was a little lion who liked to roar. He roared when he was happy, he roared when he was angry, he roared when he was bored. He roared so much that his mom and dad told him to stop.

"Leo, you are too loud!" his mom said. "You need to be quiet and listen to our order."

"But I want to roar!" Leo said. "Roaring is fun and makes me feel strong."

"Roaring is not fun for everyone," his dad said. "You are scaring the other animals and hurting their ears. You need to learn to be polite and respectful."

Leo did not like his mom and dad's order. He thought they were mean and silly. He decided to run away and find a place where he could roar as much as he wanted. He ran and ran until he reached a big hill. He climbed to the top and saw a beautiful view. He saw trees and flowers and birds and clouds. He felt happy and free. He opened his mouth and roared as loud as he could.

But then something strange happened. The hill started to shake and rumble. Leo felt the ground move under his feet. He felt dizzy and scared. He looked around and saw that the hill was not a hill at all. It was a giant turtle!

The turtle was angry and tired of Leo's roaring. He lifted his head and looked at Leo with his big eyes. He opened his mouth and roared back at Leo. His roar was louder and deeper than Leo's roar. It made Leo's ears hurt and his heart beat fast.

Leo realized that he had made a big mistake. He had roared at the wrong place and the wrong time. He had disturbed the turtle's sleep and made him mad. He felt sorry and ashamed. He wanted to go back to his mom and dad and say sorry.

He ran down the hill and looked for his home. He hoped that his mom and dad would forgive him and hug him. He learned his lesson. He decided to roar only when it was appropriate and not to bother anyone. He also decided to be more careful and curious about the world. He wondered what other animals and things he could find and learn from. He smiled and roared softly. He was still a little lion who liked to roar, but he was also a little lion who liked to listen and respect.

He tried to smash it with a hammer, but the hammer was too heavy. He tried to squeeze it with his hands, but the avocado was too slippery. He was very sad and hungry.

Tommy opened his eyes and saw his mom holding a plate. On the plate, there was a half of an avocado. It was soft and creamy. His mom had scooped out the seed and sprinkled some salt on it. She said, "This is a ripe avocado. It's very yummy and healthy. Do you want to try some?"

Tommy smiled and nodded. He sat up in his bed and took a spoon. He scooped some avocado and put it in his mouth. It was delicious. He said, "Mmm, thank you, mom. This is the best avocado ever. How did you find it?"

His mom said, "I went to the market and asked the seller. He showed me how to pick a ripe avocado. You have to look at the color, feel the skin, and press the stem. If it's dark green, smooth, and soft, it's ripe. If it's light green, rough, and hard, it's not ripe. You have to wait for it to ripen."

Tommy said, "Wow, that's very smart. I didn't know that. I was ignorant. I thought all avocados were the same."

His mom said, "That's okay, Tommy. You're not ignorant. You're just learning. There are many things you don't know yet, but you can always ask and find out. That's how you grow and learn."

Tommy hugged his mom and said, "I love you, mom. You're the best teacher ever. Can we have more avocado tomorrow?"

His mom said, "Of course, Tommy. We can have avocado every day. As long as you wake up with a smile and a curious mind."

She wanted to go see it up close. So, she carefully climbed down from the top of the cliff. When she got to the bottom, the pool was even bigger and clearer. She was happy and proud of the pool she had made.

The girl stayed for a while, swimming and playing in the pool. Then, when it started to get dark, she climbed back up the cliff and went home.

The girl was proud of the useful pool she had made, and she told other people about it. From that day on, her friends and family would go to the pool and enjoy it. And they would thank the girl for finding such a useful place.

Jen runs to Tim. She is scared. She is sorry. She says, "Tim, are you okay? I told you not to do that. You were bad. You should have listened to me."

Tim is sad. He is in pain. He is ashamed. He says, "Jen, you were right. I was bad. I should have listened to you. I am sorry. I learned my lesson. I will not do that again."

Jen hugs Tim. She is glad. She is kind. She says, "Tim, I forgive you. I am your friend. I will help you. Let's go home and tell mom. She will make you feel better."

They walk home together. They leave the apples alone. They know they did wrong. They know they can do better. They know they should be good.

The moral of the story is that it is important to be generous and kind to our friends, and to always be there to help them when they need us.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with blocks. They built towers, bridges, and castles with their blocks. Sometimes they shared their blocks, and sometimes they fought over them.

One day, they decided to have a contest. Who could build the highest tower with their blocks? They each took some blocks and started to stack them on the floor. Lily's tower was red and blue, and Ben's tower was yellow and green.

"Look at my tower, Lily!" Ben said. "It is taller than yours!"

"No, it is not!" Lily said. "My tower is taller than yours!"

They kept adding more blocks to their towers, trying to make them taller and taller. But they did not pay attention to how steady their towers were. They only cared about how high they were.

Soon, their towers became very wobbly and shaky. They swayed from side to side, and some blocks fell off. Lily and Ben did not notice. They were too busy arguing.

"I am almost finished!" Ben said. "I only need one more block!"

"Me too!" Lily said. "I only need one more block!"

They both reached for the last block on the floor. It was a big, dull, gray block. They both wanted it for their tower. They both grabbed it at the same time, and pulled hard.

"Let go!" Ben said.

"No, you let go!" Lily said.

They pulled and pulled, until the block snapped in half. They each fell back, holding a piece of the block. They looked at their towers, and gasped.

Both towers had collapsed. All their blocks were scattered on the floor. Their towers were gone.

They looked at each other, and felt sad. They had wasted their blocks, and their time, and their fun. They had been silly and greedy.

They remembered what their mom had told them once. "Wisdom is better than height," she had said. "Wisdom means knowing what is good and right, and being kind and fair."

They wished they had listened to their mom. They wished they had used their wisdom, and not their pride.

They put down their pieces of the block, and hugged each other.

"I am sorry, Lily," Ben said.

"I am sorry, Ben," Lily said.

Tom said, "Follow me, mister, follow me!" He led the man to the hole.

The man looked at the hole and saw the diamond. He said, "Wow, what a big diamond! It must be worth a lot of money! Thank you, kid, for showing me!"

The man took a rope and a bucket from his truck. He said, "Kid, hold this rope. I'm going to get the diamond."

Tom said, "But what about my friend? She is in the hole, too!"

The man said, "Don't worry, kid, I'll get her out later. First, I need to get the diamond. It is more important."

The man lowered the bucket into the hole. He said, "Hey, girl, put the diamond in the bucket. I'll pull you up."

Lily said, "But the diamond is mine! I found it!"

The man said, "No, girl, the diamond is mine! I have the rope and the bucket. Put the diamond in the bucket or I'll leave you in the hole."

Lily was scared. She did not want to stay in the hole. She put the diamond in the bucket.

The man pulled up the bucket. He took the diamond and smiled. He said, "Ha, ha, ha, I got the diamond! It is mine, all mine!"

Tom said, "But what about my friend? You said you would get her out!"

The man said, "Sorry, kid, I lied. I don't care about your friend. I only care about the diamond. Bye, bye, kid!"

The man got into his truck and drove away with the diamond. He left Tom and Lily in the park.

Tom cried. He said, "Lily, I'm so sorry. I should have never wanted the diamond. It was a bad thing. It made us fight and it made the man take it and leave us. It was not worth it."

Lily cried, too. She said, "Tom, I'm so sorry, too. I should have never kept the diamond. It was a greedy thing. It made me run and fall and it made the man trick us and leave us. It was not worth it."

Tom and Lily were stuck in the park. They did not know what to do. They wished they had never seen the diamond. They wished they had been nice to each other. They wished they had been calm and smart.

The moral of the story is: Diamonds are not always a girl's best friend. Sometimes, they can cause trouble and pain. It is better to be kind and share than to be selfish and greedy. And it is better to be calm and smart than to be angry and foolish.

Lily liked to whistle. She whistled all the time. She whistled when she woke up, when she played, when she ate, and when she went to bed. She whistled so much that her mom and dad got tired of it. They told her to stop whistling so loud and so often. But Lily did not listen. She thought whistling was fun and normal.

One day, Lily saw a big bowl of cherries on the table. She loved cherries. They were red and sweet and juicy. She wanted to eat them all. She did not ask her mom and dad if she could have some. She just took the bowl and ran to her room. She whistled as she ate the cherries. She whistled so loud that she did not hear her mom and dad calling her name.

But Lily did not know that some of the cherries had pits inside. Pits are hard and small and can hurt you if you swallow them. Lily did not look at the cherries before she ate them. She just put them in her mouth and whistled. She did not feel the pits until it was too late. One of the pits got stuck in her throat. She could not breathe. She could not whistle. She could not call for help. She felt scared and sorry.

Her mom and dad found her on the floor. They tried to help her. They called the doctor. But it was too late. Lily was gone. They cried and cried. They wished they had told her to be careful with the cherries. They wished they had listened to her whistling. They wished they had hugged her and told her they loved her.

The moral of the story is: You should always listen to your parents. They know what is good and bad for you. You should also be careful with what you eat. You should not whistle when you eat. You should not eat too much or too fast. You should enjoy the things you have, but not be greedy or rude. You should be happy and normal, but not too loud or too often. You should love and respect yourself and others. You never know when it might be too late.

Tom and Lily smiled and held up the rock and the ring. "Look, auntie, we found a treasure!" they said.

Their aunt looked at the rock and the ring. She recognized the ring. It was her ring. She had lost it in the yard a long time ago. She was so happy to see it again. She hugged Tom and Lily and thanked them. "You're right, you found a treasure!" she said. "But you still need a bath!"

But then, they saw something unknown on the table. It was a small bottle with a red cap. It had a label that said "Shrink". They did not know what it meant. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Look, Lily, a new toy!" Tim said. He grabbed the bottle and opened the cap. He smelled it and made a face. "It smells bad. Maybe it is juice."

"Let me try!" Lily said. She took the bottle from Tim and poured some on her doll. The doll started to shrink. It became smaller and smaller until it was as tiny as a bug. Lily gasped. "Oh no! What happened to my doll?"

Tim was scared. He did not want his truck to shrink too. He threw the bottle away. But it landed in the bin. The bin started to shrink. It became smaller and smaller until it was as tiny as a coin. The bottle fell out of the bin and rolled under the sofa.

Tim and Lily ran to their mom. They told her what they did. Mom was angry and worried. She went to the living room and looked for the bottle. She found it under the sofa. She read the label and sighed. It was not a toy. It was a science experiment that dad had brought home from work. He had forgotten to put it away.

Mom explained to Tim and Lily that they should never touch unknown things. They could be dangerous or harmful. She said they were lucky that nothing bad happened to them. She said she would try to fix their toys and the bin. She said they should always ask before they play with something new.

Tim and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They hugged mom and said they were sorry. They learned their lesson. They never touched unknown things again. They played with their toys and had fun. They were happy.

One day, he saw a new girl in his class. Her name was Lily. She had a big smile and a lot of ink pens. Tom wanted to talk to her, but he was shy. He watched her from his seat, and saw that she liked to draw too. She drew flowers and animals and stars. Tom thought her drawings were pretty and nice.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge people by their appearance or their hobbies. Be kind and respectful to everyone. Stand up for yourself and your friends. Friendship can make you happy.

Lily was happy and said, "Yes, I do!" The boy had a lot of toys available to play with, so they played together all day long. When it was time to go home, Lily said, "Thank you for playing with me. Can we be friends?" The boy smiled and said, "Yes, we can!" Lily was so happy that she arrived home with a big smile on her face.

One day, Sarah and her mom went to the park. They brought bread to make toast. Sarah was excited to eat the toast. 

While they were making toast, a bird flew down and scared Sarah. "Mommy, the bird scared me!" Sarah said. 

"Don't worry, sweetie. The bird just wanted some bread too," her mom said. 

After they finished making toast, they sat down to eat. Sarah took a bite and said, "This toast is dull. Can we put jelly on it?" 

"Of course, honey," her mom replied. They put jelly on the toast and it tasted much better. They enjoyed their picnic and had a great day at the park.

They both marked the aeroplane on the paper. They made different shapes and colours. They said, "Our aeroplane is the best aeroplane in the world!"

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog has rough skin and sharp teeth. The dog barks at them.

"Go away, dog!" Anna says. "You are scary!"

But the dog does not go away. The dog runs to them. Anna and Ben are afraid. They run to the swings. The dog follows them.

"Help, help!" Ben cries. "The dog wants to bite us!"

A man hears them. The man is the dog's owner. He runs to the park. He sees the dog and the children.

"Stop, stop!" the man says. "He is a good dog. He does not want to bite you. He wants to play with you."

The man calls the dog. The dog comes to the man. The man puts a leash on the dog.

"I am sorry," the man says. "He is a new dog. I just sent him from the farm. He does not know the city. He does not know how to be gentle. He needs to learn."

Anna and Ben stop crying. They look at the dog. The dog wags his tail. He looks sorry.

"Can we pet him?" Anna asks.

"Yes, you can," the man says. "But be careful. His skin is rough. He might lick you."

Anna and Ben pet the dog. The dog licks them. They laugh.

"His skin is rough, but his tongue is soft," Ben says.

"His bark is loud, but his heart is kind," Anna says.

They make friends with the dog. The man smiles.

"Thank you for being nice to him," the man says. "You are good children. You taught him a lesson. He learned that he should not be scary. He should be friendly."

The moral of the story is: Do not judge by appearances. Be kind to others. You might make a new friend.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car that they could ride in the garden. They took turns to drive the car and pretended to go on adventures.

One day, Sara had a dream that she was driving the car alone and that she could go anywhere she wanted. She saw beautiful places and met friendly animals. She was very happy and did not want to wake up.

The next morning, Sara told Tom about her dream. She said, "I had a wonderful dream. I drove the car by myself and had so much fun. I wish I could do that in real life."

Tom felt sad and jealous. He said, "But we always share the car. It is not fair that you want to keep it for yourself. You are a bad sister."

Sara did not care. She said, "I don't want to share anymore. It is my car and my dream. You can play with something else."

Tom was angry and hurt. He said, "Fine. Then I don't want to play with you anymore. You are a selfish sister."

They stopped talking to each other and went to their rooms. They did not play together for the rest of the day.

That night, Sara had another dream. But this time, she was not driving the car alone. She was chased by scary monsters and got lost in a dark forest. She was very afraid and wanted to go home. She cried and called for Tom, but he did not come.

She woke up feeling very uncomfortable and scared. She realized that her dream was a nightmare and that she had been very mean to Tom. She wished she had not been so greedy and rude.

She got out of bed and ran to Tom's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Tom, I'm sorry. I had a bad dream. I don't want to keep the car for myself. I want to share it with you. Can we be friends again?"

But Tom did not answer. He was asleep and did not hear her. He had a dream that he was playing with the car with a new friend who was kind and generous. He was very happy and did not want to wake up.

Sara felt lonely and sad. She learned that being selfish can make you lose your real friends and that sharing is better than having everything for yourself. But it was too late to fix her mistake. She had to wait until the next day to try to make up with Tom. She hoped that he would forgive her and that they could play together again.

The end.

Moral value: Sharing is caring. Being selfish can make you unhappy and lonely.

Finally, he saw the other fisherman stop at a small island. He saw him get off his boat and carry his fish to a hut. Ben thought, "This must be his home. Maybe he lives here alone with his fish. I will go and see."

He parked his boat near the island and walked to the hut. He knocked on the door and said, "Hello, can I come in?" He heard a voice say, "Who are you? What do you want?"

He opened the door and saw the other fisherman sitting on a chair. He saw his fish on a table. But they were not fresh and shiny. They were old and smelly. They had flies and worms on them. They were rotting.

Ben felt sick. He said, "Why do you keep these fish? They are bad. They are not good to eat. They are not good for anything."

The other fisherman looked at him and said, "These are my fish. I caught them with my boat and my net and my rod. They are mine. I do not want to share them with anyone. I do not want to sell them or give them away. I do not care if they rot. They are my treasure."

Ben felt sorry for him. He said, "You are not happy. You are lonely and greedy. You do not have any friends or family. You do not have any fun or joy. You only have rotting fish. That is not a good life."

He turned around and left the hut. He went back to his boat and sailed away. He thought, "I do not want to be like him. I do not want to be envious. I have enough. I have a good boat and a good net and a good rod. I have fresh and tasty fish. I have friends and family who love me. I have fun and joy. I have a good life."

"Let's go outside," Ben said.

"OK," Mia said.

They put on their shoes and coats and went to the backyard. They saw a big tree with red and yellow leaves. They saw a swing and a slide. They saw a ball and a bike. They saw a lot of things to do.

"Let's grab the ball and play catch," Ben said.

"OK," Mia said.

They grabbed the ball and threw it to each other. They had fun. They laughed and ran. They did not feel bored anymore.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a growl. It was a scary noise. It came from behind the fence. They stopped playing and looked at each other.

"What is that?" Ben asked.

"I don't know," Mia said.

They were afraid. They wanted to go back inside. They dropped the ball and ran to the door. But the door was locked. They forgot to take the key. They knocked and shouted.

"Mom, mom, let us in!" Ben said.

"Mom, mom, there is a noise!" Mia said.

But mom did not hear them. She was still on the phone. She did not know they were outside. She did not know they were scared.

They did not know what to do. They hugged each other and waited. They hoped the noise would go away. They hoped mom would come soon. They hoped it was not a monster.

But then he saw that the lake was too big. He could not jump over it. He was falling into the water. He was scared.

His mom and dad saw him and ran to the lake. They jumped into the water and swam to him. They grabbed him and pulled him out. They hugged him and kissed him. They were glad he was safe.

They told him that he was very gifted, but he should not jump over the lake. It was too dangerous. He could get hurt or drown. He should only jump over things that were small and safe.

"I just want to see how it looks," Ben said. He put the necklace around his neck. He smiled. He felt like a prince.

As Lily played with her rubber duckies, she noticed something strange floating in the water. "What's that?" she asked her mommy. "Oh no, it's your razor! It must have fallen in the water and gotten all yucky," said her mommy. "We need to throw it away before it starts to rot."

Lily didn't want her razor to rot, so she let her mommy throw it away. From then on, she made sure to keep her razor far away from the bathtub.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a velvet dress that was very soft and pretty. One day, she went to the park and saw a graceful swan swimming in the pond. 

Lily went closer to the swan and said, "Hello, Mr. Swan! You are very beautiful." The swan looked at Lily and said, "Thank you, little girl. You are very kind."

Suddenly, a loud noise came from the other side of the park. A man was yelling at his dog to come back. The swan got scared and started to swim away. Lily said, "Don't be afraid, Mr. Swan. The man is just calling his dog." 

The swan stopped swimming away and said, "Thank you for telling me. You are very kind and brave, little girl." Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Swan. Have a good day!"

But as Max was walking around, he accidentally got his zipper stuck on a shelf. He tried to wiggle free, but it was no use. Max's owner didn't notice and left the store without him. Poor Max was stuck there all alone. 

Hours passed and it started to get dark. Max was scared and lonely. He barked and barked, hoping someone would hear him. But no one came. Eventually, Max fell asleep, still stuck on the shelf. The next morning, the store workers found him and called his owner. Max was happy to be rescued, but he never forgot the scary night he spent trapped in the store.

He asked his mom if they could go outside and look at the truck. His mom said yes, and they went outside. When they got there, the driver of the truck saw Timmy and said hello. Timmy was so happy to meet the driver and see the powerful wheels on the truck. 

After they said goodbye to the driver, Timmy went back inside to finish stirring the soup. His mom tasted it and said it was delicious. Timmy was so proud that he helped make the soup taste so good.

Her friend replied, "I'm good, thank you. What are you doing?"

Her friend said, "I wish I had a purple telephone too."

The veterinarian gave Spot some medicine and told his owner to keep an eye on him. She also gave Spot's owner an original toy to keep Spot happy while he was recovering. Spot's owner was very grateful to the veterinarian for helping Spot feel better.

As they played, Timmy's team was losing. But then, Timmy saw an opportunity. He kicked the ball as hard as he could and it went flying into the goal! "I did it!" Timmy shouted. "I scored a goal!"

His friends cheered and clapped. "You're mighty good at soccer, Timmy!" one of them said. Timmy smiled and felt proud. Suddenly, it started to rain. Timmy and his friends didn't mind, though. They kept playing and splashing in the puddles. It was the best day ever.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park with their ball. They saw a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. The dog was running and barking. Lily and Tom wanted to pet the dog, but they did not know if it was friendly or not.

"Let's go and say hello to the dog," Lily said.

"No, we should not," Tom said. "The dog might be wild and bite us."

"What does wild mean?" Lily asked.

Tom tried to explain. "Wild means the dog does not have a home or a person. It lives by itself and does not know the rules. It might be scared or angry and hurt us."

"Oh, I see," Lily said. "But how can we tell if the dog is wild or not?"

Tom thought for a moment. He remembered what his mom had told him. "We can look for a collar. A collar is a thing that goes around the dog's neck. It has a tag with the dog's name and the person's phone number. If the dog has a collar, it means it has a home and a person. If it does not have a collar, it might be wild."

Lily and Tom looked at the dog. They saw that it had a collar with a shiny tag. They felt happy and relieved. They decided to walk slowly and quietly towards the dog. They held out their hands and let the dog sniff them. The dog wagged its tail and licked their faces. It was friendly and gentle. Lily and Tom petted the dog and played with it. They had fun.

A lady came running towards them. She looked worried and out of breath. She called the dog's name. It was Bella. The lady was Bella's person. She thanked Lily and Tom for finding her dog. She said Bella had run away from her leash and she had been looking for her. She said Bella was very important to her and she loved her very much.

Lily and Tom learned that dogs are not always wild and that they have feelings too. They learned that they should be careful and respectful when they meet a new dog. They learned that collars are helpful and that people care for their pets. They learned that it is good to help others and to be kind to animals. They felt proud and happy. They said goodbye to Bella and her person and went back to their ball. They continued to play in the park.

One day, they saw a big dog running towards them. It was barking and growling. Lila and Ben were fearful. They did not like the dog. They wanted to go to their nest and hide.

"Quick, Ben, we have to prepare!" Lila said. "We have to get to the tree before the dog gets us!"

They ran to the oak tree and climbed as fast as they could. The dog followed them and tried to jump and bite them. But it was too big and clumsy. It could not reach them.

"Ha ha, we are safe!" Ben said. "The dog can't get us here!"

They looked down and saw the dog still barking and jumping. They felt sorry for the dog. Maybe it was lonely and wanted to play.

"Maybe we can be friends with the dog," Lila said. "Maybe it is not so bad."

They threw some sticks and leaves to the dog. The dog stopped barking and started to wag its tail. It picked up the sticks and leaves and brought them back to the tree.

"Look, it likes us!" Ben said. "It wants to play fetch!"

Lila and Ben smiled. They decided to give the dog a chance. They climbed down from the tree and petted the dog. The dog licked their faces and wagged its tail.

They had a new friend. They named him Oak. They played with him until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to Oak and promised to come back tomorrow. They were not fearful anymore. They were happy.

Tom is a bald boy. He does not have any hair on his head. He likes to wear hats and scarves to cover his head. He does not like when other kids laugh at him or call him names.

One day, Tom wakes up and sees a new hat on his bed. It is blue and has a star on it. He is very happy. He puts on the hat and goes to school. He thinks he looks cool and smart.

But when he gets to school, he sees a mean boy named Max. Max is bigger and stronger than Tom. He likes to bully and tease other kids. He sees Tom's hat and says, "Hey, baldy, what are you hiding under that hat? Is it a big egg? Let me see!"

Max grabs Tom's hat and pulls it off his head. He laughs and shows Tom's bald head to everyone. He says, "Look, everyone, it's baldy Tom! He has no hair! He looks like a baby!"

Tom feels very sad and angry. He wants his hat back. He says, "Give me back my hat, Max! It's mine! You are mean and rude!"

Max says, "No, I won't! It's my hat now! You don't deserve it! You are ugly and weird!"

Tom tries to get his hat back, but Max pushes him away. He falls on the ground and hurts his knee. He cries and feels alone.

Then, he hears a voice. It is his friend Lily. Lily is a kind and brave girl. She likes Tom and does not care that he is bald. She says, "Tom, are you okay? Don't listen to Max. He is a bully and a liar. You are not ugly or weird. You are beautiful and special. You are my friend."

Lily helps Tom get up and hugs him. She says, "Here, I have something for you. It is lotion. It is good for your head. It makes your skin soft and smooth. It also smells nice. Do you want to try it?"

Tom nods and smiles. He says, "Yes, please. Thank you, Lily. You are very nice and sweet. You are my friend too."

Lily puts some lotion on Tom's head and rubs it gently. She says, "There, how do you feel?"

Tom feels better. He says, "I feel good. I feel warm and cozy. I like the lotion. It makes me happy."

Lily says, "I'm glad. You know, I think you look great without a hat. You don't need to hide your head. You should be proud of who you are. You are unique and wonderful. You have a big heart and a bright mind. That's what matters."

Tom says, "You are right, Lily. I don't need a hat. I don't need to be like everyone else. I need to be myself. I am proud of who I am. And I am grateful for your friendship."

Lily says, "Me too, Tom. Me too."

They hug and smile. They walk to the classroom together. They see Max with Tom's hat. He looks bored and lonely. He tries to make fun of Tom and Lily, but they ignore him. They know he is not worth their time or attention. They know he is unhappy and insecure. They feel sorry for him, but they also feel strong and confident. They have each other, and they have lotion. They have everything they need.

The moral of the story is: Be yourself and be proud of who you are. Don't let bullies or mean words hurt you or change you. Find friends who love you and support you. Share kindness and happiness with others. And always have lotion. Lotion is good.

"Nothing," Sam and Ben said.

Their dad looked at them and smiled. He knew they were hiding something. He went to their bed and lifted the sheet. He saw the broken watch.

"Boys, what did you do?" he asked.

Sam and Ben looked down and said sorry. They told him they wanted to see how the watch worked, but they broke it and tried to repair it.

Their dad was not angry. He hugged them and said he loved them. He told them he was proud that they wanted to learn, but they should have asked him first. He said the watch was very old and special. It belonged to his grandfather, who gave it to him when he was a boy. He said the watch was worth more than gold, because it had memories and love.

Sam and Ben nodded and said they would. They learned that some things are not cheap, and that they should respect their dad's things. They also learned that their dad was very kind and forgiving. They hugged him and said they loved him too.

The man smiled and said, "Sure, I have a coin. But you have to pay me for it. How about you buy an ice cream from me? They are very cheap, only one coin each."

Tom and Lily thought for a moment. They liked ice cream, but they also wanted to make a wish. They decided to buy one ice cream and share it. They gave the man one coin and took the ice cream. They thanked the man and ran back to the fountain.

They ate the ice cream quickly and enjoyed it. Then they had one coin left. They held the coin together and closed their eyes. They made a wish. They wished for more ice cream. They threw the coin in the fountain and watched it splash.

They opened their eyes and waited. They hoped their wish would happen. But nothing happened. They felt sad and confused. They wondered why their wish did not happen.

Then they heard a voice behind them. It was the man who sold them the ice cream. He said, "Hello, kids, I saw you throw a coin in the fountain. That was very nice of you. But you know what? Tom and Lily were surprised and happy. They took the coin and the ice cream. They thanked the man and said, "It's okay, mister, we forgive you. You are very kind. Thank you for the coin and the ice cream."

They made another wish. They wished for the man to have many customers and sell many ice creams. They threw the coin in the fountain and watched it sparkle.

They ate the ice cream slowly and enjoyed it. They felt happy and hopeful. They wondered if their wish would happen. They hoped it would. They smiled at each other and at the man. They had a good day.

They became friends and talked about the weather. The bird was happy to have a new friend and the tree was happy to have a visitor.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toy boat. He would take it to the pond and watch it float on the water. One day, Timmy's mom suggested they go on a real boat ride. Timmy was excited and couldn't wait to go.

They arrived at the dock and got on a big boat. Timmy was amazed at how clean and shiny it was. They sailed off into the ocean and Timmy was having a great time. Suddenly, the sky turned dark and the waves started to get bigger. Timmy's mom tried to steer the boat back to shore, but it was too late. The boat hit a big rock and started to sink.

Timmy and his mom were scared and didn't know what to do. They held onto the boat as long as they could, but eventually, they had to let go. They swam to shore and were safe, but Timmy's toy boat was lost forever. Timmy learned that sometimes, even when things seem fun and clean, bad things can happen.

However, as soon as he started looking around, the boy heard something strange. It sounded like a loud roar and he knew he was not alone. The boy quickly realized that he was standing in the middle of a lion's den. Suddenly, the lion started charging towards the boy.

The ordinary boy was in a real bind. He did not know how to get out, so he quickly ran into the wreck and closed the door. He stayed inside the wreck until the lion had finished its business and then the boy carefully started walking back home.

The end.

The moral of the story is that shaking back in the face of adversity can show strength and bring joy. By standing strong and shaking back during difficult times one can find happiness.

He jumped out from behind the tree and made a loud noise. "Screech! Screech! These are my nuts! Go away!" he shouted. He ran towards the children and tried to bite them.

Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped the nuts and ran away. The nuts scattered all over the ground. The squirrel chased them until they were out of the wood.

Lily and Ben felt sorry for the squirrel. They did not mean to make him mad. They just wanted to play. They decided to go back and say sorry.

They walked slowly to the pile of nuts. They saw the squirrel sitting on top of it. He looked sad and tired. He had to pick up all the nuts again.

"Hello, squirrel," Lily said. "We are sorry we took your nuts. We did not know they were yours. We wanted to make houses for the animals."

The squirrel looked at them. He saw that they were humble and kind. He felt a little better. He said, "It's okay. I forgive you. But please don't take my nuts again. They are very important to me. I need them for the winter."

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "We understand. We won't take your nuts again. Can we be friends?"

The squirrel smiled. He said, "Yes, we can be friends. You can help me pick up the nuts. And I can show you how to make houses for the animals."

Lily and Ben were happy. They helped the squirrel pick up the nuts. And they learned how to make houses for the animals. They had fun in the wood. And they made a new friend.

Lily and Ben were playing on the shore. They liked to make sand castles and look for shells. The sun was brilliant and made the water sparkle.

"Look, Lily, I found a big shell!" Ben said, holding up a pink and white shell. "It has a hole in it. Maybe a crab lived in it."

"Wow, Ben, that's a pretty shell!" Lily said. "Can I see it?"

Ben nodded and gave Lily the shell. She put it to her ear and listened.

"What do you hear, Lily?" Ben asked.

"I hear the sea!" Lily said. "It sounds like whoosh, whoosh, whoosh."

They laughed and took turns listening to the shell. Then they saw a big rock near the water. It was flat and smooth.

"Let's seat on the rock and watch the waves!" Ben said.

"Okay!" Lily said. They ran to the rock and climbed on it. They sat on the rock and watched the waves. They saw fish and birds and boats. They felt the breeze and the spray. They were happy.

Lila and Sam were playing in the garden. They liked to look at the flowers and smell them. Lila saw a rose that was red and pretty. She wanted to pick it and give it to her mom.

"Look, Sam, a rose!" she said. "I want to get it for mom. Can you help me?"

Sam nodded. He was a good friend. He went to the rose with Lila. But the rose had thorns. They were sharp and pointy. They could hurt Lila and Sam.

"Be careful, Lila," Sam said. "The rose has thorns. They can make you bleed."

Lila did not know what bleed meant. She reached for the rose. But Sam stopped her. He took a clear plastic cup from his backpack. He put it over the rose. He broke the stem with his hands. He gave the cup with the rose to Lila.

"Here, Lila," he said. "Now you can give the rose to mom. The cup will protect you from the thorns."

Lila smiled. She was happy. She thanked Sam. She hugged him. She ran to her mom with the cup and the rose.

"Mom, mom, look what I have for you!" she said. "A rose! Sam helped me get it. He is a good friend."

Mom smiled. She was proud of Lila and Sam. She took the cup and the rose. She smelled the rose. She kissed Lila and Sam.

"Thank you, Lila and Sam," she said. "This is a beautiful rose. And you are very kind and smart. I love you both."

Anna and Ben like to play in the garden. They see a big vine on the wall. The vine has many green leaves and purple flowers.

"Look, a vine!" Anna says. "Let's climb it and see what is on the other side."

"OK, but be careful," Ben says. "The vine may be weak and break."

Anna and Ben hold the vine and start to climb. They go higher and higher. They see birds and bees and butterflies. They feel happy and excited.

"Wow, this is so fun!" Anna says. "I can see the whole garden from here."

"Me too!" Ben says. "And I can see the house and the road and the park."

They reach the top of the wall. They see another garden on the other side. The garden has many toys and swings and slides.

"Look, a playground!" Anna says. "Let's go and play there."

"No, we can't," Ben says. "That is not our garden. That is someone else's garden. We have to ask first."

"But they are not here," Anna says. "And we are only going to play for a little while. It is not fair that they have so many toys and we have none."

"That is not fair, but it is not right to take what is not ours," Ben says. "We have to go back to our garden and play with what we have."

Anna and Ben argue. They do not agree. They do not listen to each other. They pull the vine and make it shake.

Suddenly, the vine snaps. Anna and Ben fall down. They land on the ground. They hurt their knees and elbows. They cry and scream.

Their mom and dad hear them. They run to the garden. They see Anna and Ben on the ground. They see the broken vine on the wall.

"What happened?" their mom and dad ask. "Are you OK?"

Anna and Ben tell them what they did. They say they are sorry. They say they were wrong.

Their mom and dad hug them. They say they are glad they are not hurt. They say they love them.

They also say they have to learn to share and respect. They say they have to be careful and listen. They say they have to be fair and kind.

Anna and Ben nod. They say they understand. They say they will try.

They go back to their garden. They play with their own toys. They have fun. They are happy.

Sara loved to draw with her colors. She had many colors: red, blue, yellow, green, pink, purple, and more. She liked to make pictures of her family, her friends, and her dreams. She dreamed of flying in the sky like a bird. She wanted to soar high and see the clouds and the sun.

One day, she drew a picture of herself with wings. She used her blue color for the sky, her white color for the clouds, and her yellow color for the sun. She used her pink color for her wings, and her brown color for her hair. She was very happy with her picture. She showed it to her mom and dad, and they smiled and said it was very pretty.

She wanted to show it to her teacher and her classmates, too. She put it in her backpack and went to school. When she got to school, she took out her picture and put it on her desk. She waited for her teacher to see it and say something nice.

But then, Billy, a boy who sat next to her, saw her picture and laughed. He said, "What is that? That's not you. You don't have wings. You can't fly. You look silly. That's a bad picture." He grabbed her picture and tore it in half. He threw it in the trash.

Sara felt very sad and angry. She felt ashamed of her picture and her dream. She wanted to cry, but she didn't. She looked at Billy and said, "That was not nice. That was mean. You hurt my feelings. You hurt my picture. My picture was good. My dream was good. I can fly in my dream. I can soar in my dream. You can't take that away from me."

She got up and took her picture out of the trash. She taped it back together. She put it in her backpack. She said, "I don't care what you say. I like my picture. I like my dream. I'm proud of my picture. I'm proud of my dream."

She went to her teacher and showed her the picture. She told her what Billy did and what she said. Her teacher hugged her and said, "I'm sorry that Billy was rude to you. He was wrong. Your picture is beautiful. Your dream is wonderful. You are brave and smart and creative. You should never be ashamed of your picture or your dream. You should always soar in your dream and in your life."

Lily and Ben were playing hide and seek in the house. Lily was the seeker and Ben was the hider. Ben ran to the kitchen and saw a big cupboard. He opened the door and crawled inside. He closed the door and waited for Lily to find him.

Lily looked in the living room, the bedroom, and the bathroom, but she could not find Ben. She wondered where he was hiding. She went to the kitchen and saw the cupboard. She thought Ben might be inside. She opened the door and shouted, "Boo!"

Ben was scared by the loud noise. He jumped out of the cupboard and bumped his head on the shelf. He started to cry. Lily saw that he was hurt and felt sorry. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to scare you. Are you okay?"

Ben rubbed his head and said, "It's okay, Lily. It was just a game. But you were very loud. You made my ears hurt."

Lily said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't know you were deaf. I thought you could hear me."

Ben said, "I'm not deaf, Lily. I can hear you. But sometimes I wear these things in my ears. They help me hear better. See?" He showed her his hearing aids.

Lily said, "Oh, I see. They are like little phones for your ears. That's cool. Can I try them?"

Ben said, "No, Lily. They are only for me. They are special. If you try them, they might not work for you. And you might break them. Then I would be sad."

Lily said, "Okay, Ben. I won't try them. I don't want to make you sad. I want to make you happy. Do you want to play another game?"

Ben said, "Yes, Lily. I want to play another game. But can we leave the cupboard? It's dark and small. And it has spiders."

Lily said, "Yes, Ben. We can leave the cupboard. Let's go to the garden. It's bright and big. And it has flowers."

Ben said, "Okay, Lily. Let's go to the garden. Maybe we can find some butterflies."

Lily and Ben left the cupboard and went to the garden. They played and laughed and had fun. They were good friends.

A boy heard her scream and came to see what was wrong. He saw the tiny Lily and the spider. He grabbed a ruler and scared the spider away. He picked up Lily and put her on his hand. He looked at the book and saw the word that Lily had said. He guessed what had happened.

"Don't worry, I'll help you," he said. "You have to say the word backwards to undo the spell. Try to say it with me. Oo-dak-nirhs!"

Lily repeated the word with him. "Oo-dak-nirhs! Oo-dak-nirhs!"

She felt another strange feeling. She looked around and saw that everything was normal again. She had grown back to her normal size!

She hugged the boy and thanked him. He smiled and said, "You're welcome. That was a very brave thing you did. You should be proud of yourself. You learned something new about history and magic today."

Lily nodded and smiled. She was proud of herself. She learned a lot today. She decided to put the book back on the shelf and look for another one. Maybe one that was not so old and shiny.

"Wow, a green car cloud!" Ben said, surprised.

"Maybe it is a magic car cloud," Lily said, curious.

They wondered what the green car cloud could do. Maybe it could fly faster than other clouds. Maybe it could make rainbows. Maybe it could talk.

"Hello, Lily and Ben," the green car cloud said.

Lily and Ben gasped. The green car cloud could talk!

"Hello, green car cloud," they said, shyly.

"I am a magic car cloud," the green car cloud said. "I can grant you one wish each. What do you wish for?"

Lily and Ben thought hard. They had many wishes. They wished for toys, candy, books, and more. But they also wished for something else.

"I wish for a big hug from my mom," Lily said.

"I wish for a big hug from my dad," Ben said.

The green car cloud smiled. "Those are very good wishes," it said. "I will grant them for you. But first, you have to close your eyes and count to ten."

Lily and Ben closed their eyes and counted to ten. When they opened them, they saw their mom and dad running towards them. They ran to meet them and hugged them tightly.

"Mom, dad, we missed you so much!" they said.

"We missed you too, sweeties," their mom and dad said. "We came to pick you up from the park. How was your day?"

Lily and Ben looked at the sky. The green car cloud was gone. It had vanished.

"It was a magic day," they said. "We saw a green car cloud that talked and granted our wishes."

Their mom and dad smiled and kissed them. They did not believe them, but they were happy to see them so happy.

They all walked home together, holding hands. Lily and Ben looked at the sky and thanked the green car cloud for their wishes. They hoped to see it again someday.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the garden. They had a big box of toys that they could use. One day, they found a shiny metal thing in the dirt. It looked like a coin, but it had a picture of a man with a funny hat on it.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said, holding the metal thing. "It is so shiny and lovely!"

"Let me see!" Lily said, reaching for it. "Maybe it is magic!"

They took turns looking at the metal thing. They wondered who the man with the funny hat was, and where the metal thing came from. They decided to keep it as a treasure.

"Let's bury it again, so no one can find it!" Tom said. "We can dig it up when we want to see it!"

"Good idea!" Lily said. "But we need to mark the spot, so we don't forget!"

They dug a small hole in the dirt and put the metal thing inside. Then they covered it with more dirt and patted it down. They looked around for something to mark the spot. They saw a big red flower in the garden.

"Let's use this!" Lily said, picking the flower. "It is so pretty and bright!"

She stuck the flower in the dirt, next to the hole. It looked like a flag.

"There!" Tom said. "Now we have a secret treasure!"

They smiled at each other and hugged. They were happy to have found something so shiny and lovely. They ran back to their box of toys and played some more. They did not know that the metal thing was a very old and rare coin, worth a lot of money. They only knew that it was their treasure, and they loved it.

One day, they are playing with the jet in the living room. Ben holds the jet and says, "I am the pilot. I can fly the jet very fast and high." Mia says, "I am the co-pilot. I can help you fly the jet and see the clouds." They make the jet zoom and swoop around the sofa and the table.

But then, Ben sees a bowl of lemons on the kitchen counter. He likes lemons. He thinks they are sweet and juicy. He says to Mia, "I want a lemon. Let's land the jet and get a lemon." Mia says, "OK, but be careful. The jet is heavy and the lemons are sour."

Ben and Mia land the jet on the floor and run to the kitchen. Ben reaches for a lemon and tries to peel it. But the lemon is hard and sticky. He pulls and pulls, but he cannot peel it. He gets angry and throws the lemon on the floor. The lemon rolls and hits the jet. The jet falls and breaks. The jet makes a sad noise and stops.

Ben and Mia are shocked. They look at the broken jet and the lemon. They feel bad. They love the jet. They say, "Oh no! We broke the jet! We are sorry, jet!" They pick up the jet and try to fix it. But they cannot fix it. The jet is too broken. They hug the jet and cry. They say, "We are sorry, jet! We will miss you!"

"Sure, but be careful. Hold on tight and don't let go of your cap," Mom says.

Lily and Ben run to the slide. They take turns to go down. Lily holds on to her cap. She likes her cap. It is pink and has a flower on it. Ben does not care about his cap. He thinks it is boring. It is blue and has nothing on it.

Ben is careless. He lets go of his cap when he slides down. The cap flies off his head and lands on a tree. Ben does not notice. He runs back to the slide.

"Look, Ben, your cap is on the tree!" Lily says.

"Where?" Ben says.

"Up there! See?" Lily says. She points to the tree.

Ben looks up. He sees his cap. He feels sad. He likes his cap now. He wants it back.

"Mom, help me get my cap!" Ben says.

Mom comes over. She sees the cap on the tree. She shakes her head.

"Ben, you were careless. You should have held on to your cap. Now it is too high for me to reach. We need to find a ladder or a stick," Mom says.

Lily and Ben look around. They see a ladder and a stick. They run to get them. They bring them to Mom. Mom uses the ladder and the stick to get the cap. She gives it to Ben.

"Thank you, Mom," Ben says.

"You're welcome, Ben. But next time, be careful. Don't lose your cap again," Mom says.

Ben nods. He puts on his cap. He holds on to it. He does not want to be careless again. He and Lily hug Mom. They go back to the slide. They have fun. They are happy.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. One day, they see a man with a big bag. He is selling beans.

"Hello, little ones," the man says. "Do you want to buy some beans? They are magic beans. They can grow very tall and take you to a wonderful place."

Sara and Ben are curious. They have some coins in their pockets. They give them to the man and take some beans.

"Thank you, little ones," the man says. "But be careful. You have to plant the beans in the ground and water them. And you have to wait until the night. Then, something amazing will happen."

Sara and Ben run to the garden. They dig some holes and put the beans in them. They water them with a hose. Then, they go inside and wait for the night.

When it is dark, they look out of the window. They see something shiny and light in the garden. It is a big beanstalk. It reaches up to the sky.

"Wow!" Sara and Ben say. "The beans are really magic. Let's go and climb the beanstalk. Maybe we can find the wonderful place."

They put on their coats and shoes and sneak out of the house. They run to the beanstalk and start to climb. They are very excited. They wonder what they will see at the top.

Lily was a furry mouse who liked to move around the house. She was looking for some cheese to eat, but she had to be careful of the big cat. The cat was always trying to catch her and make her his snack.

One day, Lily saw a big piece of cheese on the table. She wanted to get it, but she knew it was a trap. The cat was hiding under the chair, waiting for her to come. Lily had a plan. She found a ball of yarn and rolled it to the other side of the room. The cat saw the yarn and ran after it, thinking it was a toy.

Lily quickly moved to the table and climbed up. She took a bite of the cheese and it was very yummy. She was about to take another bite when she heard the cat coming back. He had seen her and was angry. He jumped on the table and tried to catch her.

"Meow! You are my cheese, little mouse!" the cat said.

"No, I am not! You are mean, big cat!" Lily said.

She moved fast and ran to the edge of the table. She saw a basket of flowers and jumped into it. The flowers smelled nice and hid her from the cat. The cat could not find her and gave up. He went back to his bed and fell asleep.

Lily was happy and safe. She ate some more cheese and then moved to a cozy corner of the basket. She curled up and took a nap. She dreamed of more cheese and more yarn. She was a clever and furry mouse.

One day, a boy named Tom and a girl named Sue went to the park. They saw a big hill with many flowers. They wanted to play there. They ran up the hill and looked around. They saw a big tree with a hole in it.

"Look, Tom, what is in the hole?" Sue asked.

Tom went closer and peeked inside. He saw a big sack. It was brown and dirty. It had a hole too. He smelled something bad.

"Yuck, Sue, this sack is smelly. It has garbage in it. Someone threw it away here. That is not nice," Tom said.

Sue came closer and looked too. She saw a banana peel, a can, a sock, and a toy. She felt sorry for the toy. It was a bear. It had one eye and a torn ear. It looked sad.

"Tom, can we take the bear? Maybe we can clean it and fix it. It needs a home," Sue said.

Tom nodded. He reached inside the hole and took the bear. He held it carefully. He felt something move inside the sack. He heard a meow.

"Look, Sue, there is a cat in the sack too. It is hiding under the garbage. It is scared and hungry. Can we help it?" Tom asked.

Sue nodded. She loved cats. She reached inside the hole and took the cat. It was black and white. It had a scratch on its nose. It looked tired.

"Tom, we need to take the cat and the bear to our house. Maybe Mom can help them. They need food and water and love," Sue said.

Tom agreed. He put the bear in his pocket. Sue held the cat in her arms. They ran down the hill and to their house. They prayed that Mom would let them keep the cat and the bear. They wanted to be their friends.

Lily was a curious girl. She liked to look at things and ask questions. One day, she saw a big sack in her mom's closet. She wondered what was inside. She opened the sack and saw many shiny things. They were teeth!

Lily was very surprised. She knew that teeth came from mouths. Why did mom have so many teeth in a sack? She took one tooth and looked at it closely. It was white and hard. She felt a hole in it. She remembered that her brother Tom had a hole in his tooth. He said it hurt a lot.

Lily ran to Tom's room. She wanted to show him the tooth. She thought maybe it was his. She knocked on the door and said, "Tom, look what I found!"

Tom opened the door and saw Lily holding a tooth. He was angry. He said, "That's my tooth! Give it back! Mom took it last night when I was sleeping. She said she would put it under my pillow for the tooth fairy. How did you get it?"

Lily felt bad. She did not know that mom was doing something nice for Tom. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I found it in a sack in mom's closet. I was curious. I did not mean to take it."

Tom said, "That's okay, Lily. But you should not look in mom's closet. That's not polite. And you should not touch other people's things. That's not nice. The tooth fairy will not come if you do that."

Lily said, "I understand, Tom. I will not do it again. Can I give you back your tooth?"

Tom said, "Yes, please. And let's put it under my pillow. Maybe the tooth fairy will still come. She might forgive us."

Lily and Tom hugged. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect mom's privacy and Tom's property. They learned to be less curious and more careful. They hoped the tooth fairy would be kind and generous.

Lily liked grapes very much. She liked to eat them one by one and make funny noises with them. She liked to roll them on the floor and chase them. She liked to pretend they were balls and throw them in the air.

One day, Lily saw a big bunch of grapes on the table. She wanted to have them all. She climbed on a chair and reached for the grapes. But her mom saw her and said, "No, Lily, those are not for you. Those are for the guests. You can have some later."

Lily was stubborn. She did not listen to her mom. She grabbed the grapes and ran away. She hid under the bed and started to eat them. She thought she was very clever.

But her mom was clever too. She knew where Lily was. She followed her and said, "Lily, come out of there. You are being naughty. You have to share the grapes. And you have to say sorry."

Lily did not want to come out. She did not want to share. She did not want to say sorry. She repeated, "No, no, no!" She kept eating the grapes.

But then, she felt something in her mouth. It was a seed. She did not like seeds. They were hard and bitter. She spit out the seed and made a face. She tried another grape. It had a seed too. And another. And another. All the grapes had seeds.

Lily did not like the grapes anymore. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had waited for later. She wished she had been nice.

She crawled out of the bed and looked at her mom. Her mom was not angry. She was smiling. She said, "Lily, I have a surprise for you. Come and see."

Lily followed her mom to the table. There, she saw a bowl of grapes. But they were not the same grapes. They were bigger and shinier and greener. And they had no seeds.

Lily's mom said, "These are seedless grapes. They are sweet and juicy and easy to eat. You can have some now. But you have to share with the guests. And you have to say sorry."

Lily nodded. She said, "Sorry, mom. I was wrong. I will share. I will be good."

She took a grape and bit it. It was delicious. She smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love these grapes."

Lily was scared of the dark. She did not like to sleep in her bed alone. She thought there were monsters under her bed and in her closet. She always asked her mom to stay with her until she fell asleep.

One night, her mom was very tired. She had a lot of work to do. She told Lily to be brave and to close her eyes. She said there were no monsters, only shadows and toys. She gave Lily a hug and a kiss and turned off the light.

Lily tried to be brave, but she could not sleep. She heard noises and saw shapes in the dark. She pulled her blanket over her head and hugged her white teddy bear. She wished her mom was with her.

Suddenly, she heard a loud sigh from under her bed. She was very scared. She thought it was a monster. She screamed and cried for her mom.

Her mom came running to her room. She turned on the light and looked under the bed. She saw a big, furry, white monster with horns and claws. She was surprised and scared too.

But then, the monster looked at her and said in a small voice, "Please don't be mad. I'm sorry I scared you. I'm not a bad monster. I'm just lonely. I have no friends. Can I be your friend?"

Lily and her mom looked at each other. They felt sorry for the monster. He looked sad and harmless. They decided to give him a chance. They invited him to sleep on Lily's bed with them. They gave him a hug and a kiss and turned off the light.

Lily was not scared of the dark anymore. She had a new friend. The monster was happy too. He had a new family. They all slept peacefully and dreamed of happy things.

Lila was a new girl in the village. She did not know anyone. She felt sad and lonely. She wanted to make friends and play.

One day, she saw some children playing with a ball near a big tree. She walked to them and said, "Hello, can I play with you?"

The children looked at her and said, "No, you can't. You are new. You are not one of us. Go away."

Lila felt hurt and angry. She said, "That is not nice. You should share and be kind. I want to play with you."

The children said, "No, you can't. You are new. You are not one of us. Go away."

Lila did not give up. She said, "Yes, I can. I am new. But I can be one of you. I can play with you."

The children said, "No, you can't. You are new. You are not one of us. Go away."

Lila shouted, "Yes, I can. I am new. But I can be one of you. I can play with you."

The children shouted, "No, you can't. You are new. You are not one of us. Go away."

They shouted and shouted. They made a lot of noise. They did not listen to each other.

Then, a big voice said, "Stop! What is going on here?"

It was the teacher. She came from the school. She heard the shouting. She was not happy.

She said, "Why are you shouting? Why are you not playing nicely? Why are you not welcoming the new girl?"

The children were quiet. They felt ashamed. They did not have a good answer.

The teacher said, "Lila is new. She wants to play with you. She wants to be your friend. You should be nice to her. You should share and be kind. You should not shout and be mean. Do you understand?"

The children nodded. They said, "Yes, teacher. We understand. We are sorry."

The teacher said, "Good. Now, say sorry to Lila and invite her to play with you."

The children said, "Sorry, Lila. We were wrong. Do you want to play with us?"

Lila smiled. She said, "Yes, I do. Thank you."

The children smiled. They gave Lila the ball. They played with her. They had fun.

Lila was happy. She made new friends. She felt part of the village.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play together. They lived in a big house with many toys and books. They were wealthy, but they did not know what that meant. They only knew that they had everything they wanted.

One day, they found a bottle in the garden. It was shiny and blue, and it had a cork on top. They wondered what was inside. They pulled the cork and a cloud of smoke came out. They were scared and ran away.

But then they heard a voice. It said, "Hello, I am a genie. I live in the bottle. You have freed me, so I will grant you three wishes. What do you want?"

Lila and Tom stopped and looked at each other. They did not know what to wish for. They had everything they wanted.

They thought for a while, and then Lila said, "I wish for a name for the genie. He must be lonely in the bottle."

The genie smiled and said, "That is a very kind wish. Thank you. You can name me anything you like."

Lila and Tom thought for a while, and then Tom said, "How about Bob? Bob is a nice name."

The genie nodded and said, "Bob it is. I like it. Thank you. You have two more wishes. What do you want?"

Lila and Tom thought for a while, and then Lila said, "I wish for a friend for Bob. He must be bored in the bottle."

The genie smiled and said, "That is another very kind wish. Thank you. I will make a friend for me. What do you want her to be like?"

Lila and Tom thought for a while, and then Lila said, "She should be nice and funny and smart. And she should like blue, like the bottle."

The genie nodded and said, "I will make her like that. Thank you. You have one more wish. What do you want?"

Lila and Tom thought for a while, and then Tom said, "I wish for a bigger bottle for Bob and his friend. They must be cramped in the small bottle."

The genie smiled and said, "That is the last and the best wish. Thank you. You are very generous and thoughtful. I will make a bigger bottle for us. It will have windows and doors and furniture and books and toys. It will be like a home."

The genie snapped his fingers and a bigger bottle appeared. It was shiny and blue, and it had a cork on top. The genie opened the cork and invited Lila and Tom to see inside. They saw a beautiful room with everything they had wished for. They also saw a girl who looked like the genie. She smiled and said, "Hello, I am Bob's friend. You can name me anything you like."

Lila and Tom smiled and said, "How about Ann? Ann is a nice name."

The girl nodded and said, "Ann it is. I like it. Thank you. You are very nice."

The genie and the girl hugged Lila and Tom and thanked them again. They said, "You have made us very happy. We will always remember you. You can visit us anytime you want. Just open the cork and say hello."

Lila and Tom said goodbye and closed the cork. They took the bottle and put it in their room. They were happy too. They had made new friends. They did not need any more wishes. They had everything they wanted.

Lily and Ben looked at each other and shrugged. They had not chosen anything. They had just taken the blocks they liked and put them where they wanted. Sometimes they helped each other, and sometimes they argued. But they had fun.
