"Lily and Ben, where did you get this block?" she asked.

Lily and Ben looked at the block and then at each other. They knew they were in trouble. They had taken some of the ornaments from the tree and used them as blocks. They thought they were pretty and made the castle more special. But they had not asked Mom if they could do that.

They hung their heads and said in a small voice, "We took it from the tree, Mom. We're sorry."

"Lily and Ben, I'm glad you like the ornaments, but they are not blocks. They are for the tree, and they are fragile. You could break them or hurt yourself with them. You should not take things that are not yours without asking. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We're sorry."

Mom smiled and hugged them. "It's okay. I forgive you. But you have to put the ornaments back on the tree, and be more careful next time. And you can keep your castle, but only with the real blocks. Okay?"

Lily and Ben agreed and said, "Okay, Mom. Thank you."

They ran to the tree and put the ornaments back where they belonged. Then they went back to their castle and played with it some more. They learned their lesson and did not take any more unusual blocks. They still had fun with their castle, and Mom was proud of them.

"A hurricane?" Sara asked, not knowing what that was.

"Yes, a hurricane. It's a big, scary storm with a lot of wind and rain. It can break things and hurt people. But my truck is strong and brave and can escape from it," Tom explained, making his truck zoom around the room.

Sara felt a little scared of the hurricane, but she also wanted to see it. She wondered what it looked like and how it sounded. She asked Tom if they could pretend there was a hurricane in their game.

"Okay, but you have to be careful. The hurricane can knock down your castle and your doll. You have to hide with me in my truck," Tom said.

"Alright, let's do it," Sara agreed.

They moved their toys to the middle of the room and pretended that the wind was blowing and the rain was falling. They made whooshing and splashing sounds with their mouths. Tom pretended that his truck was driving through the storm, while Sara held her doll close to her chest.

"Mom, mom, what was that?" they asked, scared.

"It's okay, kids, it's just a thunderstorm. It's like a small hurricane, but not as bad. It will pass soon. Come here, I'll hug you," their mom said, comforting them.

They hugged their mom and felt safer. They realized that their game was not as fun as they thought. They decided to play something else when the storm was over. Maybe something with animals or pirates. But not with hurricanes. They didn't like hurricanes.

When Bob reached the big flower, he opened it and found lots of sweet stuff inside. He was very happy. After eating, Bob flew back to his friends and told them about the cross and the big flower. They all wanted to see it, so they flew across the field together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was very enthusiastic about playing with his toy cars. One day, he was playing with his cars in the living room when his mom called him.

"Tim, it's time to pause your play and go to the toilet!" she said.

Tim didn't want to stop playing, but he knew he had to listen to his mom. So, he put down his cars and went to the toilet. After he finished, he washed his hands and went back to play with his cars.

Later, Tim's friend, Ella, came over to play. They both had fun playing with the toy cars. Ella said, "Tim, I like playing with you because you share your toys and listen to your mom."

Tim smiled and said, "Thanks, Ella! I learned that it's good to pause and do what we need to do, even if we don't want to."

And so, Tim and Ella played happily together. The moral of the story is that it's important to listen and do what we need to do, even if it means pausing our fun for a moment.

Lily went back outside to the garden. She picked the pretty rose very carefully. Then, she brought the rose to her mom. Her mom was so happy to see the rose. She said, "Thank you, Lily! This rose is beautiful, and your hands are clean too!" Lily smiled, happy that she could bring her mom a pretty rose without making it dirty.

The squirrel attached the rope to the deer and the tree. The deer climbed the tree with the help of the rope. From the top of the tree, he saw his family. He was so happy. The deer thanked the squirrel and went back to his family. They all played together in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a tidy little bunny named Bobo. Bobo loved to hop all day long. One day, as he hopped around his room, he found a big mirror. Bobo had never seen a mirror before. He looked at it and saw another bunny that looked just like him.

"Hello!" said Bobo to the bunny in the mirror. "Do you like to hop too?" The bunny in the mirror didn't talk, but it looked like it was hopping when Bobo hopped. They hopped together for a while, and Bobo was very happy.

After a fun day of hopping, Bobo's mom called him for dinner. Bobo said goodbye to his new friend in the mirror and went to eat. He told his mom all about the bunny he met and how they hopped together. His mom smiled and said, "That was your reflection, Bobo. You were hopping with yourself!" Bobo laughed and thought it was funny. From that day on, he always had a friend to hop with in the mirror.

They hugged each other and walked back to the bench. They sat down and looked at the remaining cone.

"Here, Lily. You can have the rest of my cone. I don't want it anymore," Ben said, offering her the cone.

"No, Ben. You can have it. You were nice to share with me. I don't want it anymore either," Lily said, pushing the cone back to him.

They stared at the cone, not knowing what to do. They felt sorry for themselves and for each other.

Then, they heard a voice behind them.

"Hello, kids. I saw what happened. That dog was very naughty. He stole your cone. I'm sorry about that," the voice said.

They turned around and saw the ice cream man. He was holding two new cones in his hands.

"I have a surprise for you. I made you two new cones. They are special cones. They have all the flavors you like. Vanilla, chocolate, strawberry, and banana. They are also very deep. They have more ice cream inside than outside. Do you want them?" the ice cream man said, smiling.

Lily and Ben's eyes widened. They couldn't believe it. They nodded eagerly and thanked the ice cream man.

"Here you go, kids. Enjoy your cones. And remember, sharing is caring. You are very good friends. You know how to share and be kind. That's more important than any cone," the ice cream man said, giving them the cones.

Lily and Ben took the cones and smiled. They licked their cones happily and felt the ice cream fill their mouths. They were delicious. They were the best cones ever.

They looked at each other and laughed. They were happy again. They learned a lesson. They learned that sharing is caring. They learned that being kind is better than being greedy. They learned that sometimes, good things happen to good people.

They thanked the ice cream man again and waved goodbye. They ran to the swings and played together. They shared their cones and their joy. They were friends who knew how to have fun.

Zip was a little fish who liked to swim fast and play with his friends. He was not afraid of anything, not even the big sharks who sometimes came near his home. One day, he saw a shiny thing at the bottom of the sea. He wanted to see what it was, so he swam down, down, down, until he reached the deep part of the water.

"Wow, what is this?" he said to himself, as he touched the shiny thing. It was a ring, with a pretty stone that sparkled in the light. Zip put it on his fin and felt very happy. He decided to show it to his friends and swam up, up, up, to the shallow part of the water.

But as he was swimming, he did not notice a big shadow behind him. It was a shark, who had seen the shiny thing and wanted to have it for himself. He opened his mouth and tried to bite Zip, who was too busy looking at his ring.

"Help, help!" Zip cried, as he saw the shark coming closer. He was scared and did not know what to do. He wished he had stayed with his friends and not gone to the deep part of the water.

But then, he heard a loud splash and saw a big tail. It was his friend, Fin, who had heard his cry and came to save him. Fin was a dolphin, who was very strong and smart. He hit the shark with his tail and made him go away.

"Are you okay, Zip?" Fin asked, as he swam to Zip and hugged him.

"Yes, thank you, Fin. You saved me. You are my best friend," Zip said, as he hugged him back.

"I'm glad you are safe, Zip. But what is that shiny thing on your fin?" Fin asked, as he noticed the ring.

"Oh, this? I found it in the deep part of the water. It is very pretty, but it is also very dangerous. The shark wanted to have it and tried to eat me," Zip said, as he took off the ring and gave it to Fin.

"Here, you can have it. You deserve it. You are my hero," Zip said, as he smiled.

"Thank you, Zip. But I don't need it. You can keep it. It is a gift from the sea. Just be careful next time and don't go to the deep part of the water alone. There are many things that can hurt you there," Fin said, as he gave the ring back to Zip.

"Okay, Fin. I will. And I will always stay with you and our friends. You are right. There are many things that can hurt me in the deep part of the water, but there are also many things that can make me happy in the shallow part of the water. Like you," Zip said, as he put the ring back on his fin.

"Me too, Zip. Me too," Fin said, as they swam away together, happy and safe.

Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, I forgive you. Come on, let's go meet my friends. They're very nice. You'll like them."

Kim felt sad and angry. She said, "No, your boat is not better! My boat is nice and bouncy!" She tried to blow harder on her boat, but it did not help. Tim's boat reached the other side of the tub first, and he cheered. He said, "I win, I win! You lose, you lose!"

Kim started to cry. She said, "You are mean, Tim! You are not a good brother!" She picked up her boat and threw it at Tim. Tim dodged the boat, but it hit his boat and knocked it over. Tim's boat sank in the water, and he gasped. He said, "Hey, what did you do? You broke my boat!"

Kim felt sorry for what she did. She said, "I'm sorry, Tim. I was mad at you, but I should not have thrown my boat at you. That was wrong." She helped Tim get his boat out of the water. Tim looked at his boat and saw that it was wet and cracked. He said, "It's okay, Kim. I'm sorry, too. I was rude to you, and I should not have laughed at your boat. That was not nice."

They hugged and said they were sorry. They decided to share their boats and play together. They learned that their boats were different, but they were both good. They also learned that being kind and fair was more important than being fast and strong. They had more fun when they were friends.

Tom and Lily felt sorry for the fish. They wanted to help it escape.

"Maybe we can find a way to get you out of here," Lily said. "But how?"

They looked around and saw a big bucket near the tank. It was filled with water and had a sign that said "Do not touch".

"Look, there is a bucket," Tom said. "Maybe we can put the fish in the bucket and take it to the sea."

"Be careful, fish," Lily said. "We will take you to the sea soon."

The fish felt the water in the bucket. It was fine. It thanked Tom and Lily and hoped they would escape too.

But her sister did notice. She saw the dress sticking out from under the bed. She pulled it out and gasped. The dress was ruined. It had holes and stains from Lily's chewing. She was very sad and angry.

She yelled at Lily, "What did you do to my dress? This was my favorite dress! It was a gift from grandma! She was very generous to give it to me! How could you be so mean and selfish? You are a bad sister!"

Lily felt sorry and scared. She did not mean to hurt her sister or the dress. She just wanted to play. She started to cry and said, "I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I didn't know, I just liked the dress, please don't be mad at me!"

But her sister did not forgive her. She said, "You are not sorry, you are a liar and a thief! You always chew on things that are not yours! You are a naughty girl and you don't deserve anything nice! Go to your room and stay there!"

She pushed Lily out of her room and slammed the door. Lily ran to her room and sobbed. She wished she had never chewed on the dress. She wished her sister would love her again. She wished she could be a good girl. But she did not know how. She felt very lonely and sad. The end.

Ben and Mia were two rabbits who lived in a big garden. They liked to eat fresh herbs and play in the grass. One day, they saw a new herb that looked very tasty. It had purple flowers and a strong smell.

"Let's try it!" said Ben.

"Wait, I don't know if it is good for us," said Mia.

"Don't be silly, it is just a herb. Come on, it will be fun!" said Ben.

He took a big bite of the herb and felt a strange feeling. He started to hop around and make funny noises. He felt very happy and crazy.

"Mia, this herb is amazing! You have to try it!" he said.

Mia was worried. She saw that Ben was acting very different. He was not careful of the fence or the cat or the road. He was in danger.

"Ben, stop! That herb is not good for you! It makes you crazy!" she said.

She ran after him and tried to catch him. She wanted to help him and take him back to their home. But Ben was too fast and too crazy. He did not listen to her.

He hopped over the fence and into the road. He did not see the big car that was coming. He did not hear Mia's scream.

The car hit Ben and he fell to the ground. He did not move. He did not hop. He did not make funny noises. He was gone.

Mia was very sad. She cried and cried. She wished she could have stopped Ben. She wished he had listened to her. She wished they had never seen that herb.

She learned a hard lesson. She learned that some herbs are bad for rabbits. She learned that being crazy is not fun. She learned that she should be careful and wise.

She never ate that herb again. She never forgot Ben. She always missed him.

Her mom heard her. She ran to the garden. She saw Lia and the snake. She was shocked. She grabbed Lia and ran to the car. She drove to the hospital. She hoped Lia would be okay.

But Lia was not okay. The snake was poisonous. The bite was bad. The doctors tried to help her. But they were too late. Lia died. Her mom was sad. She wished she had watched Lia better. She wished Lia had not lifted the rock. She wished Lia had not seen the butterfly.

One day, he saw a big island with many trees and flowers. He wanted to explore it and find new things to mix. He sailed his boat to the shore and jumped out. He saw a monkey hanging from a branch. He said hello to the monkey and asked if he could mix some bananas with him.

The monkey nodded and threw some bananas to Sam. Sam peeled them and put them in a bowl. He looked around for something else to mix with the bananas. He saw a coconut on the ground. He picked it up and tried to open it. He hit it with a rock, but it was too hard. He hit it harder and harder, until it cracked and spilled coconut water all over him.

The monkey laughed and clapped his hands. He said, "You are a funny sailor. You make a big splash with the coconut. Do you want to mix more things with me?"

Sam smiled and wiped his face. He said, "Yes, I do. You are a friendly monkey. You have many things to mix on this island. Let's go and see what we can find." He took the bowl of bananas and followed the monkey into the jungle. They had a lot of fun mixing different things and making new friends.

Sue was scared. She did not know what to do. She hugged Tim and tried to calm him down. She wished they had not played in the old house. She wished they had listened to their mom, who told them to stay away from the cobwebs.

The moral of the story is: Do not destroy things that are not yours. You might get hurt or make someone else angry. Be careful and respectful of other living things.

Mom sees Anna and hugs her. She says, "Don't be afraid of the bee, Anna. The bee is helpful. The bee helps the flower. The bee takes the flower's sweet stuff and makes honey. The bee does not want to sting you. The bee just wants to move to another flower."

Anna listens to mom. She feels better. She says, "I'm sorry, bee. I didn't know you were helpful. I like honey. I like flowers. I like to move. Can we be friends?" She smiles at the bee. The bee buzzes and flies away. Anna and mom move to another flower and smell it. They are happy.

Lily loved to admire the roses in her garden. She liked their colors, their smells, and their shapes. She wanted to be like them, so she tried to grow her own roses in a pot. She was gifted with a green thumb, and her roses were beautiful.

One day, a lady came to visit Lily and her mom. The lady was mom's friend, and she brought a cake for them. Lily liked the cake, but she liked her roses more. She wanted to show them to the lady, so she ran to her pot and picked one of her roses.

"Look, look!" Lily said, holding the rose in her hand. "This is my rose. I grew it myself. Isn't it pretty?"

The lady smiled and nodded. "Yes, it is very pretty, Lily. You are very gifted. Can I have it?"

Lily was surprised. She did not want to give her rose to the lady. She loved her rose. It was hers. She shook her head and said, "No, no. This is my rose. You can't have it."

The lady frowned and looked angry. She grabbed the rose from Lily's hand and said, "Don't be rude, Lily. You should share your things. This is my rose now. You can have the cake."

Lily felt a sharp pain in her hand. The rose had thorns, and they pricked her skin. She saw blood on her fingers, and she started to cry. She wanted her rose back, but the lady had already put it in her hair. She looked at her mom, but her mom did not help her. Her mom said, "Lily, stop crying. You should be nice to our guest. The lady likes your rose, and you should be happy for her. You can have another rose later."

Lily felt sad and angry. She did not like the lady, or the cake, or her mom. She felt like she had lost her rose, and her gift, and her joy. She ran to her room and slammed the door. She did not want to see anyone. She wished she had never admired the roses in her garden.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys in their room. Tom has a big truck that can make noise and move. Sam has a small car that can display light and change color. Tom thinks his truck is better than Sam's car. He says to Sam, "My truck is tough. Your car is not. My truck can crush your car."

Sam does not like what Tom says. He loves his car. He says to Tom, "No, my car is tough too. Your truck is not. My car can display light and make your truck blind."

Tom and Sam start to fight. They push and pull each other's toys. They yell and cry. They do not listen to their mom, who tells them to stop and share. They are very angry and mean.

Then, something bad happens. Tom pulls Sam's car too hard. The car breaks. The light goes off. The color fades. Sam is very sad. He looks at his car and cries. He says to Tom, "You broke my car. You are a bad brother. I hate you."

Tom feels sorry. He did not mean to break Sam's car. He says to Sam, "I am sorry. I did not want to break your car. I like your car. It can display light and change color. It is cool. You are a good brother. I love you."

But Sam does not listen to Tom. He is too sad and mad. He throws his car at Tom. The car hits Tom's head. Tom feels pain. He screams and cries. He says to Sam, "You hurt me. You are a bad brother. I hate you."

Mom hears Tom and Sam. She runs to their room. She sees the broken car and the bleeding head. She is very worried and angry. She says to Tom and Sam, "What did you do? You are both naughty. You broke your toys and hurt each other. You do not love each other. You make me sad."

Mom takes Tom and Sam to the doctor. The doctor fixes Tom's head and gives him a bandage. The doctor says to Tom and Sam, "You are lucky. You could have been more hurt. You should be nice to each other. You should not fight over toys. You should display love and care."

Tom and Sam feel ashamed. They wish they did not fight. They wish they did not break their toys and hurt each other. They wish they did not make their mom sad. They wish they could say sorry and hug. But they do not. They are too scared and shy. They look away and stay quiet.

The end.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make races with their cars on the floor.

"Ready, set, go!" Tom says. He pushes his red car fast. Sam pushes his blue car fast too. They watch their cars zoom on the floor. They want to win the race.

But then, Tom's car hits a book and stops. Sam's car keeps going and passes Tom's car. Sam smiles. He thinks he will win.

"Hey, that's not fair!" Tom says. He is angry. He picks up his car and throws it at Sam. Sam ducks and the car misses him. It hits the wall and makes a loud noise.

"Ow, that hurts!" Sam says. He is sad. He drops his car and runs to his mom. He tells her what Tom did.

Tom feels bad. He knows he did a wrong thing. He quits the race. He goes to Sam and his mom. He says he is sorry.

"Sorry, Sam. I was mad because you were going to win. But that was no reason to throw my car at you. Can we be friends again?" Tom says.

Sam looks at Tom. He sees that Tom is sorry. He nods. He says he is sorry too.

"Sorry, Tom. I was happy because I was going to win. But that was no reason to smile at you. Can we play again?" Sam says.

Tom and Sam hug. They are friends again. They pick up their cars and go back to the floor. They make a new race. They push their cars gently. They do not care who wins. They just have fun. They play with their cars until it is dark. Then they turn on the light and play some more.

Lily and Tom felt sorry and scared. They did not mean to make a fire. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I did not want to share," Tom said.

Lily and Tom said they loved Mom too. They said they would be careful and listen to her. They said they would share and play nicely. They picked up their blocks and started to build again. They used the red block together. They were happy.

One day, they decided to have a battle with the dragon. The dragon was a big red blanket that they spread on the grass. Tom was the knight and Mia was the dragon. Tom ran towards the blanket with his sword and shouted, "I will save the princess from the dragon!"

Mia hid under the blanket and made loud noises. She moved the blanket to look like the dragon was breathing fire. She said, "You cannot defeat me, knight! I am the strongest and fiercest dragon in the land!"

Tom was not afraid. He swung his sword at the blanket and tried to hit the dragon. But he was clumsy and he tripped over a rock. He fell down and dropped his sword. The sword flew in the air and landed on the castle. The castle fell apart and the cardboard pieces flew everywhere.

Mia saw what happened and stopped making noises. She came out of the blanket and ran to Tom. She asked, "Are you okay, Tom? Did you hurt yourself?"

Tom rubbed his knee and said, "I'm okay, Mia. But I broke the castle. I'm sorry. I'm a bad knight."

Mia hugged him and said, "You're not a bad knight, Tom. You're a brave knight. And I'm not a mean dragon, I'm your friend. We can fix the castle together. And we can play again tomorrow."

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Mia. You're a nice dragon. And you're my friend too. Let's fix the castle and have a picnic."

They picked up the cardboard pieces and the sword and the shield and the blanket. They put them back in the box and carried it to the porch. They had some sandwiches and juice and cookies. They shared their food and their stories. They had fun and they were happy.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play outside. Every morning, she would wake up and put on her pink dress and her yellow shoes. She would say hello to her mom and dad, and then run to the garden.

In the garden, there were many flowers and trees and birds. Lily loved to smell the flowers and watch the birds. She also had a friend who lived in the garden. His name was Ben, and he was a pale bunny. He had soft fur and long ears and a twitchy nose.

Lily and Ben would meet every morning and play together. They would hop and run and hide and seek. They would share carrots and berries and nuts. They would tell each other stories and jokes and secrets. They were very happy.

One morning, Lily went to the garden as usual. But she could not find Ben. She looked behind the roses and under the bushes and in the hole. She called his name and listened for his voice. But there was no sign of him.

Lily felt sad and lonely. She wondered where Ben was and if he was okay. She missed him very much. She sat on the grass and waited for him.

After a while, she heard a rustle in the leaves. She looked up and saw Ben. He was carrying a big basket full of flowers and fruits. He smiled and ran to her.

"Surprise!" he said. "I went to the other side of the garden to find these for you. They are for our friendship. I hope you like them."

Lily was so happy to see Ben. She hugged him and thanked him. She loved the gifts. She said he was the best friend ever.

They put the basket on the grass and enjoyed the treats. They laughed and talked and cuddled. They forgot about the time and the world. They only saw each other.

They were very happy.

Ben and Lily were twins, but they were very different. Ben liked to play with cars and trucks, and Lily liked to draw and sing. Ben thought Lily was unique, but not in a good way. He thought she was weird and silly, and he often teased her.

One day, their mom said they had to go to the store, because a big storm was coming. She said it was called a hurricane, and it could break things and make a lot of noise. Ben and Lily were scared, but they got in the car with their mom.

At the store, Lily saw a big box of crayons. She wanted to buy them, but mom said no. Lily was sad, and she started to cry. Ben saw her, and he laughed. He said, "Stop crying, you baby! You don't need crayons, you need a brain!" He said it very loud, and everyone heard him. Lily felt very embarrassed, and she hid behind mom.

Mom was angry, and she told Ben to apologize. But Ben was stubborn, and he said no. He said he was just telling the truth, and Lily was a crybaby. Mom said, "That's enough, Ben. You are being very rude and mean. You need to learn to respect your sister, and her unique talents. She is not weird, she is creative and smart. And you are not better than her, you are just different. Now, say you are sorry, or we are going home."

But Ben did not listen. He said, "No, I won't say sorry. I don't care about Lily, or her stupid crayons. I want to buy a toy car, and I want it now!" He threw a tantrum, and he kicked and screamed. He made a big mess, and he knocked over a shelf. The shelf fell on him, and he got hurt. He cried, and he called for mom. But mom was too busy helping Lily, who was scared and hurt by the shelf. Mom said, "I'm sorry, Ben, but you brought this on yourself. You were very naughty and selfish, and you embarrassed us all. Now, you have to wait until we get home, and then you will be punished. No toy car for you, and no TV for a week. And you still have to say sorry to Lily, and mean it."

Ben felt very sorry, but not for Lily. He felt sorry for himself. He wished he had been nicer to Lily, and listened to mom. He wished he had not made fun of her, or caused a scene. He wished he had not been hit by the shelf, or lost his toy car. He wished he had not been so mean and stupid. He wished he had not been in the store, or in the car, or in the hurricane. He wished he had been anywhere else. But it was too late. He had made a big mistake, and he had to face the consequences. He had a bad ending.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play house. They had a toy kitchen with a dishwasher, a stove, and a fridge. They pretended to cook, clean, and eat together. Sometimes they said they wanted to marry each other when they grew up.

One day, Anna's mom bought her a new dress with flowers and ribbons. Anna was eager to show it to Ben. She put it on and ran to his house. She knocked on the door and said, "Ben, Ben, look at my new dress! It's so pretty!"

Ben opened the door and saw Anna. He smiled and said, "Wow, Anna, you look very nice. Do you want to play house with me?"

Anna nodded and followed Ben to his toy kitchen. But when she saw the dishwasher, she frowned. It was dirty and full of dishes. She said, "Ben, why didn't you wash the dishes? They are yucky and smelly. You have to wash them before we play."

Ben shrugged and said, "I don't like to wash dishes. It's boring and hard. You can do it if you want. I'll wait for you."

Anna was angry and hurt. She said, "No, Ben, that's not fair. If we play house, we have to share the work. You can't make me do everything. That's not how you treat someone you want to marry."

Ben looked confused and said, "But Anna, you're the girl. Girls are supposed to wash dishes. Boys are supposed to do other things, like watch TV or play games."

Anna shook her head and said, "No, Ben, that's not true. Girls and boys can do anything they want. They can wash dishes, or watch TV, or play games, or anything else. And they should help each other and be kind. That's what my mom and dad do. They love each other and they share the work. That's what I want to do when I grow up. And that's what I want from someone I want to marry."

Ben thought for a moment and realized that Anna was right. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. You're right. I was wrong. I should have washed the dishes. I was lazy and selfish. I don't want to lose you as a friend. Will you forgive me?"

Anna smiled and said, "Of course, Ben. I forgive you. You're still my friend. And maybe one day, we can still marry each other. But only if you promise to wash the dishes sometimes."

Ben nodded and said, "I promise, Anna. I promise. Come on, let's wash the dishes together. And then we can play house and have fun."

Anna and Ben hugged and went to the dishwasher. They washed the dishes together and then played house happily. They learned that if they want to marry someone, they have to respect them, help them, and love them. And that's the moral of the story.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toy boats in the bathtub. They pretended they were sailors and explorers, looking for new lands and treasures. They had a big map with many islands and seas, and they took turns to choose where to go.

"I want to go to this island," Tom said, pointing to a green spot on the map. "It looks like it has many trees and animals. Maybe we can find some bananas or coconuts there."

"OK, let's go," Sara said, moving her boat towards the green island. "But be careful, there might be pirates or sharks on the way. We have to watch out for danger."

They made sounds of waves and wind as they sailed their boats across the bathtub. They imagined they saw dolphins and whales jumping out of the water, and birds flying in the sky. They also pretended they saw other boats with flags and cannons, and they had to avoid them or fight them.

"Look, we are almost there," Tom said, as he saw the green island getting closer. "It looks even bigger and greener than on the map. I wonder what we will find there."

"Me too," Sara said, as she followed him with her boat. "But we have to share whatever we find, OK? We are a team, and we have to be fair."

"OK, OK," Tom said, nodding. "We have to share. But I get to choose first, because I saw the island first."

"No, you don't," Sara said, shaking her head. "We have to take turns, or we have to yield. That means we have to let the other one choose sometimes, even if we want something very much. That's what mom and dad say."

"Fine, fine," Tom said, rolling his eyes. "We can yield. But only if we find something really good. Otherwise, we can keep what we like."

"Deal," Sara said, smiling. "Now let's go and explore the island. Maybe we will find something amazing."

Tom and Lily nod their heads.

"Then you can keep the robot and give the bear to someone who will love it. Do you understand?" Mom asks.

Tom and Lily understand. They agree to remove some of their old toys and keep some of their alert toys. They thank Mom for helping them. They hug Mom and each other. They start to play nicely with their toys. They are happy. Mom is happy too. She goes back to the kitchen. She smiles.

But as they walked, they heard a loud voice. It was the ice cream vendor. He had seen them. He was angry.

With a sad face, the little boy said, "I guess money is more important than a costume. I'm sorry." Mommy smiled and said, "That's okay. We'll just have to find something else that we'll all be happy with."

The moral of this story is that money is very important and we should always think about what is best for everyone, not just ourselves.

"Rabbit, what are these things?" He asked.

The rabbit smiled and said, "Oh, these are called seeds!"

Jack was surprised. He had never seen seeds before! He thanked the rabbit and flew away, his heart filled with wonder!

The elephant did not like the bear's tone and became angry. "I'm the boss!" the elephant yelled.

The bear didn't want to fight and ended up crying. But then the mouse had an idea. She pointed to the long cord they had been using to play a game. "Let's tie one end to the elephant and the other end to the bear," the mouse said. "Now, the elephant can pull the bear, but the bear can also pull the elephant. You can still be the boss, but the bear can decide when to follow and when to lead."

Everyone liked this idea and started to smile. The elephant was still bossy, but now the bear could help lead too--and they were all happy!

Later, the pig saw the bird again. The bird had found food and was now happy. The pig thought about how he had not shared his food. He felt bad. The next time a friend asked for help, the pig decided to share. He learned that sharing with others is important and makes everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a pond. In the pond, there were many fish. The fish were pale. A little boy named Tim liked to watch the fish. He would go to the pond every day.

One day, Tim went to the pond. He wanted to watch the fish. He saw a big, pale fish. Tim was very happy. He wanted to get closer to the fish. So, he went near the water.

But Tim was not careful. He fell into the pond. The water was deep. Tim could not swim. He was very scared. The pale fish swam away. Tim tried to call for help, but no one was there to hear him.

In the end, Tim did not get out of the pond. The pale fish kept swimming, and the pond was quiet again.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little tree. The little tree was eager to grow big and strong like the other trees. It wanted to have big roots and tall branches to touch the sky.

One day, a small bug came to live on the little tree. The bug liked to squeeze the tree's leaves. The little tree did not like this. It wanted the bug to go away, but the bug stayed. The little tree was sad.

A wise, old tree saw the little tree's sadness. The old tree told the little tree that the bug was helping it. The bug made the little tree's roots grow stronger by squeezing its leaves. The little tree learned to be kind to the bug, and they both lived happily in the forest. The moral of the story is that sometimes things that seem bad can actually be good for us.

The bee flew to the man's mustache. It tried to eat the sweet candy. But the mustache was not candy. The bee got mad. It stung the man on his nose. The man cried and went home. He was sad that he did not quit eating sweet candy.

Remy and Benny went into the tunnel together. They walked slowly and carefully. It was very dark. Remy felt a little less worried because Benny was with him. But then, they saw a big, scary monster! From that day on, Remy and Benny never went into the tunnel again. They knew that some things were just too scary to face, even with a friend by their side. And they learned that it was okay to be afraid, but it was also important to be careful and stay safe.

The rat ran to the cheese. But, it did not see a big rock. The rat did not look where it was going. It did not see the rock. The rat stumbled on the rock and fell down. It hurt, but the rat was okay. The rat got up and ran to the cheese. It ate the cheese and was happy again.

A little bird saw Lily clapping and flew down to see her. The bird was curious about her diary. Lily showed the bird her drawings and they became friends. They spent the whole day playing and clapping together in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big red coat. The coat was in a room with a small cat. The cat liked to play with the coat. One day, the cat saw the coat lie on the floor. The cat thought it would be fun to jump on the coat.

The cat jumped on the coat and it made a loud noise. The noise was so loud that it woke up a big dog. The dog was in the next room. The dog was dangerous and did not like the cat. The dog ran into the room to see what made the noise.

The cat was scared of the dog. The cat knew the dog was dangerous. The cat had to find a way to be safe. The cat jumped on the coat again and the coat moved. The coat moved and covered the cat. The dog could not see the cat. The cat was safe under the coat. The dog went away and the cat was happy.

Tim saw a little girl named Lily. She was sad because her shoe was broken. The buckle on her shoe had come off. Tim wanted to help her. He said, "I can fix your buckle, Lily. Then we can play together and it will be fair."

Lily smiled and thanked Tim. Tim fixed the buckle on her shoe. Now, they could both play and have fun. They went on the slide and the swing. They did not want to leave the park.

As the sun went down, Tim and Lily knew it was time to go home. They said goodbye and left the park. They were happy that they had a fair and fun day together.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the farm. They had many animals and plants to see and touch. One day, they saw a big orange pumpkin in the field. They wanted to take it home and make a pie.

"Let's hurry and get the pumpkin before Mom sees us," Tim said. He was the older brother and he liked to do things his way.

"OK, but how will we carry it? It is too big and heavy for us," Sam said. He was the younger brother and he liked to follow Tim.

"We can use this old cart. It has wheels and a rope. We can pull it together," Tim said. He found an old cart behind the barn and put the pumpkin on it.

They started to pull the cart, but it was hard work. The pumpkin was very big and the cart was very old. The wheels were rusty and the rope was thin. The cart made a lot of noise and left a lot of marks on the ground.

Mom heard the noise and saw the marks. She followed them and found them in the field. She was not happy.

"Tim and Sam, what are you doing with that pumpkin? That is not yours to take. That is for the farmer who grows them. He works very hard to grow them and sell them. You are stealing from him and hurting his business. That is very wrong and very bad," Mom said.

Tim and Sam felt very sorry and very ashamed. They did not think about the farmer or his work. They only thought about themselves and their pie.

"Mom, we are sorry. We did not know. We were just playing. We will put the pumpkin back and say sorry to the farmer," Tim said.

"Yes, Mom, we are sorry. We will not do it again. We will be good and honest," Sam said.

Mom hugged them and said, "I forgive you, but you have to learn from your mistake. You have to respect other people's things and work. You have to ask before you take or use something that is not yours. You have to be kind and fair to everyone. That is the right and good thing to do."

They put the pumpkin back on the field and went to the farmer's house. They knocked on the door and said sorry to the farmer. The farmer was surprised and angry at first, but he saw that they were sincere and regretful. He accepted their apology and thanked them for returning the pumpkin. He even gave them a small pumpkin to take home and make a pie.

Tim and Sam learned their lesson. They never stole or lied again. They always asked and thanked. They always helped and shared. They grew up to be good and honest men. They were happy and proud of themselves. And they always loved pumpkin pie.

"A baby sister is a girl who will join our family," mom says. "She will be very small and need a lot of care. She will sleep in a crib and drink milk from a bottle. She will cry and laugh and learn new things."

"Will she play with us?" Ben asks.

"Of course, she will," dad says. "But not right away. She will need some time to grow and get stronger. You will have to be gentle and patient with her. You will be her big brother and sister. You will help her and teach her and love her."

Anna and Ben think about it. They are not sure how they feel. They like being twins. They like having mom and dad to themselves. They do not want to share their toys and their dog. They do not want to hear a baby cry. They do not want to be gentle and patient.

But they also want to see their baby sister. They want to know what she looks like. They want to hear her laugh. They want to learn new things with her. They want to help her and teach her and love her.

They look at mom and dad. They see their smiles. They feel their hugs. They hear their words. They are a regular family. They accept their baby sister. They are happy.

One day, they saw a new animal on the ranch. It was big and brown and had long horns. It looked different from the other cows. Ben and Lily were curious and wanted to see it.

They asked their dad, who worked on the ranch, what it was. He said it was a bison, an original animal that lived on the land before the ranch was there. He said the bison was a friend of the ranch and they should be nice to it.

Ben and Lily decided to include the bison in their play. They brought some hay and apples for it to eat. They talked to it and stroked its fur. They named it Bob and made it a crown of flowers.

The bison liked Ben and Lily and their gifts. It snorted and nodded and followed them around. Ben and Lily were happy to have a new friend on the ranch. They said they would visit Bob every day and learn more about him.

Lily hears Tom cry. She rushes to him. She hugs him. She tries to make him feel better.

"Are you okay, Tom?" she asks.

"No, I am not. The boy is mean. He hit me with the ball," Tom says.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play on the farm. They loved to see the animals, especially the sheep. The sheep were soft and white and made funny noises. Tom and Sue liked to feed them grass and pet them.

One day, they saw a big truck come to the farm. The truck had a sign that said "Sheep Farm". The driver got out and talked to the farmer. He said he wanted to buy some sheep. The farmer nodded and showed him the sheep pen. Tom and Sue were curious and followed them.

The driver looked at the sheep and pointed at one. He said, "I'll take that one. It looks easy to catch." The sheep he pointed at was the smallest and shyest of the flock. It was Tom and Sue's favorite sheep. They had named it Fluffy. They did not want the driver to take Fluffy away.

They ran to the pen and shouted, "No, you can't have Fluffy! He's our friend!" The driver looked at them and laughed. He said, "Too bad, kids. I paid the farmer for this sheep. He's mine now." He grabbed Fluffy by the wool and lifted him up. Fluffy bleated and struggled.

Tom and Sue were angry and sad. They had to rescue Fluffy. They had an idea. They saw a pile of hay near the pen. They ran to the hay and threw some at the driver. The hay got in his eyes and mouth and made him cough and drop Fluffy. Fluffy ran back to the pen and hid behind the other sheep. Tom and Sue followed him and hugged him. They said, "Don't worry, Fluffy. We won't let anyone take you."

The driver was mad and tried to get Fluffy again. But the farmer came and stopped him. He said, "Sorry, sir. I changed my mind. I can't sell you this sheep. He's too special. He belongs to these kids. They love him." The driver grumbled and got back in his truck. He drove away.

Tom and Sue were happy and thanked the farmer. The farmer smiled and said, "You're welcome, kids. You're very brave and clever. You saved Fluffy. He's lucky to have you as his friends." Tom and Sue and Fluffy lived happily ever after on the farm.

Lily liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She liked to stir the soup, cut the bread, and taste the cheese. But her favorite thing was to look inside the freezer. The freezer was a big box that was very cold. It had ice cream, popsicles, and frozen peas. Lily wanted to try them all.

One day, Lily saw a new thing in the freezer. It was a shiny bag with a picture of a fish. Lily loved fish. She asked her mom, "Can I have the fish, please?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily, that fish is not for you. That fish is very special. It is for your grandpa. He is coming to visit us tomorrow. He is deaf, so he cannot hear us. But he can talk with his hands. And he loves fish. He gave me this fish as a gift. He said it is very rare and valuable. We have to keep it in the freezer until we cook it for him."

Lily nodded, but she was still curious. She wanted to see the fish. She wanted to touch it. She wanted to smell it. She thought, maybe I can just peek at it. Maybe I can just open the bag a little bit. Maybe I can just take a tiny bite.

When her mom was busy, Lily sneaked to the freezer. She opened the door and reached for the shiny bag. She pulled it out and tore it open. She saw the fish. It was big and silver and had a long tail. It looked yummy. Lily took a bite. It was cold and hard and salty. She did not like it. She spit it out. She tried to put the fish back in the bag, but it was too late. The fish was ruined. Lily felt bad. She heard her mom coming. She hid the fish behind the ice cream.

Her mom opened the freezer and saw the mess. She saw the torn bag, the bitten fish, and the ice cream. She was angry. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You ruined the fish! You wasted the gift! You hurt your grandpa's feelings! How could you?"

Lily was scared. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to try the fish. I didn't know it was so valuable. I didn't mean to be bad."

Her mom sighed. She said, "Lily, you have to learn to respect other people's things. You have to listen to what I say. You have to understand that some things are not for you. You have to value what you have, not what you want. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you. I love grandpa. Can I say sorry to him?"

Her mom hugged her. She said, "Yes, Lily. You can say sorry to him. But you have to use your hands, not your mouth. He cannot hear you, remember?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Okay, mom. I will use my hands. I will learn how to say sorry with my hands. I will make him happy. I will give him a hug. I will give him a kiss. I will give him a popsicle. Maybe he will like that better than the fish."

But then, he hears a loud noise. He turns around and sees a big cat. The cat is angry and hisses at Mark. The cat does not like Mark's smell on the hedge. The cat thinks the hedge is hers.

Mark is scared and runs away. He drops his ball and his stick. He looks for his owner. He finds his owner on a bench. He jumps on his owner and licks his face. His owner hugs him and says, "Good boy, Mark. You are safe now."

Mark feels warm and loved. He forgets about the hedge and the cat. He only cares about his owner. He thinks his owner is the best.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dolls. They liked to pretend that their dolls were friends and had adventures together. Lily had a pink doll with a dress and a hat. Ben had a green doll with a helmet and a gun. He said his doll was a soldier.

"Hi, I'm Lily. This is my doll, Rosie. She likes to sing and dance. What is your doll's name?" Lily asked Ben.

"Hi, I'm Ben. This is my doll, Max. He is a soldier. He likes to fight and protect. He is very fierce," Ben said.

"Wow, he is fierce. Does he have any friends?" Lily asked.

"Yes, he has many friends. They are also soldiers. They work together to stop the bad guys. Do you want to see them?" Ben asked.

"Sure, I want to see them. Can Rosie play with them too?" Lily asked.

"OK, but she has to be careful. They are not like her. They are rough and tough. Come on, I will introduce you to them," Ben said.

He took Lily and Rosie to his backpack, where he had more green dolls with helmets and guns. He showed them to Lily and Rosie and told them their names. Lily and Rosie looked at them with curiosity and fear. They were very different from their dolls.

"Hello, I'm Rosie. I'm a singer and a dancer. I like to have fun and make friends. Who are you?" Rosie said to one of the green dolls.

"I'm Rex. I'm a soldier. I like to shoot and explode. I don't have fun. I have missions. Who are you?" Rex said to Rosie.

Rosie felt scared. She did not like Rex. He was too fierce for her. She wanted to go back to Lily and play with her.

"Ben, can we go back to the swings? I don't like these dolls. They are too fierce for me. I like Rosie better. She is nice and gentle," Lily said to Ben.

"OK, Lily. We can go back to the swings. I like Max better too. He is brave and strong. He is my best friend," Ben said to Lily.

They left the backpack and went back to the swings. They played with their dolls and talked to each other. They were different, but they liked each other. They became friends.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play together at school. One day, they have math class. Math is hard, but fun. They learn to count and add.

The teacher gives them a math problem. She says, "What is two plus two?" Tom and Mia think hard. They use their fingers to help them. Tom says, "Two plus two is four!" Mia says, "No, two plus two is five!" They look at each other and laugh. They think they are funny.

The teacher smiles. She says, "Tom is right. Two plus two is four. Mia, you are close. You just need to take away one finger. Can you try again?" Mia nods. She takes away one finger and says, "Two plus two is four!" The teacher says, "Good job, Mia! You are smart. You both are."

Tom and Mia are happy. They give each other a high five. They say, "Math is nice. We like math. And we like each other." They laugh some more and hug. They are good friends.

Anna likes toast for breakfast. She likes it with butter and jam. She puts bread in the toaster and waits for it to pop. She is very hungry.

But then she hears her mom call her. She has to go to the bathroom. She runs to the bathroom and does her business. She washes her hands and dries them. She is very proud.

But she forgets about the toast. She does not go back to the kitchen. She goes to her room and plays with her dolls. She has a lot of fun.

The toast gets cold and hard. It is not yummy anymore. It is different. It is bad.

Mom comes to the kitchen and sees the toast. She is not happy. She calls Anna and asks her why she did not eat her toast. Anna remembers the toast. She feels sorry. She says she is sorry.

Mom is not angry. She is kind. She makes new toast for Anna. She gives it to her with a hug and a kiss. Anna says thank you. She eats the toast. It is warm and soft. It is yummy. She is happy.

Ben and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big swing. They want to try it.

"Can we go on the swing, please?" Mia asks Ben.

"OK, but I go first," Ben says. He runs to the swing and sits on it. He pushes with his feet and goes higher and higher.

Mia waits for her turn. She watches Ben swing. She hears him sing a song. He sings, "I am the king of the swing, I can do anything!"

Mia claps her hands. She likes his song. She wants to sing too.

"Ben, let me go on the swing now," Mia says.

"OK, OK, but you have to weigh me first," Ben says. He stops the swing and jumps off. He stands on a big rock. He points to a small rock. He says, "You stand on that rock and tell me how much I weigh."

Mia does what he says. She stands on the small rock. She looks at Ben. She thinks for a moment. She says, "You weigh... ten apples!"

Ben laughs. He says, "No, I weigh more than that. I weigh... twenty bananas!"

Mia laughs too. She says, "No, you weigh less than that. You weigh... fifteen oranges!"

Ben and Mia keep guessing each other's weight. They have fun. They forget about the swing.

Then they hear a voice. It is their mom. She says, "Time to go home, kids. Did you have a good time?"

Ben and Mia run to their mom. They hug her. They say, "Yes, we had a good time. We played on the swing and we sang a song and we weighed each other. But now we are dizzy!"

Their mom smiles. She says, "That sounds like a lot of fun. But don't worry, you will feel better soon. Let's go home and have some juice and cookies."

Ben and Mia nod. They hold their mom's hand. They walk home. They are happy.

Lila and Ben were playing by the pond. They liked to look at the fish and the ducks. They also liked to throw pebbles into the water and watch the ripples.

"Look, Ben, I found a big pebble!" Lila said, holding up a smooth, round stone. "I bet it will make a big splash!"

"Let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the pebble. He wanted to throw it too.

But Lila did not want to share. She pulled the pebble away from Ben and said, "No, it's mine! I found it first!"

Ben felt sad and angry. He wanted to play with Lila, but she was being mean. He looked around and saw another pebble on the ground. He picked it up and said, "Fine, I have my own pebble. And it's bigger than yours!"

He threw the pebble as hard as he could into the pond. It made a loud splash and scared the fish and the ducks. Lila was surprised and a little scared too. She dropped her pebble and said, "Ben, why did you do that? You scared the animals!"

Ben did not answer. He felt sorry for the animals, but he also felt proud of his big splash. He did not know what to say to Lila.

Lila looked at the pebble she dropped. It was still shiny and smooth. She felt sorry for Ben, but she also felt proud of her pebble. She did not know what to say to Ben.

They both sat quietly by the pond, feeling mixed up. They wanted to be friends, but they also wanted to have their own things. They did not know how to share.

Then, a duck came over to them. It quacked and waddled around, looking for food. It saw the pebbles and thought they were bread. It picked up Lila's pebble and tried to eat it. But it was too hard and it hurt its beak. It spat out the pebble and quacked again, looking unhappy.

Lila and Ben saw the duck and felt sorry for it. They realized that their pebbles were not food for the duck. They also realized that their pebbles were not worth fighting over. They looked at each other and smiled.

"Sorry, Lila, I was mean to you," Ben said. "You can have your pebble back. It is very pretty."

"Sorry, Ben, I was mean to you too," Lila said. "You can have your pebble back. It made a big splash."

They gave each other their pebbles and hugged. They decided to share their pebbles and play together. They also decided to give some bread to the duck, to make it happy. The duck quacked and ate the bread, feeling better.

Lila and Ben were thoughtful. They learned to share and to care for the animals. They had fun by the pond. They were friends.

Jen and Sam were friends who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big melon on a table. It was green and round and looked yummy.

"Let's eat the melon!" Jen said.

"But it's not ours," Sam said. "It belongs to someone else."

Jen did not care. She was independent and did what she wanted. She took a knife and cut the melon in half. She gave one half to Sam and kept the other for herself.

"Come on, Sam, it's good!" Jen said.

Sam was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. He quit playing with Jen and ran away.

"Sam, wait!" Jen called. But Sam did not look back.

Jen was sad. She ate the melon by herself, but it did not taste good. It was sour and bitter. She felt sick and sorry.

Soon, a man came to the table. He was angry. He saw the melon and the knife and Jen.

"Who did this?" he shouted. "Who stole my melon?"

Jen was afraid. She wished Sam was with her. She wished she did not eat the melon. She wished she was not so independent.

Lily loved her pony, Brownie. She liked to brush his hair, feed him carrots, and ride him around the farm. She always held his reins gently and talked to him softly. Brownie was her best friend.

One day, a new girl came to the farm. Her name was Anna, and she had a big smile and a pink dress. She said she wanted to ride Brownie, too. Lily did not like that. She felt jealous. She did not want to share her pony with anyone.

"Please, Lily, can I ride Brownie for a little while?" Anna asked. "He looks so nice and friendly. I have never ridden a pony before."

Lily shook her head. "No, you can't. Brownie is my pony. He only likes me. You can't hold his reins or touch his hair. Go away!"

Anna looked sad. She did not understand why Lily was so mean. She liked ponies, and she wanted to be friends with Lily. She walked away slowly, and looked for something else to do.

Brownie saw what happened. He felt sorry for Anna. He knew she was not bad, and he wanted to make her happy. He also did not like how Lily was acting. She was being selfish and rude. He decided to teach her a lesson.

He waited until Lily was not looking, and then he trotted over to Anna. He nudged her with his nose, and made a soft noise. Anna turned around, and saw Brownie. She smiled, and reached out to pet him. Brownie liked that. He let her hold his reins, and walked with her around the farm.

Lily saw them, and felt angry. She ran after them, and shouted. "Hey, that's my pony! Give him back! He doesn't like you!"

But Brownie did not listen. He ignored Lily, and kept walking with Anna. He showed her the flowers, the chickens, and the pond. He made her laugh, and feel happy.

Lily realized she had made a mistake. She had been mean to Anna, and to Brownie. She had hurt their feelings, and lost their trust. She felt sorry, and ashamed. She wanted to say sorry, and make up with them.

She ran up to them, and said. "Anna, Brownie, I'm sorry. I was wrong. I was jealous, and selfish. I should have shared my pony with you, and been nice to you. Can you forgive me? Can we be friends?"

Anna and Brownie looked at her. They saw she was sincere, and felt sorry for her, too. They nodded, and smiled. They forgave her, and welcomed her. They let her join them, and walk with them. They shared the pony, and the farm. They became friends.

Tom liked the idea. He said, "Yes, let's do that!" They took a big sheet from the closet and put it over their bed. They crawled under the sheet and pretended they were camping.

"Can we be friends with the ants, Anna?" he asks.

Anna and Ben watch as some ants come and take the crumb. They feel happy and reliable. They are friends with the ants.

Lily liked to whistle. She whistled when she played, when she ate, and when she slept. She whistled so much that her mom and dad sometimes asked her to be quiet.

One day, Lily found a shiny spoon in the kitchen. She thought it was a good thing to whistle with. She put the spoon in her mouth and blew hard. But the spoon did not make a nice sound. It made a loud and ugly noise.

Lily's mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily with the spoon in her mouth and said, "Lily, what are you doing? That is not a toy. That is a spoon. You use it to eat, not to whistle. You could hurt your teeth or your tongue with the spoon. And you are making a lot of noise. Please put the spoon back where it belongs and play with something else."

Lily felt sad. She did not mean to make her mom angry. She just wanted to whistle. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I like to whistle. It makes me happy. Can I whistle with something else?"

Lily's mom was thoughtful. She knew that Lily loved to whistle, but she also wanted her to be safe and respectful. She said, "I understand, Lily. Whistling is fun, but you have to be careful and polite. You can whistle with your lips, or with a whistle, or with a flute. But not with a spoon, or a fork, or a knife. Those are not for whistling. They are for eating. And you have to whistle softly, not loudly, when other people are around. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will whistle with my lips, or with a whistle, or with a flute. And I will whistle softly, not loudly, when other people are around. Thank you, mom. You are very kind."

Lily's mom smiled. She said, "You are welcome, Lily. You are very thoughtful. I love you."

Lily hugged her mom. She said, "I love you too, mom. And I love to whistle."

The end.

Lily loved to read books. She had many books in her room. She liked to read about animals, princesses, and pirates. She read every night before bed.

One day, Lily saw a new book on the shelf. It was a big book with a red cover. It had a picture of a dragon on it. Lily wanted to read it. She took the book and opened it.

But the book was not a story book. It was a book of matches. Lily did not know what matches were. She thought they were sticks with colors on them. She saw a picture of a match with a flame on it. She thought it looked pretty.

Lily was curious. She wanted to make a flame like the picture. She took a match and rubbed it on the book. The match made a spark and a fire. Lily was scared. She dropped the match on the floor. The floor had a carpet. The carpet caught fire.

"Help! Help!" Lily cried. She ran out of the room.

Her mom heard her cry. She smelled smoke. She ran to Lily's room. She saw the fire on the floor. She grabbed a bucket of water and poured it on the fire. She put out the fire.

She was angry and worried. She looked at Lily. She saw the book of matches in her hand.

"Lily, what did you do?" she asked. "Did you play with matches?"

Lily nodded. She was sorry. She did not mean to start a fire.

"Playing with matches is very naughty and dangerous," her mom said. "You could have burned the house or hurt yourself. Matches are not toys. You should never touch them."

Lily felt bad. She hugged her mom and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I won't play with matches again. I just wanted to read the book."

Her mom hugged her back and said, "I'm glad you're okay, Lily. But this is not a book. This is a book of matches. It is for grown-ups only. You should only read books that are for children. They have stories and pictures that you can enjoy. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She understood. She gave the book of matches to her mom. She asked her mom to read her a real book. Her mom agreed. She picked a book from the shelf. It was a book about a friendly dragon. Lily liked it. She listened to her mom and learned new words. She was happy. She decided to never play with matches again. She only wanted to read books.

Tim and Sue did not listen to their mom. They waited until she went to the kitchen and then they took the magazine. They opened it and saw many things they liked. They pointed and laughed and said the names of the things. They did not see that their mom came back and saw them.

Their mom was very angry. She took the magazine from them and said they were naughty. She said they forgot to obey her and they ruined the magazine. She showed them that some pages were torn and some had crayon marks. She said they had to go to their room and stay there until dinner. She said they could not play with their toys or watch TV.

Tim and Sue felt very sad and sorry. They cried and said they were sorry. They said they did not mean to forget or ruin the magazine. They said they just wanted to see the things. But their mom did not listen. She said they had to learn their lesson and be good.

Tim and Sue went to their room and felt helpless. They wished they had listened to their mom and left the magazine alone. They learned that it was wrong to take things that did not belong to them and to disobey their mom. They hoped their mom would forgive them and love them again. They decided to be better twins from now on.

The end.

Moral: Listen to your mom and do not take things that do not belong to you.

Lily was sick. She had a hot head and a sore throat. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to lie in bed and cuddle her teddy bear.

Mama came to check on her. She put a thermometer in Lily's mouth and waited. The thermometer beeped and Mama looked at it. She frowned and said, "Oh, Lily, you have a fever. You need to drink some water and take some medicine."

Lily shook her head. She did not like water or medicine. They tasted bad and made her feel uncomfortable. She spit out the thermometer and said, "No, Mama, no water, no medicine. I want juice and cookies."

Mama sighed and said, "I know, Lily, but juice and cookies won't make you better. Water and medicine will. Please, Lily, be a good girl and do what Mama says."

Lily pouted and said, "No, Mama, no good girl. I want juice and cookies."

Mama tried to be patient and said, "Lily, if you don't drink water and take medicine, you will feel worse. You might even have to go to the hospital. Do you want that?"

Lily did not want to go to the hospital. She was scared of the hospital. She had been there once when she fell and hurt her knee. There were many people and machines and noises. She did not like it at all.

Lily looked at Mama and saw that she was worried and sad. She did not want to make Mama worried and sad. She loved Mama. She said, "Okay, Mama, I will drink water and take medicine. But can I have juice and cookies later?"

Mama smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you can have juice and cookies later, when you feel better. Thank you, Lily, for being a brave girl. I love you."

Mama gave Lily a glass of water and a spoon of medicine. Lily drank the water and swallowed the medicine. They were not as bad as she thought. She felt a little better. Mama gave her a hug and a kiss and said, "Good girl, Lily. Now, try to sleep and rest. I will be here with you."

Lily closed her eyes and snuggled with her teddy bear. She felt Mama's hand on her forehead. She felt warm and safe. She said, "I love you, Mama."

Mama said, "I love you, too, Lily."

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big puddle near the church. They ran to the puddle and jumped in it. They splashed and laughed and got very wet.

"Look, Sara, I can make a big wave!" Ben said. He kicked the water hard and sent it flying.

"Wow, Ben, that's fun!" Sara said. She kicked the water too and made another wave.

But they did not see that the water went over the fence and into the church yard. The water soaked the flowers and the grass and the path. It also soaked the shoes and the socks of a man who was walking to the church. He was the pastor and he was not happy.

"Hey, you two, what are you doing?" he shouted. He came to the fence and looked at Sara and Ben. They stopped jumping and looked at him. They saw his wet shoes and socks and his angry face. They felt scared and sorry.

"We're sorry, sir, we didn't mean to soak you and the church," Sara said.

"We were just playing in the puddle, we didn't see the water go over the fence," Ben said.

The pastor sighed and shook his head. He saw that Sara and Ben were wet and cold and sad. He remembered that he was once a child who liked to play in puddles too. He decided to be kind and not angry.

"It's okay, Sara and Ben, I forgive you. But next time, be careful where you splash the water. And come, let me take you to the church. You can dry off and warm up and have some cookies. How does that sound?" he said.

Sara and Ben smiled and nodded. They followed the pastor to the church. They were glad that he was kind and not angry. They learned to be more careful and respectful. They also made a new friend.

He went to his truck and brought back a ladder and a hook. He climbed the ladder and reached for the loop. He hooked it with the hook and pulled it down. He handed it to Sam and Mia. They were very happy. They thanked the park ranger and hugged him.

"You're welcome, kids," the park ranger said. "But be careful with that loop. It's not a toy. It's a kite. It's meant to fly in the sky, not in the trees. If you want to play with it, you need to find a big open space and a windy day. And always hold on to the string, or you might lose it again."

Sam and Mia nodded. They learned something new. They decided to save their loop for a special day. They said goodbye to the park ranger and went home with their loops. They still liked to play with their other loops, but they also looked forward to flying their kite. They hoped for a big open space and a windy day.

"Let's make a cake!" Sara said. "We need to gather all the ingredients and mix them well."

"OK!" Ben said. "I will get the flour and the eggs. You get the milk and the sugar."

They gathered all the ingredients and put them in the bowl. Sara used the teaspoon to scoop some sugar and add it to the bowl. She did it four times.

"Is that enough sugar?" Ben asked.

"I think so," Sara said. "Now we need to stir everything with a big spoon."

They took turns stirring the bowl with a big spoon. The mixture became smooth and creamy.

"Wow, it looks good!" Ben said. "Can we taste it?"

"Sure!" Sara said. "But only a little bit. We need to save some for the cake."

They each took a small bite of the mixture with the teaspoon. It was sweet and delicious.

"Mmm, this is the best cake ever!" Sara said.

"Hi, kids!" Mom said. "What are you doing in the kitchen?"

"We are making a cake!" Sara said.

"A cake?" Mom said. "With what?"

"Oh, I see," Mom said. "That's very nice of you, but you know you should not use the kitchen without asking me first. And you should not eat raw eggs. They can make you sick."

"We are sorry, Mom," Ben said.

They sit at the table and look at their books. They see letters and numbers and colors. They have to write and draw and count. They think it is hard and boring. They whisper to each other.

"Let's cut our homework," Tom says.

"OK, let's cut our homework," Lily says.

They take their scissors and cut their books. They cut the letters and numbers and colors. They cut the pages and the covers. They make a big mess. They laugh and giggle.

But Lily's mom hears them. She comes to the table and sees the cut books. She is angry. She says they are naughty and wasteful. She says they have to clean up and buy new books. She says they can't play with paper and scissors anymore. Tom and Lily are sorry. They cry and say they are sorry. They wish they didn't cut their homework. They wish they did their homework. They learn their lesson.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. They look at the sky and see many clouds. Some clouds are big and white. Some clouds are small and gray.

"Look, Anna, that cloud looks like a dog!" Ben says. He points at a cloud with a long tail and ears.

Anna smiles. She sees another cloud. "And that cloud looks like a sign!" she says. She points at a cloud with a square shape and a line in the middle.

"What does the sign say?" Ben asks. He tries to read the cloud.

Anna thinks. She knows some letters, but not all. She makes up a word. "The sign says, 'Be kind'," she says.

"Be kind? What does that mean?" Ben asks.

Anna remembers what her mom told her. "It means to be nice to others. To share and help and say sorry," she says.

Ben nods. He likes to be kind. He thinks of something. He gives Anna a hug. "You are my kind friend," he says.

Anna hugs him back. "You are my kind friend, too," she says.

They look at the sky again. The clouds change shape. They see a heart, a star, and a flower. They smile and hold hands. They are happy and kind.

Tom is a big boy who goes to school. He wears a uniform with a blue shirt and a red tie. He likes to learn new things and make friends. But there is a boy in his class who is not nice. His name is Sam.

Sam does not wear a uniform. He wears a green hat and a yellow coat. He does not listen to the teacher or the other children. He thinks he knows everything. He is ignorant.

One day, Tom and Sam have to work together on a project. They have to speak to each other and share their ideas. But Sam does not want to speak to Tom. He says, "You are stupid. You wear a silly uniform. You do not know anything. I do not need you."

Tom feels sad and angry. He says, "You are rude. You wear a funny hat and coat. You do not know how to be kind. I do not like you."

The teacher hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She says, "Boys, why are you fighting? You have to work together and respect each other. You have to speak nicely and listen to each other. You have to learn from each other. You are both smart and special."

Tom and Sam look at each other. They feel ashamed. They say, "We are sorry, teacher. We are sorry, Tom. We are sorry, Sam. We will try to be friends. We will try to speak and learn together."

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they have a picnic. They bring a basket with food and a blanket to sit on.

They find a nice spot under a big tree. They put the blanket on the grass and open the basket. They have sandwiches, apples, cookies and juice. They are happy and hungry.

But then, they see a big bear. The bear is walking towards them. It looks angry and hungry too. Tom and Mia are scared. They grab the basket and run away.

But the bear does not chase them. It stops at the blanket and sniffs the food. It picks up a sandwich and bites it. But it does not like it. It spits it out. It picks up an apple and bites it. But it does not like it either. It spits it out too. It picks up a cookie and bites it. But it does not like it at all. It spits it out and roars.

Tom and Mia are hiding behind a bush. They peek at the bear. They see something shiny on its neck. It is a collar. They see something on its ear. It is a tag. They read the tag. It says: "Name: Bob. Fake bear. Do not feed."

Tom and Mia laugh. They realize the bear is not real. It is a toy. Someone left it in the park. They are not scared anymore. They go back to the blanket and share their food with Bob. They have a fun picnic with their new friend.

Lily liked to balance on the wall. She walked on it like a cat, with her arms out. She felt happy and brave. But Tom did not like it. He was scared of falling. He wore a uniform for school. It was blue and white. He wanted Lily to get down.

"Stop it, Lily!" he said. "You will fall and hurt yourself. And you will make your dress dirty. Come down now!"

Lily did not listen. She smiled and said, "No, Tom. I like it here. It is fun. You are a chicken. Bawk, bawk, bawk!"

Tom was angry. He did not like being called a chicken. He threw a stone at Lily. It hit her leg. It hurt. Lily lost her balance. She fell off the wall. She landed on the grass. She cried.

Tom felt sorry. He ran to Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. Are you okay?"

Lily was not okay. She had a cut on her leg. It bled. She was scared. She said, "Tom, you are mean. You made me fall. You hurt me. Go away!"

Tom did not go away. He stayed with Lily. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. Please forgive me. I will help you. I will get a band-aid. I will be your friend."

Lily looked at Tom. He looked sad. He looked thin. He looked lonely. She felt sorry for him. She said, "Okay, Tom. I forgive you. You can help me. You can be my friend. But don't throw stones again. And don't be scared of the wall. It is fun. Maybe you can try it someday."

Tom nodded. He said, "Okay, Lily. I won't throw stones again. And maybe I will try the wall someday. But not today. Today, I will help you. Come on, let's go to the nurse. She will make your leg better."

Lily and Tom held hands. They walked to the nurse. They were friends. They learned to balance.

Lily and Ben love blueberries. They are sweet and juicy and make their tongues blue. One day, they go to the market with Mom and see a big basket of blueberries. Mom says they are expensive, but she will buy some for them if they are good.

Lily and Ben are very happy. They hold Mom's hand and walk to the basket. They want to pick the biggest and best blueberries. But they are too small to reach the basket. They try to stand on their toes, but they still cannot reach.

Then, Ben has an idea. He sees a stool near the basket. He thinks he can climb on the stool and get the blueberries. He lets go of Mom's hand and runs to the stool. He does not see the sign that says "Do not touch".

Ben climbs on the stool and reaches for the blueberries. He grabs a handful and smiles. He wants to show Lily and Mom. But he does not balance well on the stool. He wobbles and loses his grip. He falls off the stool and drops the blueberries.

The blueberries fly in the air and land on the floor. Some of them burst and make a mess. Ben lands on his bottom and cries. Lily runs to him and hugs him. Mom runs to him and checks if he is hurt. She is not angry, but she is worried.

The market man comes and sees the stool and the blueberries. He is angry. He says the stool and the blueberries are expensive. He says Ben has to pay for them. Mom says she is sorry and gives him some money. She says Ben did not mean to do it. She says he learned his lesson.

Lily and Ben say they are sorry too. They say they will not touch things they are not supposed to. They say they will listen to Mom. The market man calms down and gives them some blueberries. He says they can have them as a gift. He says they are good kids.

Lily and Ben thank him and smile. They eat the blueberries and share them with Mom. They are sweet and juicy and make their tongues blue. They are happy. They learned a new word today: expensive.
