One day, Anna goes to the park with her mom. She brings her favorite magazine with her. It has a picture of a big elephant on the cover. She thinks the elephant is lovely. She wants to share her magazine with someone.

She sees a boy sitting on a bench. He has a red ball and a blue hat. He looks bored. Anna walks up to him and says hello. She smiles and holds out her magazine.

"Hi, I'm Anna. This is my magazine. It has an elephant. Do you like elephants?" she asks.

The boy looks at her and then at the magazine. He nods and smiles back.

"Hi, I'm Ben. I like elephants. They are big and strong. Can I see your magazine?" he says.

Anna nods and gives him her magazine. They sit on the bench and look at the pictures. They point at the animals and say their names. They introduce each other to their favorite animals. They have fun.

Anna and Ben become friends. They share their magazines and their toys. They play with the ball and the hat. They laugh and talk. They are happy.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys. One day, they find a medal in their dad's drawer. It is shiny and has a star on it.

"Wow, look at this medal!" Ben says. "It is so pretty and clean!"

"Can we play with it?" Lily asks.

"I don't know. Maybe dad will be mad if we take it," Ben says.

They hear a knock on the door. It is their friend Tom. He has a big bag of candy.

"Hi, Ben and Lily! Do you want some candy?" Tom says.

"Yes, please!" Ben and Lily say.

They run to the door and see the candy. Tom sees the medal in Ben's hand.

"Hey, what is that?" Tom says.

"It is a medal. It is shiny and has a star on it," Ben says.

"That is cool. Can I have it?" Tom says.

Ben thinks for a moment. He likes the medal, but he also likes candy.

"OK, you can have it. But you have to give me all your candy," Ben says.

"Deal!" Tom says.

He gives Ben the bag of candy and takes the medal. He puts it around his neck and smiles.

"Thank you, Ben! This is the best medal ever!" Tom says.

Ben and Lily open the bag of candy and start to eat. They are happy.

But then, they hear their dad coming upstairs. He is looking for his medal. It is a special medal that he got from the army. He is very proud of it.

"Ben, Lily, have you seen my medal?" he says.

Ben and Lily look at each other. They are scared. They ate all the candy. They gave away the medal. They don't know what to say.

Anna liked to go to the park with her mom. She liked to see the flowers, the swings, and the pigeons. She always brought some bread to feed the pigeons. She liked to watch them eat and fly.

One day, she saw a charming pigeon with a shiny ring on its leg. It was white and gray, and had a red spot on its head. Anna wanted to be friends with it. She threw some bread near the pigeon and said, "Hello, pigeon. Do you want to play with me?"

The pigeon looked at Anna and cooed. It walked closer to the bread and pecked at it. Anna smiled and threw more bread. She said, "You are a nice pigeon. What is your name?"

The pigeon cooed again and flapped its wings. It seemed to like Anna. It moved closer to her and rubbed its head on her hand. Anna giggled and stroked its feathers. She said, "I will call you Ruby, because you have a red spot. Do you like that name?"

The pigeon nodded and cooed. It liked the name Ruby. It liked Anna too. It felt happy and full. It decided to stay with Anna and be her friend. Anna was happy too. She had a new friend in the park. She hugged Ruby and said, "You are the best pigeon ever. I love you, Ruby."

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to pretend they were pirates and find treasure. Lily had a bow in her hair and Ben had a hat with a feather. They dug a hole and put some rocks and shells in it. Then they covered it with dirt and made a map.

"Let's go inside and get some juice," Lily said. "We can come back later and look for our treasure."

They ran to the house and opened the door. But they saw something scary. A big dog was in the living room. It had sharp teeth and a loud bark. It looked angry and hungry.

"Help!" Lily and Ben screamed. They tried to close the door, but the dog was too fast. It ran after them and bit Ben's leg. Ben fell down and cried. Lily was scared and ran to the kitchen. She saw a key on the counter. She grabbed it and locked the door behind her. She hoped the dog would not break it.

"Ben, are you okay?" Lily shouted through the door. She heard Ben's voice, but it was weak and sad.

"No, Lily, I'm not okay. The dog hurt me a lot. I'm bleeding and it hurts. Why did you lock the door? Why did you leave me alone?"

Lily felt ashamed. She wanted to help Ben, but she was too afraid of the dog. She did not know what to do. She wished their mom and dad were home. She wished they never played pirates. She wished they never opened the door. She wished the dog would go away. But the dog did not go away. It kept barking and biting. And Ben kept crying and bleeding. And Lily kept hiding and locking. One day, they saw a new boy in the garden next door. He was sitting on a swing and looked bored. Tim and Lily wanted to make a new friend, so they waved at him and said hello.

"Hello," the boy said. "What are you playing with?"

"This is Fluffy, our dragon," Tim said. "He is very nice and fun. Do you want to play with us?"

The boy frowned and shook his head. "No, I don't. Dragons are silly and fake. They don't exist. You are ignorant if you believe in dragons."

Tim and Lily felt sad and angry. They did not like the boy's words. They loved Fluffy and they knew he was real to them.

"Fluffy is not silly or fake. He is our friend. You are ignorant if you don't like dragons," Lily said.

"Whatever. I don't care. Go away and leave me alone," the boy said.

Tim and Lily turned away and hugged Fluffy. They decided to ignore the boy and keep playing with their dragon. They knew he was the ignorant one, not them. Fluffy smiled and winked at them. He was happy to have such good friends.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with their toys and pretend they are travelers. They have a big box that is their ship. They have a stick that is their staff. They have a scarf that is their flag.

One day, they want to travel to a new land. They put their toys and snacks in the box. They wave their flag and say, "Bye, Mom! Bye, Dad! We are going to travel!"

They push the box across the room. They make noises like a ship. They see a big sofa. They say, "Look! A mountain! Let's climb it!"

They pull the box to the sofa. They try to lift it up. But the box is too heavy. They cannot move it. They get angry. They say, "This is not fair! We want to travel!"

They start to push and pull the box. They start to yell and cry. They forget they are friends. They forget they are travelers.

Mom and Dad hear the noise. They come to the room. They see Anna and Ben fighting. They see the box and the staff and the flag. They say, "What is going on? Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben stop fighting. They look at Mom and Dad. They feel sad. They say, "We are sorry. We wanted to travel to a new land. But the box is too tight. We cannot climb the mountain."

Mom and Dad smile. They hug Anna and Ben. They say, "We understand. Traveling is fun. But sometimes it is hard. Sometimes you need to work together. Sometimes you need to be kind. Sometimes you need to use your imagination."

They help Anna and Ben to move the box. They make a ramp with a blanket. They say, "Now you can climb the mountain. But be careful. And have fun."

Anna and Ben smile. They thank Mom and Dad. They climb the ramp with the box. They wave their flag and say, "We did it! We are travelers!"

They play with their toys and pretend they are in a new land. They share their snacks and stories. They are friends again. They are happy.

At the zoo, Anna sees many animals. She sees lions, monkeys, elephants, and more. She likes them all. But her favorite animal is the zebra. She thinks the zebra is perfect. It has black and white stripes. It runs fast. It makes funny noises.

Anna wants to touch the zebra. She asks her mom and dad if she can. They say no. They say the zebra is not a pet. It is a wild animal. It can bite or kick. It can hurt Anna. Anna is sad. She does not understand.

She sees a fence around the zebra. She thinks the fence is not strong. She thinks she can climb over it. She waits for her mom and dad to look away. Then she runs to the fence. She tries to climb over it.

But the fence is not weak. It is electric. It gives Anna a shock. Anna screams. She falls to the ground. She cries. Her mom and dad hear her. They run to her. They hug her. They check if she is okay. They are scared and angry.

They take Anna to the nurse. The nurse gives Anna a band-aid. She tells Anna she is lucky. She could have been hurt worse. She tells Anna to never climb over fences at the zoo. She tells Anna to listen to her mom and dad. They know what is best for her.

Anna is sorry. She says she is sorry to her mom and dad. She says she is sorry to the zebra. She says she learned her lesson. She says she will never do it again. She says she still loves the zebra. Sara was a gifted lady who could make many tasty things. She liked to bake cakes and pies and cookies for her friends and family. She also liked to share her food with the animals in her garden. She would leave some crumbs and seeds for the birds and squirrels and rabbits.

One day, a big bear came to her garden. He smelled the food and wanted to taste it. He saw a pie on the window sill and reached for it with his paw. But Sara saw him and ran out of the house. She shouted at the bear, "No, no, no! That pie is not for you! That pie is for my grandma! Go away, bear, go away!"

The bear was angry and hungry. He growled at Sara and showed his teeth. He did not want to go away. He wanted the pie. He tried to push Sara away, but Sara was brave and strong. She picked up a stick and hit the bear on the nose. The bear felt pain and fear. He ran away from Sara and her garden.

Sara was happy and proud. She saved her pie and her garden. She put the pie in a basket and went to visit her grandma. She told her grandma what happened and gave her the pie. Her grandma hugged her and said, "You are a gifted lady, Sara. You can make tasty things and you can protect them. You are my sweet pie." Sara smiled and said, "I love you, grandma. You are my sweet pie, too." They ate the pie together and enjoyed it.

Nina and Leo were twins who loved to look at the stars and the moon. Every night, they would ask their mom to tell them stories about the sky. Their mom knew many stories, but their favorite one was about the ancient people who lived on the moon.

"One night, a long time ago, some brave people decided to fly to the moon in a big metal bird," their mom began. "They wanted to see what the moon was like, and if anyone lived there. They flew for many hours, until they reached the moon. They put on special suits and helmets, and stepped out of the metal bird."

"What did they see, mom?" Nina asked.

"They saw a lot of rocks and dust, and some big holes. They also saw the earth, shining like a blue ball in the sky. They walked around, and collected some rocks and dust to take back home. They were very happy and curious," their mom continued.

"Did they meet anyone?" Leo asked.

"Well, they did not see anyone at first, but then they heard a soft voice. It said, 'Welcome, welcome, welcome. We are happy to see you. We are the moon people.' They looked around, and saw some small, round, and shiny beings. They had eyes, but no mouths or noses. They talked with their minds. They were the ancient people who lived on the moon, and they had been waiting for visitors for a long time. They invited the brave people to their homes, which were inside the big holes. They showed them their treasures, and their secrets, and their stories. They became friends, and exchanged gifts. The brave people were amazed and grateful," their mom said.

"Wow, that's so cool, mom. I wish we could go to the moon and meet the moon people," Nina said.

"Me too, mom. Maybe someday we will," Leo said.

"Maybe, my loves. Maybe. But for now, let's say good night to the moon and the stars, and thank them for their light and their magic. They are always watching over us, and smiling at us. Good night, moon. Good night, stars. Good night, moon people. Good night, my twins," their mom said, and kissed them on their foreheads.

They snuggled in their beds, and closed their eyes. They dreamed of flying to the moon, and meeting the ancient people who lived there. They dreamed of being welcome, and being happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park with their dolls. They liked to pretend that their dolls were having a tea party under the big tree. They had a small basket with cups, plates and cookies that they shared with their dolls.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a big dog barking. They looked around and saw a big, black dog running towards them. The dog had a mean face and sharp teeth. It looked angry and hungry.

Lily and Ben were very scared. They grabbed their dolls and ran to the bench where their mom was sitting. They hid behind her and trembled. They hoped the dog would not see them or hurt them.

"Mom, mom, there is a big, bad dog!" Lily cried.

Mom got up and walked slowly to the dog. She spoke softly and kindly to him. She reached out her hand and touched his rag. The dog stopped barking and wagged his tail. He licked Mom's hand and looked at her with sad eyes. He was pale and thin. He was hungry and cold.

Mom took the rag off his neck and wrapped it around his body. She gave him a cookie from the basket and a sip of water from her bottle. She smiled at him and said, "You are a good boy. You are not a big, bad dog. You are a friend. Do you want to come with us?"

One night, she put on her blouse and got into bed. She hugged her teddy bear and said, "Good night, Mommy. Good night, Daddy. Good night, blouse."

Sara shook her head. She said, "No, I love my blouse. It is my favorite. I want to sleep in it. Please, let me."

Her mommy and daddy sighed. They did not want to argue with her. They said, "Okay, Sara. You can sleep in your blouse. But be careful with it. It is very pretty and special."

They turned off the light and left the room. Sara smiled and closed her eyes. She felt happy and cozy in her blouse.

The mouse climbed on the bed and nibbled on the blouse. It tore a hole in it. It made a mess. Sara did not hear or feel anything. She was sleeping deeply.

The next morning, Sara woke up and saw her blouse. She screamed. She saw the hole and the dirt and the mouse droppings. She cried. She said, "My blouse! My blouse! What happened to my blouse?"

Her mommy and daddy ran into the room. They saw the blouse and the mouse. They said, "Oh, no! Sara, we are so sorry. A mouse did this. It ruined your blouse. We should have made you wear your pajamas. We were wrong."

Sara sobbed. She said, "I hate the mouse. I hate the mouse. It took away my unique blouse. I will never find another one like it. I will never be happy again."

Tim and Liz are twins. They like to play outside with their toys. One day, they find a box of matches in the garage. They do not know what matches are for.

"Look, Liz, these are sticks with red heads. They are pretty," Tim says.

"Let me see, Tim. Maybe we can use them for our game," Liz says.

They take the matches to the backyard. They see a pile of dry leaves. Tim has an idea.

"Let's show Mom and Dad what we can do with the sticks. Maybe they will be happy," Tim says.

He takes a match and rubs it on the box. The match makes a spark and a flame. Tim is surprised and drops the match on the leaves. The leaves catch fire and make a lot of smoke.

"Wow, Tim, you made fire! Fire is hot and bright," Liz says.

She takes another match and lights it. She throws it on the fire. The fire grows bigger and louder.

"Look, Liz, we made a big fire! Mom and Dad will see it and come to us," Tim says.

But Mom and Dad are not happy. They smell the smoke and hear the fire. They run to the backyard and see Tim and Liz and the fire. They are scared and angry.

"Tim, Liz, what have you done? You could have burned the house and yourselves! Fire is dangerous, not a toy! You are very naughty and foolish!" Mom says.

She grabs a hose and sprays water on the fire. Dad takes Tim and Liz and carries them inside. He puts them in their room and locks the door.

"Tim, Liz, you are in big trouble. You will stay in your room until we say so. You will not play with matches ever again. You will say sorry and learn your lesson," Dad says.

Tim and Liz are miserable. They cry and hug each other. They are sorry for what they did. They wish they had not played with the matches. They wish they had not shown Mom and Dad the fire. They wish they had listened to Mom and Dad and played safely. They hope Mom and Dad will forgive them and love them.

Tom was sick and had to stay in bed. He did not like it. He wanted to play with his toys and his friends. His mom gave him some medicine to make him feel better. But the medicine was spicy and bitter. Tom did not want to drink it.

"Please, Tom, drink your medicine. It will help you get well soon," his mom said.

"No, mom, it is yucky. I do not like it. It makes my mouth burn," Tom said.

"Come on, Tom, it is not that bad. Look, I will drink some too. See, it is not yucky. It is yummy," his mom said. She pretended to drink some medicine from a different bottle. But it was not medicine. It was juice.

Tom saw his mom drink the juice. He thought she was joking. He laughed. He thought it was funny. He decided to drink his medicine too. He made a funny face and said, "Yummy, yummy, medicine. It is so good. Can I have some more?"

His mom smiled and hugged him. She was happy that he drank his medicine. She said, "You are a good boy, Tom. I am proud of you. And you have a good sense of humor. Joking can make you feel better too. But remember, do not joke about important things. Some things are not funny. They are serious."

Tom nodded. He understood. He said, "I know, mom. I will not joke about important things. But sometimes, joking can make me happy. And happy is good."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches that joking can be a way of coping with unpleasant situations, but also that there are limits to joking and some things are not appropriate to joke about. It also shows that listening to parents and taking medicine can help with recovery.

Sara and Ben were hungry. They wanted to eat dinner. Mom said they could choose what to eat. She had two pots on the stove. One pot had spaghetti. The other pot had rice.

"Spaghetti or rice?" Mom asked. "You can choose."

Sara looked at the pots. She liked spaghetti. She liked rice too. But she liked spaghetti more. She pointed at the pot with spaghetti.

"I choose spaghetti, please," Sara said.

Ben looked at the pots too. He did not like spaghetti. He did not like rice either. He wanted something else. He wanted pizza.

"I don't want spaghetti or rice," Ben said. "I want pizza."

Mom shook her head. She did not have pizza. She only had spaghetti and rice.

"Sorry, Ben. No pizza today. You have to choose spaghetti or rice. They are both good. And they are both regular. Not spicy or sweet or sour."

Ben frowned. He did not want to choose. He crossed his arms and pouted.

"I don't want to choose. I want pizza."

Mom sighed. She knew Ben was being stubborn. She decided to help him choose.

"Okay, Ben. How about this? You can have half spaghetti and half rice. That way, you can try both. And maybe you will like them. What do you say?"

Ben thought about it. He did not like the idea. But he was hungry. And he did not want to make Mom angry. He nodded slowly.

"Okay, Mom. I will try half spaghetti and half rice. But I still want pizza tomorrow."

Mom smiled. She was glad Ben agreed. She gave Sara and Ben a plate each. She put spaghetti on one side and rice on the other. She added some sauce and cheese. She hoped they would enjoy their dinner.

"Here you go, Sara and Ben. Spaghetti and rice. Bon appetit!"

Sara and Ben said thank you. They started to eat. Sara liked her spaghetti. She ate it all. Ben tried his spaghetti. He did not like it. He pushed it away. He tried his rice. He liked it a little. He ate some of it. He left some on his plate.

Mom noticed Ben did not finish his dinner. She asked him why.

"Ben, why didn't you eat your spaghetti and rice? Don't you like them?"

Ben shrugged. He did not want to hurt Mom's feelings. But he did not want to lie either.

"I don't like spaghetti, Mom. It is too long and sticky. And I don't like rice much, Mom. It is too small and bland. I like pizza, Mom. It is round and cheesy. Can I have pizza tomorrow, Mom?"

Mom smiled. She understood Ben's preferences. She did not mind. She loved him anyway.

"Maybe you can have pizza tomorrow, Ben. If you are good. And if you eat your breakfast and lunch. And if you try new things sometimes. Okay?"

Ben nodded. He was happy. He hugged Mom.

"Okay, Mom. I will be good. And I will eat my breakfast and lunch. And I will try new things sometimes. But I still like pizza best. Thank you, Mom."

Mom hugged Ben back. She was proud of him. He was a good boy. She kissed him on the cheek.

"You're welcome, Ben. I love you. And I love Sara too. And I love spaghetti and rice and pizza. And I love you both more than anything. Good night, Sara and Ben."

Sara and Ben said good night. They hugged Mom. They went to bed. They dreamed of pizza. And spaghetti. And rice. And Mom. And they were happy. The end.

Sam thinks for a moment. He likes the mouse too, but he knows it is not right to keep it. He has an idea.

"OK, we can keep it for a little while. But we have to pass it to someone who can take care of it. Maybe a farmer or a vet. They know how to help animals," Sam says.

Tom agrees. He is happy. He holds the mouse gently in his hands. He gives it a name. He calls it Nibbles.

They go to the house to find a box for Nibbles. They put some grass and water in the box. They make a hole for Nibbles to breathe. They put the box on the table.

They go to the kitchen to get some cheese for Nibbles. They think Nibbles will like cheese. They are wrong.

Nibbles does not like cheese. Nibbles is scared. Nibbles hears a loud noise. It is the cat. The cat sees the box. The cat smells the mouse. The cat jumps on the table. The cat knocks over the box. The cat grabs Nibbles.

Tom and Sam hear the noise. They run to the table. They see the cat. They see Nibbles. Nibbles is not moving. Nibbles is dead.

Tom and Sam are sad. They cry. They say sorry to Nibbles. They bury Nibbles in the garden. They say goodbye to Nibbles.

They learn a lesson. They learn that mice are not toys. They learn that they should not keep live things that do not belong to them. They learn that they should pass them to someone who can help them. They learn that they should be careful with animals. They learn that animals can die.

She came back to the garden and looked for the butterfly. She saw it on a red rose. She was very happy. She opened her book and started to write. She wrote: "I see a butterfly. It is yellow and black. It likes flowers."

But then, a big bee came. It buzzed near the butterfly. It wanted the rose. The butterfly was scared. It flew away. The bee followed it. Lily was sad. She wanted the butterfly to come back.

She said: "Butterfly, don't be afraid. The bee won't hurt you. You are brave. You can fly fast. Come back to me. I want to write more about you."

She waited for a while. She hoped the butterfly would hear her. She looked at the sky. She saw a flash of yellow and black. It was the butterfly. It came back to the garden. It flew to Lily. It landed on her book. It looked at her.

Lily smiled. She said: "Hello, butterfly. Thank you for coming back. You are very brave. You are my friend. Can I write more about you?"

The butterfly nodded. It stayed on her book. Lily wrote: "The butterfly is brave. It flew away from the bee. It came back to me. It is my friend. I love the butterfly."

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play together. One day, they visit Lily's grandpa. He lives in a big house with a garden.

Grandpa is bald. He has no hair on his head. He is very kind and funny. He gives Tom and Lily some cookies and juice. He tells them stories about when he was young.

"Grandpa, can we see your room?" Lily asks.

"Sure, my dear. Come with me," Grandpa says. He takes them upstairs to his room. He has a big bed, a closet, and a desk. On his desk, there is a switch.

"What is this, Grandpa?" Tom asks, pointing at the switch.

"That is a special switch. It makes the lights go on and off. Do you want to try it?" Grandpa says.

"Yes, please!" Tom and Lily say. They take turns to press the switch. The lights go on and off. On and off. They laugh and clap.

"Wow, this is fun, Grandpa!" Lily says.

"I'm glad you like it, my dear. But don't press it too much. You might break it," Grandpa says.

"Okay, Grandpa. We will be careful," Tom says.

They play with the switch for a while. Then they hug Grandpa and say thank you. They go back downstairs and play in the garden. They have a happy day.

Lily and Tom are playing with a big board. The board has many pictures of animals and things. Lily likes the board. She wants to keep it.

"Tom, can I have the board?" Lily asks.

"No, Lily, it is mine. I found it first," Tom says.

"But I like it more. Please, Tom, let me have it," Lily begs.

"No, Lily, go away. Find your own board," Tom says.

Lily is sad and angry. She wants the board very much. She tries to pull the board from Tom. Tom pulls back. They both pull hard. The board makes a loud sound. It tears in half.

"Look what you did, Lily! You broke the board!" Tom cries.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to. I just wanted the board," Lily says.

They both look at the board. It is torn and ruined. The pictures are gone. They feel bad.

They hear a voice. It is Mom. She is coming. She sees the board.

"What happened here? Who tore the board?" Mom asks.

Lily and Tom are quiet. They are scared. They know Mom will be mad.

They see a fat cat. The cat is walking by. The cat sees the board. The cat likes the board. The cat picks up the board with its mouth. The cat runs away with the board.

"Look, Mom, the cat did it! The cat tore the board!" Lily and Tom say.

Mom looks at the cat. She sees the board. She is surprised. She laughs.

"Wow, that is a very fat and naughty cat. It likes to tear boards. I guess you two are not in trouble. But next time, be careful with your toys. And share them nicely," Mom says.

Lily and Tom nod. They hug Mom. They are happy. They are not mad at each other. They are friends again.

They watch the cat. The cat is playing with the board. The cat is happy. The cat does not care that the board is torn. The cat likes to tear things.

Sam laughs. He says, "Friends are boring. Toys are fun. I don't need you. Go away."

Ben goes away. He cries. He walks to the park. He sees a big tree. He sees a rope. He thinks, "Maybe I can hang on the rope. Maybe I can fly like an aeroplane. Maybe I can be happy."

He climbs the tree. He grabs the rope. He swings on the rope. He feels the wind. He smiles. He says, "Whee! I am flying!"

But the rope is old. It breaks. Ben falls. He hits the ground. He hurts. He bleeds. He stops moving. He stops breathing.

Sam hears a scream. He runs to the park. He sees Ben. He sees the rope. He sees the blood. He feels scared. He feels sorry. He says, "Ben! Ben! Wake up! Please wake up! I am sorry! I want to be your friend!"

But Ben does not wake up. Ben is gone. Sam cries. He cries and cries. He says, "I am not rich. I am poor. I have lost my friend."

One day, they see a big dog with a tiny hat. The dog looks very funny. Sara and Ben wink at each other and giggle. They want to pet the dog, but they are a little scared.

"Hello, doggy," Sara says. "Do you like your hat?"

The dog wags his tail and barks. He seems friendly. Sara and Ben go closer. They touch his soft fur and his wet nose. The dog licks their faces.

"His name is Max," a voice says. Sara and Ben look up. They see a man with a smile. He is holding a leash. "He likes to wear hats. He has many hats. Do you want to see?"

Sara and Ben nod. They follow the man and Max to a bench. The man opens a bag. He takes out many hats. There are red hats, blue hats, yellow hats, and more. He puts them on Max, one by one. Max looks very funny. Sara and Ben wink at each other and laugh.

"Which hat do you like best?" the man asks.

Sara and Ben point at the same hat. It is a green hat with a flower. It matches Max's eyes.

"I like that hat too," the man says. "You have good taste. Do you want to keep it?"

Sara and Ben look at each other. They are surprised and happy. They nod and say thank you.

The man gives them the hat. He says goodbye and walks away with Max. Sara and Ben wave at them.

They put the hat on their heads. It is very tight. They have to share it. They take turns wearing it. They feel very special.

They run to the slide. They slide down together. They hug and smile.

They remember this day. They remember Max and his hats. They remember their secret game. They remember their best friend. They wink at each other. They are happy.

Mia likes to help her mom in the kitchen. She likes to wash the fruits and vegetables and put them in a big bowl. Today, mom is making soup with cauliflower and carrots. Mia thinks cauliflower looks like a white flower. She asks mom, "Can I smell the cauliflower?"

Mom smiles and says, "Sure, you can smell it. But be careful, it might tickle your nose." She gives Mia a small piece of cauliflower and holds it under her nose. Mia sniffs and giggles. It smells fresh and a little bit sweet.

Mom says, "Do you want to taste it too? It's good for you. It has vitamins and minerals that make you strong and healthy." She breaks off another piece of cauliflower and puts it in Mia's mouth. Mia chews and makes a face. It tastes bitter and mushy. She does not like it at all. She spits it out and says, "Yuck! I don't like cauliflower. It's gross!"

Mom says, "That's okay, Mia. You don't have to like everything. But maybe you will like it better when it's cooked in the soup. It will be soft and creamy and have more flavor. Do you want to help me stir the soup?"

Mia nods and says, "Yes, please. I like to stir." She climbs on a stool and holds a wooden spoon. Mom turns on the stove and pours some water and milk in a big pot. She adds some salt and pepper and some cheese. Then she puts the cauliflower and the carrots in the pot and says, "Now we have to wait for the soup to boil. It will take some time. Can you be calm and patient, Mia?"

Mia says, "Yes, mom. I can be calm and patient. I will watch the soup and stir it sometimes. And I will sing a song to make the time go faster." She starts to sing a song about flowers and bees and butterflies. Mom listens and smiles. She thinks Mia is a very sweet and smart girl. She hopes Mia will like the soup when it's done. She thinks it will be delicious.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. Sometimes they are loud and sometimes they are quiet.

One day, they find a big box in the living room. It has a picture of a printer on it. They are curious and want to see what is inside.

"Can we open it, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Not yet, sweetie. It is a gift for Dad. He will be home soon. You can help me wrap it later." Mom says.

Anna and Ben nod. They wait for a while, but they get bored. They look at the box again. It has a hole on one side. They peek inside and see a shiny machine.

"Wow, look! It is a printer!" Ben says.

"What does it do?" Anna asks.

"It can print pictures and words on paper. Like in our books." Ben says.

"Can we try it?" Anna asks.

"Maybe just one. Mom won't notice." Ben says.

They pull the printer out of the box. They find a cord and plug it into the wall. They turn it on and hear a beep.

They look for some paper and find a stack on the table. They take one and put it in the printer. They press a button and wait.

The printer makes a noise and prints something on the paper. It is a picture of a flower. It is red and yellow and green. It is very pretty.

"Wow, look! It is a flower!" Anna says.

"It is so delicate. Like the ones in the garden." Ben says.

They smile and admire their print. They want to make more. They take another paper and put it in the printer. They press another button and wait.

The printer makes another noise and prints something else on the paper. It is a word. It is "silence". It is black and big and bold.

"Wow, look! It is a word!" Ben says.

"What does it mean?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a name. Like Alice or Mike." Ben says.

They shrug and look for another button. They want to print more pictures and words. They don't hear Mom coming in the room.

"Anna! Ben! What are you doing?" Mom says.

They turn around and see Mom. She looks angry and surprised. She sees the printer and the papers on the floor.

"Mom, look! We made a print!" Anna says.

"It is a flower and a word!" Ben says.

They show Mom their print. Mom looks at it and sighs.

"Kids, you can't play with the printer. It is not a toy. It is a gift for Dad. And you can't print whatever you want. It costs money and ink. And you can't make so much noise. It is not polite. It breaks the silence." Mom says.

She explains to them what the word "silence" means. It means no sound. It means quiet. It means calm.

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They didn't know. They didn't mean to be bad.

"We are sorry, Mom. We didn't know. We didn't mean to be bad." They say.

They hug Mom and say they love her. Mom hugs them back and says she loves them too.

She tells them to help her put the printer back in the box. She tells them to clean up the papers. She tells them to be more careful and respectful.

They nod and do what Mom says. They learn their lesson. They still like the printer, but they know they can't use it without permission. They still like the print, but they know they can't waste it. They still like the noise, but they know they have to respect the silence.

When the rain finally stopped, Tim and Sam went outside to play. They saw the toy car and cried. They tried to fix it, but it was too late. They were very sad and sorry. They wished they had taken care of their toy car.

The moral of the story is: You should take care of your things, especially if they are rare and special. If you leave them in the rain, they might get damaged and you might lose them.

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys of different colors, shapes and sizes. Sometimes they would sort their toys into groups, like red toys, round toys or big toys. They thought sorting was fun and smart.

One day, their mom told them to sort their toys and put them away in their boxes. She said she would be back soon and they should not make a mess. Sam and Lily nodded and started to sort their toys. But then they had an idea. They decided to sort their toys in a different way. They sorted them into good toys and bad toys. Good toys were the ones they liked and bad toys were the ones they did not like or were broken or dirty.

They put all the good toys in one box and all the bad toys in another box. They were very proud of their sorting. They thought their mom would be happy too. But they were wrong. When their mom came back, she saw the two boxes and opened them. She was very angry and sad. She saw that the bad toys box had some of her favorite toys that she gave them when they were babies. She also saw that the bad toys box had some toys that belonged to their friends or cousins. She said that they were very naughty and selfish. She said that they should not sort their toys by good or bad, but by who they belonged to and how they could share them. She said that they should not throw away or ruin their toys, but take care of them and appreciate them. She said that they should not judge their toys by their looks, but by their value and meaning.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a cage. Inside the cage, there is a lion. The lion looks sad.

"Where is the lion going?" Sara asks.

The man who drives the truck says, "He is going to the zoo. He came from the jungle, but he was sick. We have to weigh him and check him."

"Can we see him weigh?" Tom asks.

The man nods. He stops the truck and opens the cage. He puts a big scale on the ground. He gives the lion some meat. The lion walks out of the cage and eats the meat. He steps on the scale.

"Wow, he is very heavy!" Sara says.

The man looks at the number on the scale. He writes it on a paper. He says, "He is fine. He is not sick anymore. He just needs some rest and friends. He will be happy at the zoo."

"Can we visit him at the zoo?" Tom asks.

The man smiles. He says, "Sure, you can. He will like to see you. He is a friendly lion. But be careful, he is still a wild animal. Don't touch him or go too close to him."

Sara and Tom nod. They say, "Thank you, mister. Bye, lion. We hope you like the zoo."

The lion roars. He sounds happy. He goes back to the cage. The man closes the cage and drives away. Sara and Tom wave to the lion. They go back to the park. They play some more. They are happy too.

"Ha! I got you, Lily!" Ben said, pointing his gun at his sister.

"No, you didn't! You missed!" Lily said, sticking out her tongue.

"Yes, I did! You have to fall down and play dead!" Ben said, running towards her.

But before he could reach her, he tripped over a big pile of stuff. It was their dad's old clothes and books that he was going to give away. Ben fell down and hurt his knee. He started to cry.

Lily heard him and ran to help him. She saw the blood on his knee and felt sorry for him. She forgot about their game and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Ben. Are you okay?" she asked.

"It hurts, Lily. It hurts a lot." Ben said, sobbing.

Lily looked around and saw the back door was open. She saw their mom inside the house. She had a band-aid and a kiss for Ben.

"Mom! Mom! Ben is hurt! He needs a band-aid and a kiss!" Lily shouted.

Mom heard her and came out. She saw Ben's knee and felt sorry for him too. She picked him up and carried him inside. She cleaned his wound and put a band-aid and a kiss on it.

"There, there. You'll be fine, Ben. It's just a scratch." Mom said, smiling.

"Thank you, Mom. You're the best." Ben said, smiling too.

She wants Sara all to herself.

You have to sleep in your basket, eat from your bowl, and use your scratching post. You have to share your toys, milk, and hugs. You have to be nice to Lulu and other kittens. If you do these things, I will still love you and play with you. But if you don't, I will be angry and sad."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends saw an elderly man sitting on a bench. The man had a big smile on his face.

"Hello, young ones," said the man. "Do you want to hear a story about a lion?"

"Yes, please!" said Timmy and his friends.

The elderly man began to tell the story. "Once upon a time, there was a lion who lived in the jungle. He was very strong and powerful. But as the lion grew older, he began to forget things."

"Like what?" asked Timmy.

"Like where he left his food, or where he had been the day before," said the man. "One day, the lion forgot where his den was. He wandered around the jungle for hours, feeling lost and scared."

Timmy and his friends listened intently to the story. As the man finished, Timmy said, "I will remember to help others when they forget things, just like we helped the lion."

And so, Timmy and his friends went back to playing, remembering the lesson they had learned from the story of the forgetful lion.

Lily loved to help her grandma cook. Grandma was elderly, but she was very kind and funny. She taught Lily how to chop carrots, stir soup and make bread. Lily felt happy when she cooked with grandma.

One day, grandma asked Lily to help her make a salad. She gave Lily a big green pepper and a small knife. Lily liked peppers, they were crunchy and sweet. She started to cut the pepper into pieces, just like grandma showed her.

But then, Lily felt a sting in her eyes. The pepper was not sweet, it was spicy! It made Lily's eyes hurt and water. Lily dropped the knife and the pepper and started to cry. She rubbed her eyes, but it only made them hurt more.

Grandma heard Lily cry and ran to her. She saw the pepper and the knife and understood what happened. She hugged Lily and said, "Oh, my dear, you cut a hot pepper, not a sweet pepper. Hot peppers are very spicy and they can make your eyes burn. I'm sorry, I should have checked the pepper first."

Grandma took Lily to the sink and washed her eyes with cold water. She dried them with a soft towel and kissed them gently. She said, "There, there, it's okay. The pain will go away soon. You are very brave and smart, Lily. You did a good job cutting the pepper. Next time, we will make sure we have the right pepper, okay?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt better now. She said, "Thank you, grandma. I love you. Can we still make the salad?"

Grandma smiled and said, "Of course, we can. Let's go find a sweet pepper and finish the salad. And then we can have some bread and soup and cake. How does that sound?"

Lily clapped her hands and said, "That sounds yummy. I love cooking with you, grandma. You are the best."

Grandma and Lily went back to the kitchen and made the salad. They had a delicious lunch and a happy time together. They both forgot about the hot pepper and the tears. They only remembered the love and the laughter.

Once upon a time, there was a generous bunny. The bunny was always kind to his friends in the forest. He was always ready to share what he had and help those around him.

One day, the bunny decided to settle down in a cozy spot. He hopped over to a sunny tree and wiggled his way into the crevice. He made a comfy nest for himself and settled in for a nap.

Suddenly, he felt something tickle his nose! He opened one eye to see what it was. He saw a tiny ladybug. It hadn't noticed that the bunny was in the tree and it had tried to land on his nose.

The bunny gave the little ladybug a friendly wink and showed her the spot in the tree that he had settled in. The little ladybug laughed and thanked the Bunny for being so generous. It hopped away and waved goodbye.

The Bunny was so happy. It was nice to know so many friends in the forest. He settled back down into his cozy nest and went to sleep.

Timmy learned a lesson that day. He realized he should have listened to his mom and kept the knife away from his fingers. From then on, he promised to be more careful with sharp things. But it was too late, and his finger hurt for a long time. The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and keep yourself safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden and pick flowers. One day, she found a shiny crown in the dirt. It was so pretty and made her feel like a princess. She put it on her head and danced around.

Suddenly, the world around her started to shrink. The trees got smaller, the flowers got tiny, and even the sun looked far away. Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. She tried to take off the crown, but it wouldn't come off.

As the world around her got smaller and smaller, Lily started to feel very cold. She shivered and wished she had never found the crown. Finally, everything was so small that Lily couldn't see anything at all. She was lost and alone in a tiny world.

Sadly, Lily stayed lost forever, never able to take off the crown or return to her normal size. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Mittens. Mittens liked to sleep all day and didn't like to play with toys. One day, Mittens saw a big bowl of powder on the table. Mittens wondered what it was and decided to investigate. 

Mittens jumped onto the table and sniffed the powder. It smelled funny, but Mittens was curious. Suddenly, Mittens sneezed and the powder went everywhere! Mittens was covered in white powder and looked very silly. 

Mittens didn't feel lazy anymore, he felt energized and started to play with the powder. He rolled around in it and made a big mess. Mittens had so much fun that he forgot all about being lazy. From that day on, Mittens was always curious and loved to explore new things.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom always slept and never did any work. One day, Tom's friend asked him to help with the cooking. Tom said no because he was too lazy. 

His friend told him, "Tom, if you don't help, we won't have enough sauce for everyone." Tom didn't care and went back to sleep. 

Later that day, when everyone was eating, they realized there wasn't enough sauce. Tom's friend was sad and everyone was hungry. Tom felt bad and realized that he should have helped. From that day on, Tom promised to never be lazy again and always help his friends. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to help others, even if you feel lazy. And always remember, if you don't help, the number of people who will be happy will be less.

One day, Tom and Lily went for a walk with their big dog, Rex. They liked to walk in the park and see the trees and flowers. Rex liked to run and sniff and bark.

But today, they saw something new in the park. It was a big sack, and it was moving. Tom and Lily were curious. They wanted to see what was in the sack. Rex wanted to see too. He ran to the sack and started to pull it with his teeth.

"Rex, stop!" Tom shouted. "You don't know what's in there!"

But Rex did not stop. He ripped the sack open. And out came a fierce cat. The cat was angry and scared. It hissed and scratched at Rex. Rex yelped and ran away.

"Meow!" the cat said. "Go away! This is my home!"

Tom and Lily felt sorry for the cat. They saw that the sack had some food and a blanket inside. Someone had left the cat in the park.

"Hello, cat," Lily said softly. "We are sorry. We did not mean to scare you. Do you want to be our friend?"

The cat looked at Lily. She saw that Lily was kind and gentle. She calmed down and purred.

"Meow," the cat said. "Yes, I want to be your friend. But I don't like dogs."

Tom and Lily smiled. They decided to take the cat home with them. They put the food and the blanket in the sack and carried it. Rex followed them, but he kept his distance from the cat.

They named the cat Sack. Sack was happy to have a new home and new friends. Rex was happy too, but he learned to be careful around fierce cats.

It is a label with a wide blade inside, and it cuts Mia's hair and scalp. Mia cries and bleeds. Ben drops the label and sees what he has done. He is shocked and sorry.

"Mia, Mia, I'm sorry, I didn't know, I didn't mean to hurt you!" he says, sobbing.

But Mia does not answer. She is too hurt and scared. She runs to their mom and shows her the wound. Their mom is angry and worried. She takes Mia to the doctor and calls Ben's dad. Ben is in big trouble. He has to say sorry to Mia and to his mom and dad. He has to throw away all his stickers and labels. He has to learn what sharp means and why it is dangerous. He has to be more careful and kind with his sister. He feels very bad and sad. He wishes he never found the sharp label.

Lily and Sam liked to play in the garden. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They liked to look for bugs and flowers and rocks. One day, they saw a cricket on the grass. It was brown and shiny and had long legs.

"Look, a cricket!" Lily said. "Let's catch it!"

They ran after the cricket, but it was very fast. It hopped and skipped and hid. Lily and Sam tried to be quiet and careful, but the cricket always got away.

"Wait, I have an idea!" Sam said. He got a jar and a lid from the house. He put some grass and leaves in the jar. "Let's make a home for the cricket. Maybe it will like it and come inside."

They put the jar on the ground near the cricket. They waited and watched. The cricket saw the jar. It paused and looked. It seemed curious. It moved closer and closer.

"Shh, don't scare it!" Lily whispered. "Be ready to put the lid on!"

The cricket hopped on the grass. It reached the jar. It climbed on the leaves. It went inside.

"Now!" Sam shouted. He put the lid on the jar. He and Lily cheered. They caught the cricket!

They picked up the jar and looked at the cricket. It was still and quiet. It looked sad.

"Maybe it doesn't like the jar," Lily said. "Maybe it misses its friends and family."

Sam nodded. He felt sorry for the cricket. He opened the lid and let the cricket go. It jumped out of the jar and back to the grass. It chirped and hopped away.

"Bye, cricket!" Lily and Sam said. "Thank you for playing with us!"

They smiled and waved. They were happy to see the cricket happy. They went back to the house and told their mom about their adventure. They had fun in the garden.

"Not yet, it is not ready. You have to wait a little bit." Lila's mom says.

Lila and Tom are impatient. They want to taste the rice. They think it is ready. They sneak to the pot. They open the lid. They see the steam. They reach for the rice.

"Ouch!" Lila and Tom say. They burn their fingers. They cry.

Lila's mom hears them. She runs to the kitchen. She sees what happened. She is angry and worried. She takes Lila and Tom to the sink. She puts cold water on their fingers. She puts bandages on their fingers. She hugs them.

"I'm sorry, mom. We were hungry. We wanted to taste the rice." Lila says.

"I'm sorry, too. We did not listen to you. We were not careful." Tom says.

Lila's mom is not angry anymore. She is sad. She says:

"I know you were hungry and excited. But you have to listen to me. I know what is best for you. I want you to be safe and happy. The rice was not ready. It was too hot. You could have hurt yourself more. You have to be patient and wait for the right time. Do you understand?"

Lila and Tom nod. They say:

"Yes, mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will listen to you next time. We will be patient and wait for the right time."

Lila's mom smiles. She says:

"Thank you. I love you. Now, the rice is ready. Let's have lunch together. But be careful, it is still hot."

Lila and Tom smile. They say:

"Thank you. We love you, too. Let's have lunch together. We will be careful, it is not too hot."

They have lunch together. They enjoy the rice. They are happy. They learn a lesson. They learn to listen, to be patient and to be careful.

Tom and Mia nod. They say sorry to the other kids. They promise to be good and listen to their friend's warnings. They do not want to open any more boxes.

One day, a sailor went to the sea with his boat. He liked to zip on the water and feel the wind in his hair. He saw many fish and birds and waves.

He met another sailor who had a bigger boat. The other sailor said, "Hello, do you want to race with me? My boat is fast and strong. I can beat you easily."

The sailor did not like to be challenged. He said, "No, thank you. I like to zip on the water and enjoy the view. I do not care about being fast or strong. I am happy with my boat."

The other sailor laughed and said, "You are scared. You know you will lose. Come on, let's race. It will be fun."

The sailor did not want to be rude. He said, "OK, fine. Let's race. But only to the big rock over there. Then I will go back to zipping on the water."

The other sailor agreed and they both started their engines. The bigger boat was fast and loud. It made a lot of noise and spray. The smaller boat was quiet and smooth. It glided on the water and followed the wind.

The bigger boat reached the big rock first. The other sailor shouted, "I win! I win! You are slow and weak. My boat is the best."

The sailor did not mind. He smiled and said, "Good for you. You are fast and strong. But I am happy and free. My boat is the best for me."

He turned his boat around and zipped on the water. He felt the wind in his hair. He saw many fish and birds and waves. He was happy.

"Mom, can I use your needle and thread to make a paper quilt?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, needles are sharp and can hurt you. You are too little to use them. You can use glue or tape instead." Mom said.

"But I want to make a quilt like you. Please, mom, let me try." Lily begged.

Mom was busy and did not want to argue. She gave Lily a needle and thread and told her to be careful. She said she would check on her later.

Lily was happy. She took the needle and thread and went to her room. She started to sew the paper squares together. She did not know how to make a knot, so the thread was loose. She did not know how to hold the needle, so she poked her finger. She did not know how to cut the thread, so she used her teeth. She did not know how to clean the mess, so she left the paper and thread on the floor.

"Lily, why did you use the needle? I told you it was dangerous. You could have hurt yourself badly. You should have listened to me. I know what is best for you. You are not ready to use the needle. Lily was sorry and ashamed. She said:

"I'm sorry, mom. I wanted to make a paper quilt like you. I thought I could use the needle. I did not mean to hurt myself. I love you too. I will listen to you next time. I will not use the needle until you teach me how."

Mom smiled and kissed her. She said:

"It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. I'm proud of you for trying to make a paper quilt. It was a nice idea. But you have to be careful with tools. Lily said:

"I will, mom. I promise."

Anna loved carrots. She ate them every day for lunch and dinner. She liked how they were crunchy and sweet. She also liked how they made her eyes bright and her skin healthy.

One day, Anna went to the market with her mom. She saw a big pile of carrots and wanted to buy some. She asked her mom if she could have one. Her mom said yes, but only if she was obedient and stayed close to her.

Anna was happy and took a carrot. She washed it with water and bit into it. It was delicious. She smiled and thanked her mom.

But then, something bad happened. Anna felt a tickle in her nose. She tried to hold it in, but she couldn't. She sneezed very loud and hard. The carrot flew out of her mouth and hit a man in the face.

The man was angry and shouted at Anna. He said she was rude and messy. He said she should say sorry and give him a new carrot.

Anna was scared and sad. She didn't mean to sneeze. She didn't mean to hit the man. She wanted to say sorry, but she didn't know how.

Her mom saw what happened and came to help. She hugged Anna and told her it was okay. She said sneezing was normal and not her fault. She said the man was mean and wrong. She said she was proud of Anna for being obedient and eating carrots.

She gave the man a new carrot and told him to be nice. She took Anna's hand and walked away. She bought Anna another carrot and a treat. She told Anna she loved her and that she was a good girl.

Anna felt better and smiled. She ate her carrot and her treat. She said she loved her mom and that she was sorry for sneezing. Her mom said she didn't have to be sorry and that she was happy for sneezing. She said sneezing was good for clearing the nose and the germs.

Anna learned a new word: germs. She asked her mom what they were. Her mom explained that they were tiny things that could make people sick. She said carrots helped to fight them and keep people healthy.

Anna was amazed and curious. She wanted to know more about germs and carrots. She asked her mom many questions. Her mom answered them and taught her more words.

Anna enjoyed learning and talking with her mom. She felt smart and brave. She decided she would always eat carrots and sneeze when she needed to. She decided she would always be obedient and kind. She decided she would always love her mom and herself.

Sara is a young girl who likes to write. She has a big book with many pages and a red pen. She writes stories about animals, flowers and stars. She likes to show her stories to her mom and dad.

One day, Sara is writing a story about a telephone. She thinks telephones are fun and smart. They can talk to other telephones far away. She writes how the telephone makes sounds and how she can say hello to her grandma.

She hears the telephone ring in the living room. She runs to answer it. She picks up the telephone and says hello.

"Hello, Sara, this is grandma. How are you?" says the voice on the telephone.

"Hi, grandma, I am good. I am writing a story about you and the telephone," says Sara.

"Really? That sounds wonderful. Can you tell me your story?" says grandma.

Sara smiles and tells her story to grandma. She tells how the telephone helps them talk and how she loves grandma very much. Grandma listens and says she loves Sara too. She says she is proud of Sara for writing stories.

Sara is happy and says thank you to grandma. She says goodbye and hangs up the telephone. She runs back to her book and writes more stories. She thinks writing is fun and smart too.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books and a big bed. They also have a sheet with amazing colors and shapes. They call it the magic sheet.

One day, Anna and Ben want to play with the magic sheet. But they have different ideas. Anna wants to make a tent with the sheet and pretend to camp. Ben wants to wear the sheet as a cape and pretend to fly. They both pull the sheet and say, "It's mine!"

The sheet rips in the middle. Anna and Ben are shocked. They look at the torn sheet and start to cry. They cry very loud. They cry so loud that Mom hears them. She comes to their room and sees the mess.

"What happened here?" Mom asks. She is not happy.

Anna and Ben stop crying and point at each other. They say, "He did it!" and "She did it!"

Mom shakes her head. She says, "You both did it. You both ripped the sheet. You both need to say sorry and share."

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They say sorry to each other and hug. They say sorry to Mom and hug. They say sorry to the sheet and hug.

Mom smiles. She says, "It's okay. The sheet is still amazing. We can fix it. We can sew it or patch it or make something new with it. We can still have fun with it."

Anna and Ben nod. They agree. They thank Mom and help her clean the room. They decide to play with the sheet together. They make a tent and a cape and many other things. They have fun with the sheet. They are happy.

Lily and Ben wanted to go to the store with Mom. They liked to look at the toys and books there. But Mom said they had to wait in the car. She had a ticket for a big prize. She wanted to see if she won.

"Can we come with you, Mom?" Lily asked. "Please?"

"No, sweetie, you have to stay here. It will be very quick. I'll be right back," Mom said. She gave them a kiss and locked the car.

Lily and Ben were bored. They played with their toys for a while, but then they wanted to get out. They saw other kids walking with their parents. They saw a big balloon man making funny shapes. They saw a dog with a hat.

"Let's go see the balloon man," Ben said. He opened the door and got out.

"No, Ben, we can't. Mom said to stay here," Lily said. She was bossy. She always told Ben what to do.

"But I want to see the balloon man. He looks fun. Come on, Lily," Ben said. He grabbed her hand and pulled her out.

Lily and Ben ran to the balloon man. He smiled and gave them each a balloon. Lily got a pink flower. Ben got a blue sword. They were happy.

But then they heard Mom's voice. She sounded angry.

"Lily! Ben! Where are you? Come back here right now!" Mom shouted. She had a paper in her hand. It was the ticket.

Lily and Ben saw Mom. They felt scared. They dropped their balloons and ran to her.

"Mom, we're sorry. We just wanted to see the balloon man," Lily said.

"Mom, we're sorry. We were bored," Ben said.

Mom hugged them and sighed. She was not happy.

"You should have listened to me. You could have gotten lost or hurt. You have to stay in the car when I tell you to," Mom said.

She looked at the ticket. It had a big red X on it.

"And I didn't win the prize. It was a waste of time," Mom said.

She threw the ticket in the trash and took Lily and Ben back to the car.

"Maybe next time we can go to the store together," Mom said.

"Maybe next time we can get more balloons," Lily said.

"Maybe next time we can see the dog with the hat," Ben said.

They all laughed and drove home.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to look for things on the ground. They found leaves, stones, and bugs. They put them in a basket.

"Look, Lily, I found a big twig!" Tom said. He held up a long, brown stick.

"Wow, that is a big twig, Tom!" Lily said. "What can we do with it?"

Tom thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"I recommend we use it as a sword!" he said. "We can pretend to be knights and fight dragons!"

Lily liked Tom's idea. She smiled and nodded.

"OK, let's do that!" she said. "But we need another twig for me. Where can we find one?"

Tom looked around. He saw another big twig near a tree.

"There, Lily, there is one!" he said. He pointed to the twig.

Lily ran to the tree and picked up the twig. It was big and heavy.

"Thank you, Tom!" she said. "Now we have two swords!"

Tom and Lily held their twigs and waved them in the air. They made sounds like swords.

"Zing, zang, zong!" Tom said.

"Zap, zop, zup!" Lily said.

They ran around the park, pretending to be knights and fight dragons. They had a lot of fun with their big twigs.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with paint and paper. They have many tubes of paint. Red, blue, yellow, green, and more. They squeeze the paint on the paper and make shapes and pictures.

One day, they want to paint outside. It is cold and windy. They put on their coats and hats and go to the garden. They find a big rock to put their paper on. They open their tubes of paint and start to paint.

"Look, Mia, I paint a sun!" Tom says. He paints a big yellow circle with orange rays.

"That is nice, Tom. I paint a flower!" Mia says. She paints a red circle with purple petals.

They paint more things. They paint a tree, a bird, a house, a car. They have fun.

But then, the wind blows hard. It blows their paper off the rock. It blows their tubes of paint away. Tom and Mia are sad. They run after their paper and paint. But they are too slow. The wind takes them far, far away.

"Where is our paper? Where is our paint?" Tom cries.

"I don't know, Tom. They are gone." Mia cries.

They hug each other. They are cold and sad. They go back to the house. They tell their moms what happened. Their moms hug them. They give them hot chocolate and cookies. They say they can paint again another day.

Tom and Mia feel better. They thank their moms. They say they are still friends. They say they will paint again when it is not cold and windy. They smile.

Lily and Ben are hungry. They want to eat meat for lunch. But they have no meat at home. They have to go to the shop.

They walk to the shop with Mum. They see many things on the way. They see cars and bikes and dogs and cats. They look at everything. They like to look.

They get to the shop. Mum says, "Wait here. I will get the meat." She goes inside. Lily and Ben wait outside. They see a big bird. It is black and has a yellow beak. It is a crow.

The crow sees the meat in the shop. It wants to eat the meat. It flies to the shop. It tries to get the meat. Mum sees the crow. She shouts, "Go away, crow! That is my meat!"

Lily and Ben see the crow too. They are scared. The crow is big and loud. They want Mum to come back. They hold hands. They are brave. They say, "Go away, crow! That is our meat!"

The crow hears Lily and Ben. It is surprised. It sees that they are brave. It does not like brave children. It flies away. It looks for another meat.

Mum comes back. She has the meat. She sees Lily and Ben. She smiles. She says, "Well done, Lily and Ben! You are very brave. You scared the crow away. Now we can have meat for lunch."

Lily and Ben are happy. They hug Mum. They say, "We love you, Mum. We love meat. We are brave." They go home. They have meat for lunch. They are full and happy. The end.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. They ran after the ball and laughed.

One day, a big dog appeared in the park. It saw the ball and ran after it too. It grabbed the ball with its teeth and shook it. Tom and Lily were scared. They wanted their ball back, but they did not want to go near the dog.

"Hey, that's our ball!" Tom shouted. "Give it back!"

The dog growled and barked. It did not want to give the ball back. It thought the ball was its toy.

Tom and Lily were worried. They did not know what to do. They looked around for help.

They saw a man walking in the park. He had a leash in his hand. He was the dog's owner.

"Excuse me, sir," Lily said. "Can you please get our ball from your dog? He took it from us and we are scared."

The man smiled and nodded. He walked over to the dog and said, "Drop it, Rex. That's not your ball. That's their ball. Be nice and share."

The dog obeyed and dropped the ball. The man picked it up and gave it to Tom and Lily. He apologized for the dog's behavior and said, "He's a friendly dog, but he loves to play with balls. He didn't mean to scare you. Do you want to pet him?"

Tom and Lily hesitated, but they saw that the dog was wagging its tail and licking the man's hand. They decided to give the dog a chance. They petted the dog and said, "Hello, Rex. You are a good dog. We are sorry we yelled at you."

The dog licked their faces and wagged its tail more. He was happy to make new friends. He let them play with his ball too.

Tom and Lily thanked the man and the dog for their kindness. They learned that sometimes things are not what they seem, and that they should not judge by appearances. They also learned to be brave and ask for help when they need it. They had a fun day in the park with their ball and their new friend, Rex. They felt welcome and safe.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play on the farm. They had many animals to see and feed, but their favorite was the goat. The goat was white and soft, and he liked to eat grass and hay. Sometimes he would make funny noises and jump around.

One day, Ben and Lily saw a big dog near the goat pen. The dog was barking and growling, and he wanted to chase the goat. The goat was scared and ran to the corner of the pen. Ben and Lily were scared too, and they ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, there is a big dog and he wants to hurt the goat!" Ben cried.

"Where is the dog?" Mom asked.

"Over there, near the goat pen!" Lily pointed.

Mom took a stick and went to the goat pen. She saw the dog and shouted, "Go away, bad dog! Leave the goat alone!" The dog was surprised and ran away. Mom checked the goat and saw that he was not hurt. She gave him some water and a hug.

"Thank you, mom, you are so brave!" Ben and Lily said.

"No, you are brave, for telling me about the dog. And the goat is brave too, for not giving up. He is a good goat, and we love him." Mom said.

"Can we give him a name?" Ben asked.

"Sure, what do you want to call him?" Mom asked.

Ben and Lily thought for a moment, and then they said together, "Change!"

"Why Change?" Mom asked.

"Because he changed from scared to happy, and because he changed our day from bad to good." Ben and Lily explained.

Mom smiled and said, "That is a very nice name. I like it. Come on, let's go and play with Change. He is our brave goat."

Anna and Ben walked slowly to the statue. They wanted to see its teeth and eyes. They were not afraid of the lion.

But when they got closer, they heard a loud roar. It came from behind the statue. They turned around and saw a real lion. It had escaped from the zoo. It was angry and hungry.

Anna and Ben screamed. They ran back to their mom. Mom screamed too. She picked them up and ran to the car. She locked the doors and called the police.

The police came and caught the lion. They took it back to the zoo. They said sorry to Anna, Ben and mom. They said the lion was not supposed to be in the park. They said it was a mistake.

Anna and Ben were very scared. They hugged their mom. They did not want to see the statue or the lion ever again. They wanted to go home and play with their toys. They were glad they were safe.

"Maybe there are treasures in there," Sara said.

"Or secrets," Ben said.

They tried to pull the lock, but it was too hard. They looked for a key, but they could not find one. They felt upset. They wanted to know what was in the box.

"Let's go and ask Mom," Sara said.

"OK," Ben said.

They ran down the stairs and found Mom in the kitchen. She was wiping the table with a cloth.

"Mom, Mom, can you help us?" Sara said.

"What is it, sweeties?" Mom said.

"We found a big box in the attic, but it has a lock on it. Do you have the key?" Ben said.

Mom smiled. She put down the cloth and took their hands.

"Come with me. I'll show you something," she said.

She led them back to the attic and to the big box. She took out a key from her pocket and unlocked the box. She lifted the lid and showed them what was inside.

There were many photos and letters and medals and souvenirs. They were from Mom's dad, who was a soldier and a hero. He died when Mom was little.

"These are his memories. He wanted me to have them and to share them with you," Mom said.

She took out a photo of him and showed it to Sara and Ben. He had a big smile and a uniform.

"This is your grandpa. He loved you very much, even if he never met you," Mom said.

Sara and Ben looked at the photo and felt curious and happy. They hugged Mom and thanked her for showing them the box.

They decided to sit with Mom and look at the other things in the box. They learned more about their grandpa and his stories. They felt closer to him and to Mom.

They forgot to be upset. They were glad they found the box.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play with paper. They cut paper, fold paper, and draw on paper. They make paper hats, paper planes, and paper animals.

"Wow, Tom, where does the map go?" Anna asks. She sees a red X on the map.

"Maybe it goes to a treasure!" Tom says. He wants to find the treasure.

"Let's follow the map!" Anna says. She is excited.

Tom and Anna take the paper and walk along the streets. They look at the map and the buildings. They try to find the red X.

But the map is not easy to read. It has many words and numbers that Tom and Anna do not know. It also has many lines and shapes that Tom and Anna do not understand.

"Tom, I am lost. I do not know where we are." Anna says. She is scared.

"Me too, Anna. I do not know where the treasure is." Tom says. He is sad.

They look around and see a man. He is wearing a blue shirt and a hat. He is holding a bag.

"Excuse me, sir, can you help us?" Tom asks. He shows the paper to the man.

The man looks at the paper. He smiles.

"What does it tell people?" Anna asks.

"Tickets?" Tom and Anna say.

"OK, Tom, let's go!" Anna says.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play near the lake. They saw a big white boat on the water. It looked shiny and fast.

"Can we go on the boat?" Tom asked Sam.

"I don't know. Maybe we can ask the man who owns the boat," Sam said.

They ran to the dock where the boat was tied. They saw a man with a hat and a beard. He was holding a fishing rod.

"Hello, sir. Can we go on your boat?" Tom asked the man.

The man smiled and nodded. "Sure, you can. But you have to be careful and wear these vests," he said. He gave them two orange vests that had straps and buckles.

"Thank you, sir. You are very nice," Sam said.

They put on the vests and climbed on the boat. The man started the engine and the boat moved on the water. It made a loud noise and splashed the waves.

Tom and Sam felt happy and excited. They waved to the birds and the trees. They saw a big bridge and a small island.

The man told them stories about the lake and the fish. He said he had a surprise for them.

"What is it?" Tom asked.

"You'll see soon," the man said.

He steered the boat to a hidden cove. There, they saw a huge white swan. It had a long neck and a fluffy tail. It looked like a fairy tale.

"Wow! It's beautiful!" Sam said.

The man threw some bread to the swan. The swan came closer and ate the bread. It let Tom and Sam touch its feathers.

The brothers felt amazed and happy. They thanked the man and the swan. They had the best day ever.

Tom and Sam take off their masks and say, "Yes, please, Mom. We love cookies and milk."

"Stop it, stop it!" their mom said. She heard the noise and came to their room. She saw them fighting. She was not happy. She took off their ears and tails and collar and bone. She said, "You are not animals. You are children. You have to be nice to each other. Say sorry and hug."

Lily and Sam felt bad. They said sorry and hugged. They did not want to act like animals anymore. They wanted to act like friends. They asked their mom if they could watch a real TV. Their mom said yes. They watched a show about animals. They learned how animals live and act. They liked the show. They said, "Maybe we can act like animals again. But only the nice ones."

Tommy liked to play in the garden. He liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. He liked to make friends with the bugs and talk to them. He did not like to hurt them.

One day, he found a big hill of dirt with many ants on it. He wanted to say hello to the ants. He put his hand on the hill and said, "Hi, ants! Do you want to play with me?" But the ants did not answer. They did not like Tommy's hand on their home. They bit his hand with their little teeth. Tommy felt a lot of pain. He cried and ran to his mom.

Mom saw Tommy's hand. It was red and swollen. She put some cream on it and gave him a hug. She asked him, "What happened, Tommy? Did you touch something you shouldn't have?" Tommy was ashamed. He did not want to tell Mom that he bothered the ants. He thought Mom would be angry with him. He said, "I don't know, Mom. I just played in the garden."

Mom looked at Tommy. She knew he was not telling the truth. She said, "Tommy, I know you like bugs, but you have to be careful. Some bugs can hurt you if you touch them. You have to respect their space and leave them alone. Do you understand?" Tommy nodded. He said, "I'm sorry, Mom. I won't do it again." Mom smiled. She said, "It's okay, Tommy. I love you. But next time, if you have a problem, you have to answer me honestly. Can you do that?" Tommy nodded again. He said, "Yes, Mom. I love you too." He gave Mom a big kiss and hugged her. He learned his lesson. He did not play with the ants anymore. He played with the butterflies instead. They did not bite him. They were nice.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big hole in the ground. They want to see what is inside.

"Can we go in?" Sara asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "It looks deep."

They look at the hole. It is dark and scary. They hear a noise.

"Hello?" a voice says. "Is anyone there?"

Sara and Ben are surprised. Who is in the hole?

"Who are you?" Ben calls.

"I am Tom," the voice says. "I am stuck. I need help."

Sara and Ben feel sorry for Tom. They want to help him.

"How can we help you?" Sara asks.

"Can you find a rope?" Tom says. "Or a ladder? Or something to pull me up?"

Sara and Ben look around. They see a rope on a tree. They run to get it.

"Here, we have a rope!" Ben says. He throws one end of the rope into the hole.

"Thank you!" Tom says. He grabs the rope. Sara and Ben pull hard. They pull Tom out of the hole.

Tom is dirty and tired. He smiles at Sara and Ben.

"Thank you so much!" he says. "You are very kind. How did you find me?"

"We heard your word," Sara says.

"Yes, your word helped us," Ben says.

Tom hugs Sara and Ben. They are happy. They are friends. They play in the park. They stay away from the hole. It is too deep.

Ben and Lily liked to play hide and seek in the park. Ben was good at finding hidden places, like behind the big tree or under the slide. Lily was good at counting and looking for Ben, but sometimes she got tired and wanted to do something else.

One day, they saw a big post with a sign on it. The sign had words and pictures, but they could not read them. They only knew that the post was for people who wanted to send letters. Ben had an idea. He said to Lily, "Let's play a new game. I will hide a letter for you, and you have to find it. Then you hide a letter for me, and I have to find it. We can use these leaves as letters."

Lily liked the idea. She agreed to play. Ben went first. He took a leaf and wrote his name on it with a stick. He looked for a good place to hide it. He saw a hole in the post, near the bottom. He thought it was a perfect spot. He put the leaf inside the hole and ran back to Lily. He said, "I hid a letter for you. Can you find it?"

Lily started to look for the letter. She checked behind the bushes, under the bench, and in the trash can. She could not find it. She was getting frustrated. She asked Ben, "Is it very hidden?" Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, it is. But you can do it. You can manage."

Lily did not give up. She looked harder. She noticed the post and the sign. She wondered if Ben hid the letter there. She walked closer and looked at the post. She saw the hole. She reached inside and felt something. She pulled it out. It was the leaf with Ben's name on it. She was so happy. She shouted, "I found it! I found it!"

Ben clapped and cheered. He said, "You did it! You managed! You are very smart!" Lily smiled and hugged him. She said, "Thank you! That was a fun game. Now it's your turn. I will hide a letter for you." They took turns hiding and finding letters, until it was time to go home. They had a lot of fun with the post and the leaves. They decided to play the game again next time.
