One day, they find a big box in the corner of the room. It has a lock on it and a key next to it. They wonder what is inside the box. Maybe more cars or other toys. They want to open it and see.

Ben takes the key and puts it in the lock. He turns it and hears a click. He unlocks the box and lifts the lid. He and Mia look inside and gasp. There are many animals in the box. There are dogs and cats and rabbits and birds. They are all very quiet and still.

Ben and Mia are confused. Why are there animals in the box? Why are they not making any sounds? They touch them gently and see that they are soft and warm. They are not toys, they are real.

They hear a voice behind them. It is their mom. She smiles and says, "Surprise! These are your new friends. They are from the shelter. They need a home and someone to love them. They are all deaf, so they cannot hear you, but they can feel you. Do you want to keep them?"

Ben and Mia nod and hug their mom. They are happy and excited. They take the animals out of the box and play with them. They give them names and food and water. They make signs with their hands to communicate with them. They are a big group of friends. They love their deaf animals.

Sam liked to help his mom in the garden. He liked to see the green plants grow and make red tomatoes. He liked to pick the tomatoes and put them in a basket. He liked to eat the tomatoes with salt and cheese.

One day, Sam went to the garden with his mom. He saw a big tomato on a plant. He wanted to pick it and eat it. He reached for the tomato, but it was too high. He tried to jump, but he could not reach it. He looked for a stool, but he could not find one.

He saw a big rock near the plant. He thought he could step on the rock and get the tomato. He ran to the rock and stepped on it. But the rock was not a rock. It was a spoiled tomato that had fallen from the plant. It was soft and mushy and smelly. It squished under Sam's foot and made a loud pop. Sam slipped and fell on the ground. He was covered in spoiled tomato juice and seeds.

Sam started to cry. He did not like the spoiled tomato. He did not like the smell and the mess. He wanted a clean tomato. He wanted his mom.

His mom heard him cry and ran to him. She saw what had happened and hugged him. She said, "It's okay, Sam. It was an accident. You did not know it was a spoiled tomato. Let's go inside and wash up. We have more tomatoes in the basket. We can eat them later."

Sam nodded and sniffed. He felt better. He went inside with his mom and washed up. He put on a clean shirt and pants. He ate a fresh tomato with salt and cheese. He liked the fresh tomato. He did not like the spoiled tomato. He learned to be careful where he stepped.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play hide and seek in the park. Tom is good at hiding. Mia is good at finding. One day, they play hide and seek when it is cold outside. They wear warm hats and coats.

Tom says, "I will hide first. You count to ten and then find me." Mia says, "OK. I will find you fast." Tom runs away and looks for a good spot. He sees a big box near a tree. He thinks, "This is a good spot. I can fit in the box and Mia will not see me." He opens the box and gets inside. He closes the box and waits.

Mia counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!" She looks around and tries to find Tom. She sees the swings, the slide, the bench, the flowers, but no Tom. She thinks, "Where is Tom? He is very good at hiding." She walks around and looks for clues. She sees a big box near a tree. She thinks, "Maybe Tom is in the box. I will peek and see." She walks to the box and lifts the lid.

She sees Tom in the box. He is shivering and his nose is red. He says, "Brrr, it is cold in here. You found me, Mia." Mia says, "Yes, I found you, Tom. But why did you hide in the box? Lila and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide and swing. But it was very hot and sunny. Lila wanted to find some shade to rest.

"Come on, Ben, let's go under that big tree. It has a lot of shade and we can sit on the grass," Lila said.

But Ben did not want to go. He wanted to stay on the swing. He liked to go high and fast. He did not care about the sun.

"No, Lila, I don't want to go. I want to swing. You go if you want, but I'm staying here," Ben said. He was very bossy.

Lila was sad and angry. She did not like Ben's tone. She wanted him to be nice and yield. She tried to persuade him.

"Please, Ben, it's too hot here. You can swing later. The tree is not far. It will be cooler and nicer there. Don't you want to be my friend?" Lila said.

But Ben did not listen. He shook his head and kept swinging. He did not want to be Lila's friend. He wanted to do what he wanted.

"Fine, Lila, go away. I don't need you. I don't need anyone. I'm the best swinger in the park. No one can swing higher than me," Ben said. He was very proud and rude.

Lila felt hurt and lonely. She decided to go to the tree by herself. She walked away from Ben and did not look back. She hoped he would change his mind and follow her.

But he did not. He kept swinging and swinging. He did not see the big bee that was flying near him. He did not hear the buzz that was getting louder and louder. He did not feel the sting that was coming closer and closer.

Until it was too late.

The bee stung Ben on his nose. He screamed and let go of the swing. He fell to the ground and cried. He felt a lot of pain and fear. He wanted Lila to help him. He wanted Lila to be his friend.

But Lila was not there. She was under the tree. She was in the shade. She was happy and safe.

She did not hear Ben's scream. She did not see Ben's fall. She did not care about Ben's sting.

She had a new friend. A nice and kind friend. A friend who liked to share and yield. A friend who was not bossy.

His name was Tom.

"We're sorry, Mama," they say. "We were hungry. And we both wanted the toast."

Sara and Ben nod. They say sorry again. They help Mama clean the kitchen. They learn their lesson.

"Maybe it is a mole," Mia says. "Moles live in holes."

Suddenly, a small brown animal pops out of the hole. It has a long nose and tiny eyes. It is a mole!

"We are playing," Mia says. "We wanted to see you."

They were very happy and hugged each other. Then they heard a loud sound. It was rain. The rain came down fast and hard. It made the leaves, stones and berries wet and muddy. Lily and Ben ran to find shelter under a big tree. They were sad and cold.

They saw a big dog under the tree. The dog was lazy and sleepy. He did not mind the rain. He looked at Lily and Ben and wagged his tail. He licked their faces and made them laugh. He shared his warm fur with them. He was very nice.

Lily and Ben felt better. They said, "Thank you, dog. You are our friend. Do you want some cake?" They gave him some stones. The dog ate them and smiled. He said, "Woof, woof. You are welcome. You are my friends. Do you want to play?" Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, please. Let's play." They forgot about the rain and had fun with the dog. They were happy again.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of animals, cars, dolls and blocks. One day, they found a new toy in the box. It was a red crocodile with sharp teeth and a long tail. Tom and Lily wanted to play with it, but they did not know how to share.

"I saw it first!" Tom said. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Lily said. "I like red!"

They pulled and tugged on the crocodile, but it did not move. They pulled harder and harder, until they heard a loud snap. The crocodile broke in two. Tom had the head and Lily had the tail.

They looked at the broken toy and felt sad. They did not want to play with it anymore. They wished they had been nice to each other.

They heard a voice behind them. It was their mom. She had seen what happened.

"Oh, no!" she said. "What did you do to the crocodile?"

Tom and Lily hung their heads. They knew they had been bad.

"We are sorry, mom," they said. "We broke the crocodile."

Mom looked at the toy and sighed. She picked up the pieces and held them together.

"Do you know what this is?" she asked.

Tom and Lily shook their heads.

"This is a special crocodile," mom said. "It is a puzzle. You can take it apart and put it back together. See?"

She showed them how to fit the head and the tail. The crocodile was whole again.

Tom and Lily gasped. They smiled and clapped.

"A puzzle!" they said. "That is so cool!"

Mom smiled too. She gave them the crocodile.

"Here you go," she said. "You can play with it, but you have to share. Can you do that?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They hugged mom and thanked her.

They took the crocodile and sat on the grass. They took turns to break it and fix it. They had fun and did not fight. They learned to share and be happy.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Tom," Lily said. "Maybe we can find something fun."

"OK, Lily," Tom said. "But we have to be careful. It is getting dark soon."

They ran to the hill and started to climb. It was hard and steep, but they did not give up. They helped each other and cheered each other on.

They reached the top and looked around. They saw a big forest with many trees and animals. They also saw a small house with a light in the window.

"Wow, look at that, Lily," Tom said. "Who lives there?"

"I don't know, Tom," Lily said. "Maybe we can go and say hello."

They walked to the house and knocked on the door. A kind old woman opened it and smiled at them.

"Hello, children," she said. "What are you doing here?"

"We climbed the hill and saw your house," Lily said. "We wanted to meet you."

"That's very brave of you," the woman said. "But you should not stay here too long. It is dark and cold outside. You need to go back to your home."

"Can we come in for a bit?" Tom asked. "We are tired and thirsty."

"Of course, you can," the woman said. "Come in and sit by the fire. I will give you some water and cookies."

They followed the woman into the house and sat on a cozy sofa. The woman gave them water and cookies and told them stories. She told them about the forest and the animals and the stars. She told them about her life and her wisdom. She told them to be kind and curious and brave.

Tom and Lily listened and learned. They felt warm and happy. They thanked the woman for her kindness and her wisdom.

"You are very welcome, children," the woman said. "But you should go now. Your parents must be worried about you."

She gave them a hug and a flashlight and showed them the way back to the hill.

"Be careful, children," she said. "And come back anytime you want. I will be happy to see you again."

Tom and Lily waved goodbye and ran back to the hill. They used the flashlight to see the path. They climbed down the hill and ran back to their house. They saw their parents waiting for them.

"Where have you been, Tom and Lily?" their mother asked. "We were so worried about you. It is dark and late."

"We are sorry, mom," Tom and Lily said. "We climbed the hill and met a nice old woman. She gave us water and cookies and stories. She taught us a lot of wisdom."

Their parents looked surprised and curious. They asked them to tell them more about the woman and the hill and the forest. Tom and Lily told them everything they saw and heard and felt.

Their parents listened and smiled. They hugged them and praised them.

"You are very brave, Tom and Lily," their father said. "But you are also very lucky. You had a wonderful adventure and made a new friend. You increased your wisdom and your joy."

They all went inside and had a warm dinner. They talked and laughed and shared their stories. They felt happy and grateful. They went to bed and dreamed of the hill and the woman and the forest. They looked forward to the next day and the next adventure.

He finished his tower and went to sleep in his bed. He pretended to be asleep, but he was really watching his door. He knew Lily would come soon. And she did. She saw the big tower and smiled. She tiptoed to the tower and reached her hand to push it.

Lily liked to read the newspaper with her dad every morning. She learned many interesting things from the newspaper, like the names of animals, places, and people. She also liked to look at the pictures and the comics.

One day, Lily saw a newspaper on the floor of her living room. She thought it was the one that her dad had read with her, but it was not. It was a different newspaper that her mom had brought home from work. Lily did not know that. She picked up the newspaper and started to read it.

She saw a big headline that said "Bad Man Robs Bank". She saw a picture of a man with a mask and a gun. She felt scared and curious. She wanted to know more about the bad man. She turned the page and saw another headline that said "Fire Destroys House". She saw a picture of a house with flames and smoke. She felt sad and sorry. She wanted to know more about the house.

She turned the page again and saw another headline that said "Dog Bites Boy". She saw a picture of a boy with a bandage and a dog with a collar. She felt angry and confused. She wanted to know more about the boy and the dog.

She turned the page one more time and saw a big word that said "END". She did not know what it meant. She thought it was the name of a story. She wanted to read the story. She opened the newspaper and saw nothing. It was blank. There was no story. There was no end.

She felt disappointed and cheated. She threw the newspaper on the floor and started to cry. Her mom heard her and came to see what was wrong. She saw the newspaper and realized what had happened. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, honey. This is not the newspaper that you read with your dad. This is a fake newspaper that I use for my work. It has no real stories. It has no end. It is only for pretending."

Lily looked at her mom and said, "But why do you pretend with a fake newspaper? It is not fun. It is not interesting. It is not nice."

Her mom said, "You are right, Lily. It is not fun, interesting, or nice to pretend with a fake newspaper. It is only for my work. Sometimes I have to pretend with a fake newspaper to teach people how to write real stories. But you don't have to pretend with a fake newspaper. You can read real stories with your dad. You can learn real things from the real newspaper. You can have fun, interesting, and nice times with the real newspaper."

Lily said, "OK, mom. I understand. I don't want to read the fake newspaper anymore. I want to read the real newspaper with dad. Can we do that tomorrow?"

Her mom said, "Of course, Lily. We can do that tomorrow. And every day after that. But for now, let's put the fake newspaper away. And let's find something else to do. Something that is fun, interesting, and nice. Something that has a good end."

Lily said, "OK, mom. I like that idea. What can we do?"

Her mom said, "How about we play with your toys? Or we read a book? Or we draw a picture? Or we bake a cake?"

Lily said, "Yes, yes, yes, and yes! Let's do all of that! That sounds fun, interesting, and nice. That sounds like a good end."

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily. That sounds like a good end. A very good end."

The moral of the story is: Don't be fooled by fake things. They can make you feel bad and unhappy. Look for real things. They can make you feel good and happy.

The gorilla does not like to be pulled. It feels hurt and sad. It wants Lily and Ben to be nice and play together. It tries to say, "Please stop! You are hurting me!" But Lily and Ben do not listen. They pull harder and harder.

Then, something bad happens. The gorilla rips apart. Its arms and legs and head fall off. Its stuffing comes out. Lily and Ben are shocked. They look at the gorilla and see that it is broken. They see that they have made a big mistake.

They start to cry. They say, "We are sorry, gorilla! We did not mean to hurt you! We love you, gorilla!" But it is too late. The gorilla can not hear them. The gorilla can not talk. The gorilla can not hug. The gorilla is different. The gorilla is gone.

One day, a boy named Tom and a girl named Mia went to the park with their mom. They saw a big slide that looked like fun. Tom and Mia ran to the slide and took turns to go down. They laughed and shouted as they slid fast and smooth.

"Look, mom, I'm so fast!" Tom said.

"Me too, me too!" Mia said.

Mom smiled and watched them play. She was happy to see them have fun.

But then, a big boy came to the slide. He had a spear in his hand. It was not a real spear, but a stick with a pointy end. He looked mean and strong. He pushed Tom and Mia away from the slide and said, "This is my slide. Go away, you little babies. I'm the king of the slide."

Tom and Mia felt scared and sad. They did not want to fight with the big boy. They wanted to share the slide and play nice. They looked at mom for help.

Mom saw what happened and walked to the slide. She was not afraid of the big boy. She was strong and kind. She said to the big boy, "Hey, you, stop being rude. This is not your slide. This is a slide for everyone. You have to share and be polite. And put down that spear. You could hurt someone with that."

The big boy did not listen to mom. He said, "No, you go away. This is my slide and my spear. I do what I want."

Mom did not like that. She said, "No, you don't. You have to follow the rules. If you don't, you have to leave the park. Now, give me that spear and say sorry to Tom and Mia."

The big boy did not want to give up his spear or say sorry. He tried to run away, but mom was faster. She grabbed his spear and took it away. She said, "This is not a toy. This is dangerous. You are not allowed to play with this. Now, say sorry to Tom and Mia or go home."

The big boy felt ashamed and angry. He did not like to lose his spear or be told what to do. But he knew mom was right. He said, "Sorry, Tom. Sorry, Mia." He did not sound very sorry, but he said it anyway.

Mom said, "Thank you. Now, you can play with Tom and Mia if you want, but you have to be nice and share. Or you can go to another part of the park and find something else to do. But no more spears, okay?"

The big boy nodded and walked away. He did not want to play with Tom and Mia. He wanted to find another spear and another slide. He hoped no one would bother him again.

Tom and Mia hugged mom and thanked her. They said, "You are the best, mom. You are so strong and brave. We love you."

Mom hugged them back and said, "I love you too, my sweeties. Now, let's go back to the slide and have some more fun."

They went back to the slide and slid down again and again. They had a lot of fun and made some new friends. They forgot about the big boy and his spear. They were happy and safe.

The girl looked up and smiled. She said, "I'm Mia. I like your whistle. It sounds nice."

Ben smiled back and said, "Thank you. Do you want to play with me? I have many toys and clothes. You can have some if you like."

Mia nodded and followed Ben inside. They played with his cars and trains and dolls. They had fun and laughed. Ben gave Mia a new dress and shoes and a doll with two eyes. Mia was very happy and thanked Ben.

His mom said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Mia and her family had to move away. They were very poor and had no home. They had to find a new place to live. Maybe you can write her a letter and send her a whistle. She will remember you and be happy."

Ben felt a big itch in his heart. He missed Mia very much. He wanted to see her and play with her again. He said, "Okay, mom. I will write her a letter and send her a whistle. I hope she is okay and finds a good home. I hope she is still my friend."

One day, Lily and Ben want to study how the truck works. They take the truck to their room and look at it. They see the screw on the side of the truck. They wonder what it does.

"Let's unscrew it and see," says Lily. She takes a tool from their dad's box and tries to turn the screw.

"Be careful, Lily," says Ben. "You might break the truck."

Lily does not listen. She turns the screw harder and harder. Then, with a pop, the screw comes out. But so does the wheel. The wheel falls off the truck and rolls away.

"Oh no!" says Lily. "What have we done?"

Ben is sad. He loves the truck. He picks up the wheel and the screw. He tries to put them back on the truck. But he does not know how.

"Maybe we can ask dad for help," says Lily. She feels sorry for Ben. She hugs him and says, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was curious. I didn't mean to ruin our lovely truck."

"What happened, kids?" he asks.

"We're sorry, dad. We love our truck. Can you fix it?" says Ben.

He takes the truck, the wheel, and the screw. He puts them on the table and explains how they work. He teaches Lily and Ben how to screw and unscrew the wheel. He lets them try it themselves.

"See, kids? It's easy. You just need to be gentle and careful. And always ask for permission before you take apart your toys. They might have parts that are hard to put back together."

Lily and Ben nod and say, "Yes, dad. We understand. Thank you for fixing our truck. You're the best dad ever."

One day, they saw a big sign on the tree. It said: "This tree will be cut down soon." Lily and Tom were very sad. They loved the tree. They did not want it to go away.

They decided to discuss what to do. They said:

- Tom: "But how can we save it? The sign says it will be cut down soon. Who can stop them?"
- Lily: "Maybe we can talk to the people who want to cut it down. Maybe we can make them change their mind."
- Tom: "That is a good idea. Let's go and find them."

Lily and Tom soon noticed that their sheet was gone. They looked around and saw Sam in the living room. They ran to him and asked him to give back their sheet. Sam said no. He said it was his sheet now, and he did not want to share. He told them to go away.

Lily and Tom felt sad and angry. They told their mom what Sam had done. Their mom was not happy. She went to the living room and scolded Sam. She told him that he had been very bad and rude. She told him that he had to give back the sheet and say sorry to Lily and Tom. She told him that stealing was wrong, and that sharing was good.

Sam felt ashamed and scared. He realized that he had made a big mistake. He gave back the sheet and said sorry to Lily and Tom. He asked them if they wanted to play with him. Lily and Tom forgave him and said yes. They all played with the sheet and had fun together. They learned to be kind and friendly.

Lily liked to swim. She had a big pool in her backyard. She wore a pink swimsuit and a hat. She swam with her mom and dad and her brother Max. They splashed and played and had fun.

One day, Lily saw something different in the pool. It was a small green frog. It jumped and swam in the water. Lily was curious. She wanted to touch the frog. She swam closer and reached out her hand.

But the frog was scared. It did not like Lily. It croaked and jumped out of the pool. It ran away to the grass. Lily was sad. She wanted to be friends with the frog.

She asked her mom, "Why did the frog run away? I just wanted to say hi."

Her mom said, "The frog is not used to people. It likes to be alone. It is different from us. We have to respect its space and let it be."

Lily nodded. She understood. She went back to swim with her family. She still liked frogs, but she knew they were different. She was happy to swim with her mom and dad and her brother Max. They were not different. They were her family.

Tim and Lily were playing in the backyard. They liked to dig holes and find things in the dirt. Sometimes they found rocks, worms, or old toys. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they found something shiny and round. It was a stove. A stove is something you use to cook food. It was very old and dirty. Tim and Lily wondered how it got there.

"Maybe someone buried it here a long time ago," Tim said.

"Why would they do that?" Lily asked.

"Maybe they didn't want it anymore. Or maybe they were hiding it from someone. Or maybe they were playing a game," Tim said.

Tim and Lily decided to play a game too. They pretended they were pirates and the stove was their treasure. They dug a bigger hole and buried the stove again. They made a map and hid it under a rock.

The next day, they came back to dig up their treasure. But they couldn't find it. Someone had taken it. They looked for their map, but it was gone too. They felt sad and angry.

"Who took our treasure?" Tim cried.

"Maybe it was the owner of the stove. Maybe they wanted it back," Lily said.

"Or maybe it was another pirate. Maybe they followed our map and stole it," Tim said.

They looked around and saw a man with a truck. He had a lot of old things in his truck. He was a junk man. He collected old things and sold them or recycled them. He had their stove.

"Hey, that's our treasure!" Tim shouted.

The junk man looked at them and smiled. He said, "Sorry, kids. I didn't know it was yours. I found it buried in the ground. I thought it was junk. Do you want it back?"

Tim and Lily nodded. They ran to the truck and took their stove. They thanked the junk man and carried their stove back to their hole.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that one man's junk is another man's treasure. They also learned that if they want to keep something, they shouldn't bury it. They should put it somewhere safe and normal. Like in their house. Or in their room. Or in their toy box.

The doctor shook his head and said, "I'm afraid not, Lily. Sometimes, things break and can't be fixed. You have to let them go."

Lily did not want to let Rose go. She held her tight and said, "No, no, no. I don't want to let her go. She is my best friend. I love her."

Anna heard Lily and felt sorry for her. She remembered how much she loved her own doll when she was little. She had a idea. She whispered to the doctor and asked him something. The doctor nodded and smiled. He said to Lily, "Lily, I have a surprise for you. Do you want to see it?"

Lily looked at him and said, "What is it?"

The doctor said, "Close your eyes and count to ten."

Lily closed her eyes and counted, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten."

The doctor said, "Open your eyes, Lily."

Lily opened her eyes and saw a new doll in the doctor's hands. The doll looked like Rose, but she was not broken. She had a pink dress and a rose in her hair. She was pretty and new.

The doctor said, "This is your new doll, Lily. She is a gift from your sister, Anna. She wanted to make you happy. She said you can name her whatever you want, but she suggested you name her Hope, because she hopes you will heal soon and be happy again."

Lily looked at the new doll and then at Anna. She saw Anna smiling and nodding. She felt a warm feeling in her heart. She said, "Thank you, Anna. Thank you, doctor. She is so pretty. I will name her Hope, because I hope I will heal soon and be happy again. And I hope Rose will be happy too, wherever she is."

Lily hugged Hope and smiled. She felt a little better. She learned that sometimes, things break and can't be fixed, but sometimes, things can be replaced and can make you happy. She learned that she had a big sister who loved her and cared for her. She learned that she had hope. And hope can heal.

"It's probably just the wind," his mommy replied.

But Timmy knew it wasn't the wind. He heard the noise again and it sounded like it was coming from outside. Timmy went to investigate and saw his neighbor, Mr. Johnson, trying to fix his car.

"Hi Mr. Johnson, what are you doing?" Timmy asked.

"I'm trying to fix my car, but I think I'm being foolish," Mr. Johnson said.

Timmy didn't understand what "foolish" meant, but he knew that Mr. Johnson needed help. So, he grabbed his laser gun and started to make "pew pew" noises. Mr. Johnson laughed and thanked Timmy for his help. From that day on, Timmy and Mr. Johnson became good friends and Timmy always kept his laser gun close by in case Mr. Johnson needed his help again.

As Benny hopped through the forest, he saw a big, scary wolf lurking in the shadows. Benny was scared, but he remembered the magical carrot and knew he had to be brave. Suddenly, Benny had an idea. He used his strong back legs to create a trap for the wolf using some vegetables he had picked up along the way. 

The wolf fell into the trap, and Benny was able to safely grab the magical carrot. He ate it right away and his eyes suddenly lit up. He could see everything in the dark! Benny was so happy that he could now eat all the vegetables he wanted and never be scared of the dark again.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim all day long in the big blue pond. He had many friends, like the frogs and the ducks. They would all play together and have lots of fun.

One sunny day, Fin decided to swim far away from his friends. He wanted to see what was on the other side of the pond. He swam and swam until he found a tight spot between two big rocks. Fin tried to go through the tight spot, but he got stuck.

Fin started to wiggle and wiggle, trying to get free. Then, a big fish named Bubba saw Fin and swam over to help. Bubba used his strong tail to strike the rocks. The rocks moved a little bit, making the tight spot bigger. Fin wiggled out and was free again. Fin thanked Bubba and they swam back to their friends. From that day on, Fin and Bubba were best friends and they all played happily in the big blue pond.

Tom and Anna were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hole in the ground near their house. They wanted to see what was inside the hole.

"Can we go and look?" Tom asked their mom.

Mom shook her head. "No, you can't. The hole is deep and dangerous. You might fall and hurt yourself. Stay away from it, please."

Tom and Anna were sad. They wanted to explore the hole. They waited until mom was busy in the kitchen. Then they sneaked out of the house. They took a cane from the porch. They thought they could use it to poke the hole.

They ran to the hole and looked down. It was dark and scary. They could not see the bottom. Tom held the cane and leaned over the hole. He tried to touch the edge with the cane.

"Be careful, Tom!" Anna said. "You might fall!"

Tom did not listen. He wanted to see how deep the hole was. He pushed the cane harder. But the cane was too short. It slipped from his hand and fell into the hole. Tom lost his balance and fell too.

"Tom!" Anna screamed. She ran to the hole and looked for her brother. She could not see him. She could only hear him cry.

"Help! Help! I'm stuck!"

Anna was scared. She did not know what to do. She ran back to the house and told mom what happened.

Mom was angry and worried. She called dad and the firemen. They came quickly and brought a rope and a ladder. They lowered the rope into the hole and pulled Tom out. He was dirty and bruised, but not badly hurt. The firemen also found the cane and gave it back to him.

Mom hugged Tom and Anna. She was glad they were safe. But she was also very upset.

"You were very naughty and foolish," she said. "You did not obey me. You did not stay away from the hole. You put yourself in danger. You could have died. You are not permitted to play outside for a week. You have to stay in your room and think about what you did."

Tom and Anna felt sorry. They knew they had done wrong. They said sorry to mom and dad and the firemen. They went to their room and cried. They wished they had never seen the hole. They learned their lesson. They decided to never disobey mom again.

One day, a little mouse named Milo wanted to wash his fur. He did not like to be dirty and smelly. He looked for some water in the underground tunnels where he lived with his family. He found a small puddle near a big pipe. He was happy and jumped into the water.

But the water was not clean. It was dark and oily and made Milo's fur sticky and black. He felt bad and tried to get out of the water. He saw a big rat coming out of the pipe. The rat was mean and scary. He wanted to take the water for himself. He saw Milo and growled.

"Get out of my water, you little pest!" the rat said. He moved closer to Milo and showed his sharp teeth.

Milo was afraid and did not know what to do. He wished he had a friend to help him. He heard a soft voice behind him.

"Leave him alone, you bully!" the voice said. Milo turned around and saw a little rabbit. The rabbit was white and fluffy and had long ears. He looked brave and kind.

The rat was surprised and angry. He did not like rabbits. He thought they were weak and stupid. He snarled.

"What are you doing here, you hopper? This is my underground. Go away or I will bite you!"

The rabbit did not go away. He stood in front of Milo and faced the rat. He said.

"This is not your underground. This is everyone's underground. You have no right to take the water and hurt the mouse. He just wanted to wash his fur. You should be generous and share the water. Or better yet, find another water that is clean and not oily."

The rat did not like what the rabbit said. He felt ashamed and angry. He wanted to fight the rabbit and the mouse. But he saw that the rabbit was not afraid of him. He also saw that the mouse was grateful to the rabbit. He felt a little sorry for them. He thought maybe the rabbit was right. Maybe he should be generous and share the water. Or maybe he should find another water that was clean and not oily.

He decided to do both. He said to the rabbit and the mouse.

"Fine. You can have this water. I don't want it anyway. It is dirty and smelly. I will go and find another water that is clean and not oily. But don't come near my pipe again. Or I will bite you."

He turned around and walked away. He did not look back.

The rabbit and the mouse were happy and relieved. They thanked each other and became friends. They washed their fur in the water. They did not mind that it was dirty and smelly. They were glad that they had each other. They were generous and shared the water. They lived happily in the underground.

"Be brave, Timmy," his dad said. "The wolf won't get us. We'll get him."

Sam felt sad and angry. He liked his frog. He thought it was a cool toy. He said, "My frog is not gross. It is a real frog. It has slime and smell because it is alive. It is a life. You are mean, Lily. You are not my friend."

Sam took his frog and ran away. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He wanted to find someone who liked his frog and who was nice to him. He thought, "Lily is disgusting. She is not a fun friend. She is a rude friend."

Lily was a big girl who liked to learn new things. She went to school with her friends and had a nice teach who showed them how to read, write and count. Lily was good at all these things, but she wanted to learn more. She wanted to learn how to play the piano, like her mom.

One day, Lily saw a piano in the school hall. It was shiny and black and had many keys. Lily felt an urge to touch the keys and make sounds. She looked around and saw no one. She ran to the piano and climbed on the stool. She put her fingers on the keys and pressed them. The piano made loud and strange noises. Lily liked it and pressed more keys.

"Stop! Stop!" a voice said. Lily turned and saw the music teach. He looked angry and sad. "What are you doing, Lily? You are hurting the piano. You don't know how to play it. You need to learn first."

Lily felt scared and sorry. She did not want to hurt the piano or make the teach mad. She got off the stool and said, "I'm sorry, teach. I just wanted to play the piano, like my mom. Can you teach me how to play it?"

The music teach sighed and smiled. He said, "Lily, I'm glad you want to play the piano, but you need to be patient and respectful. The piano is a special instrument that needs care and practice. You can't just play it without knowing how. If you want to learn, you need to ask me first and follow my rules. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, teach. I understand. Can you please teach me how to play the piano?"

The music teach said, "Yes, Lily. I can teach you, but you need to be ready. You need to listen to me, follow my instructions, and practice every day. It will take time and effort, but you will learn. Are you ready?"

Lily said, "Yes, teach. I'm ready. Thank you for teaching me."

The music teach said, "You're welcome, Lily. Come on, let's start with the basics. This is how you sit on the stool. This is how you hold your hands. This is how you press the keys. This is how you make music."

Lily smiled and followed the teach. She was happy and excited. She learned how to play the piano, and she learned how to be patient and respectful. She made the teach proud and the piano happy. She also made her mom happy, when she played a song for her at home. Lily was a big girl who liked to learn new things.

Sara and Anna are sisters. They like to play with dolls and dress them up. Sara has a lovely doll with long hair and a pink dress. Anna has a doll with curly hair and a blue dress. They share their toys and have fun.

One day, Sara sees a bottle of lotion on the table. She thinks it will make her doll's hair shiny and soft. She takes the lotion and puts some on her doll's hair. But the lotion is sticky and makes the hair clump together. Sara tries to comb the hair, but it only gets worse. She starts to cry.

Anna hears Sara crying and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the lotion and the doll's hair. She feels sorry for Sara and gives her a hug. She says, "Don't cry, Sara. We can fix it. Let's wash the doll's hair with water and soap. Maybe it will come off."

They go to the bathroom and wash the doll's hair. They rub and rinse and dry the hair. The lotion comes off, but the hair is still tangled and frizzy. Sara looks at her doll and says, "She is not lovely anymore. I miss her long hair and her pink dress. I was silly to use the lotion. I should have asked first."

Anna says, "She is still lovely, Sara. She is your doll and you love her. Her hair and her dress don't matter. What matters is how you treat her and play with her. You can still have fun with her. And maybe we can find a new dress for her later."

Sara smiles and says, "Thank you, Anna. You are a good sister. You are right. I love my doll and I will play with her. And I will not use lotion on her hair again. I learned my lesson."

They hug and go back to their room. They play with their dolls and have fun. They are happy.

Sam and Mia were very happy. They were going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They packed their bags and toys in the car. They wanted to see the big sea and the big boats.

"Are we there yet?" Sam asked.

"Soon, honey," Mom said. "Look, there is the bridge. We have to cross it to get to the island."

Sam and Mia looked out the window. They saw the big bridge over the water. It was very high and long. They saw many cars and trucks on the bridge.

"Wow, look at that!" Mia said. "That truck has a big balloon on it. It is red and round. I want it!"

Mia opened the door and jumped out of the car. She ran after the truck. She wanted to pull the balloon.

"Mia, no!" Mom and Dad shouted. They stopped the car and got out. They tried to catch Mia.

But it was too late. The truck was too fast. Mia could not pull the balloon. She fell off the bridge. She hit the water. She did not come up.

Sam, Mom and Dad cried. They did not go on vacation. They went home. They were very sad.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and brown. It has sharp teeth and a loud bark.

"Wow, look at that dog!" Tom says. "It is so big and strong. I want to pet it."

Sam is scared. He shakes his head. "No, Tom, we can't pet it. It is not our dog. It may bite us. That is the law. We have to ask the owner first."

Tom does not listen. He runs to the dog. He reaches out his hand. The dog growls. It snaps at Tom. Tom screams. He pulls back his hand. It is bleeding.

Sam runs to Tom. He helps him. He wraps his scarf around Tom's hand. He says, "Tom, are you okay? You were very weak. You did not follow the law. You made the dog angry. You should have nodded to me."

Tom is sorry. He nods to Sam. He says, "You are right, Sam. I was weak. I did not follow the law. I made the dog angry. I should have nodded to you. Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend."

They go to the nurse. She cleans Tom's hand. She puts a bandage on it. She says, "You are lucky. The dog did not bite you hard. Next time, be careful. Do not pet strange dogs. Follow the law. Nod to your friend."

Tom and Sam nod to the nurse. They say, "Yes, we will. We learned our lesson. We will follow the law. We will nod to our friend." They hug each other. They go home. They are still friends.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big box in the living room. It was a gift from their grandma, who was deaf and could not hear them. They opened the box and saw a beautiful dollhouse with many rooms and furniture. They were very happy and thanked their grandma with hugs and kisses.

They decided to play with the dollhouse together, but soon they had a problem. Ben wanted to put his toy car in the garage, but Lily said no. She said the garage was for her toy horse, and the car was too big. Ben said that was not fair, and tried to take the horse out. Lily said that was not nice, and pulled the car away. They started to fight and yell.

Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw them pulling and pushing the toys and the dollhouse. She was not happy and said, "Stop! You are being very rude and selfish. You should share your toys and play nicely. Grandma gave you this dollhouse to make you happy, not to make you fight. How do you think she would feel if she saw you like this?"

Ben and Lily felt ashamed and sorry. They knew their mom was right, and they loved their grandma. They said sorry to each other and to their mom. They hugged and made up. They decided to share the toys and the dollhouse, and to play together. They also made a card for their grandma, and drew a picture of them smiling with the dollhouse. They put the card in an envelope and asked their mom to help them send it to their grandma. They hoped their grandma would like it and be happy too.

Anna and Ben like to play outside. They have a big yard with a swing, a slide and a seesaw. They like to swing high, slide fast and seesaw up and down. They also like to balance on the fence. They try to walk on the fence without falling off. They hold their arms out and look at the sky.

One day, the weather is very nice. The sun is bright and the air is warm. Anna and Ben want to play outside all day. They put on their hats and shoes and run to the yard. They swing, slide and seesaw. They also balance on the fence. They walk on the fence and see the flowers, the birds and the clouds.

They get hungry and thirsty. They go inside and ask their mom for a snack. Their mom gives them some yummy food. She gives them apple slices, cheese sticks and juice. They eat and drink and say thank you. They feel happy and full. They go back outside and play some more. They have a lot of fun. They love the weather, the balance and the yummy food.

Anna and Ben were twins, but they were very different. Anna liked red things, and Ben liked blue things. Anna liked sweet things, and Ben liked sour things. Anna liked to share, and Ben liked to keep.

One day, their mom gave them each a cherry. Anna was happy, because cherries were red and sweet. Ben was not happy, because cherries were not blue and sour. He wanted a lemon instead.

"Can I have your cherry, Ben?" Anna asked.

"No, it's mine!" Ben said. He did not want to share.

Anna was sad, but she did not want to fight. She ate her cherry and smiled. Ben put his cherry in his pocket and ran away.

He wanted to find a lemon, but he did not know where to look. He ran around the yard, the street, the park, but he did not see any lemons. He saw many other things, like flowers, birds, cars, but no lemons.

He was getting tired and hungry. He decided to go back home and eat his cherry. He reached into his pocket, but he did not feel his cherry. He looked inside, but he did not see his cherry. He had lost his cherry!

He started to cry. He wanted his cherry back. He wanted to share with Anna. He wanted to say sorry. But it was too late. His cherry was gone, and he did not know where it was.

He ran back home, hoping to find his cherry there. But he did not find his cherry. He found Anna, who was playing with a lemon. She had found it in the park, where Ben had dropped his cherry.

"Look, Ben, I found a lemon!" Anna said. "Do you want to share it with me?"

Ben did not answer. He was too angry and sad. He had lost his cherry, and Anna had his lemon. He felt very different from his sister. He felt very alone.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their pet bird, Lila. Lila is yellow and blue and can sing very well. Sara and Ben have a cage for Lila, but they also let her fly around the room sometimes.

One day, Sara and Ben are playing with Lila in their bedroom. They are making funny noises and Lila is copying them. They are having a lot of fun. But then, they hear their mom calling them.

"Sara, Ben, it's time for lunch. Come downstairs, please."

Sara and Ben say "OK, mom" and run to the door. They forget to close the cage. Lila sees the open cage and thinks it is a game. She flies out of the cage and follows Sara and Ben.

Sara and Ben do not notice Lila behind them. They go downstairs and sit at the table. Mom has made sandwiches and juice for them. They start to eat and talk.

"Mom, Lila can sing very well. She can copy our noises. She is very smart."

Mom smiles and says "That's nice, dear. I'm glad you like your bird. But where is she? Did you put her back in the cage?"

Sara and Ben look at each other. They remember the open cage. They say "Oh no, mom. We forgot to close the cage. Lila is not in the cage. Where is she?"

Mom says "Don't worry, we'll find her. Maybe she is still in your room. Let's go and look."

They leave their plates and go upstairs. They look in their room, but they do not see Lila. They look in the bathroom, the closet, the hallway, but they do not see Lila. They start to feel sad and scared.

"Where is Lila, mom? What if she is lost? What if she is hurt?"

Mom says "Don't cry, sweeties. Lila is a smart bird. She will not go far. Maybe she is hiding somewhere. Let's keep looking."

They go downstairs and look in the living room, the kitchen, the garage, but they do not see Lila. They are about to give up, when they hear a familiar sound.

"Tweet, tweet, tweet."

They follow the sound and find Lila in the laundry room. She is sitting on a pile of clothes and singing. She sees Sara and Ben and says "Hello, hello, hello."

Sara and Ben are very happy. They hug Lila and say "Lila, we found you. We are sorry we forgot to close the cage. We love you."

Lila says "I love you too. I followed you. I wanted to play. It was fun."

Mom says "Lila, you are a naughty bird. You scared us. But we are glad you are safe. Next time, stay in your cage, OK?"

Lila says "OK, OK, OK."

Mom says "Now, let's go back to the table and finish our lunch. And then, we have to tidy up the laundry room. Lila made a mess."

Sara and Ben say "Yes, mom."

They take Lila back to the cage and close it. They go back to the table and eat their sandwiches and juice. They are happy and hungry. They thank mom for the lunch. Then, they help mom to tidy up the laundry room. They fold the clothes and put them away. They make the laundry room neat and clean. They are good and helpful. Mom is proud of them. Lila is quiet and sleepy. She sings a little song and falls asleep. They all have a good day. The end.

Sara loved to read books. She had many books on her bookshelf in her room. She liked to look at the pictures and make up stories in her head. Sometimes, her mom or dad would read to her before bed.

One day, Sara came home from preschool and wanted to read a book. She ran to her room and looked at her bookshelf. But she saw something that made her sad and angry. Her little brother, Ben, had taken some of her books and ripped them apart. He had thrown the pages all over the floor. He had also drawn on some of the covers with crayons.

Sara screamed and cried. She ran to her mom and told her what Ben had done. Her mom was shocked and upset. She went to Sara's room and saw the mess. She scolded Ben and made him pick up the papers. She told him he was very naughty and he had to say sorry to Sara.

Ben said sorry, but Sara did not forgive him. She said he had killed her books. She said they were dead and she could not read them anymore. She said she hated him and she never wanted to play with him again.

Sara's mom hugged her and tried to calm her down. She said she understood how Sara felt, but she also said that books were not alive and they could not die. She said they were just things that could be fixed or replaced. She said she would buy Sara some new books and help her glue the old ones back together. She said she loved Sara and Ben very much and she wanted them to love each other too.

She asked Sara to remember a time when Ben was nice to her and did something to make her happy. Sara thought for a while and remembered when Ben gave her a flower he had picked from the garden. She remembered when he shared his cookies with her. She remembered when he made her laugh with his funny faces. She felt a little better and a little less angry. She decided to give Ben a chance and try to be nice to him. She said she was sorry for yelling at him and she hugged him. Ben hugged her back and said he was sorry for ruining her books. He said he liked her books too and he wanted to read them with her.

Sara's mom smiled and said she was proud of them. She said they were good siblings and good friends. She said they could go to the library and borrow some more books to read together. Sara and Ben agreed and said they loved books and they loved their mom. They went to the library and had a fun time. They learned to take care of their books and each other. They lived happily ever after. The end.

Lily and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw many animals there. They saw ducks, rabbits, squirrels and birds. They liked to feed them bread and seeds. Mom told them to behave and not to scare the animals.

Then they saw a deer. It was huge and brown. It had big horns on its head. Lily and Ben wanted to see it closer. They ran towards it. The deer saw them and got scared. It ran away very fast. Lily and Ben were sad. They wanted to pet the deer.

Mom came and hugged them. She said, "I know you like the deer, but you have to be gentle and quiet. The deer is shy and does not like loud noises. Maybe next time, we can watch it from far away and see how it eats and plays. Would you like that?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They said they were sorry. They learned to behave better with the animals. They had fun at the park. They saw many other things. They saw a slide, a swing, a sandbox and a fountain. They played until it was time to go home. They thanked Mom for taking them to the park. They said they loved her. Mom smiled and said she loved them too.
